official_details.description: France Excellence Charpak is the French government scholarship programme in India, divided into four sub-programmes covering full-time Bachelor's and Master's study, summer laboratory training and semester exchanges. Both degree sub-programmes provide a monthly living allowance of EUR 860 plus French government scholarship holder status, covering social security, health insurance, housing assistance and subsidised meals, but not travel. Applications for the 2026 session are closed, with Master results finalised and Bachelor applications not accepted.

24.title: Humboldt Research Fellowship
24.description: The Humboldt Research Fellowship sponsors researchers with above-average qualifications from across the globe to conduct their own research at a German host institution. For postdocs the monthly fellowship amount is €3,000 and for experienced researchers €3,600, plus additional benefits. On top of the fellowship amount the Foundation provides family benefits for children and partners, subsidies for private full health insurance, and travel expense allowances, as well as personal support throughout the sponsorship. The host institute generally receives an allowance for research costs of €800 per month for natural sciences and engineering, or €500 for humanities and social sciences.
24.deadline_display: Rolling in three calls per year, each opening approximately eight months before the selection meeting and closing when 800 applications are received. The next call opens on 15 November 2026 for the July 2027 selection meeting, with the earliest possible fellowship start in September 2027. The current call has reached the maximum of 800 applications and no new applications can be created.

24.duration: Postdocs: 6 to 24 months, divided into up to three stays within three years. Experienced researchers: 6 to 18 months, divided into up to three stays within three years.
24.application_period: Three calls per year: opened 15 March 2026 (selection meeting November 2026, earliest start February 2027), 15 July 2026 (selection meeting March 2027, earliest start May 2027), and next on 15 November 2026 (selection meeting July 2027, earliest start September 2027). Each call closes automatically once 800 applications are received.
eligibility: Postdocs: did you complete your doctorate - or equivalent academic qualification - during the last four years?
Experienced researchers: did you complete your doctorate - or equivalent academic qualification - during the last twelve years?
Postdocs: have you been published in academic journals and by publishing houses that are reviewed according to international standards?

Experienced researchers: is your academic profile substantiated by an extensive list of publications including important papers in which you acted as thematic lead, and do you hold a leadership role commensurate with your career level (for example assistant professor, lecturer, head of an independent research group or higher)?

If a doctorate in your field or country of origin is not possible or uncommon, you can still apply up to 16 years after completing your master's or other postgraduate degree provided you have a publication record commensurate with your career level.

You are not a German national. If you are a German national, or if you obtained your university entrance qualification and university degree, or your university degree and your doctorate, in Germany, you can apply if you have lived and worked abroad for more than ten years and intend to continue doing so long-term. Have you lived and worked abroad for more than five years? You can still apply if there is a strong connection to your current country of residence (permanent employment, additional citizenship etc.).
For your application to be successful, you may not have lived in Germany for longer than a total of 90 days within the 18-month period prior to submitting your application.

A researcher from an academic institution of your choice in Germany will provide you with a mentoring agreement and written confirmation that research facilities are available, and will compile a detailed review for you.

You can provide two expert reviews. For postdocs: your doctoral supervisor and one other researcher - outside of your institute, if possible. For experienced researchers: important collaborative partners and/or researchers at your own institute as well as other institutes - outside your country of origin, if possible.

Natural sciences and engineering: you must have a good knowledge of German or English. Humanities, social sciences and medicine: you must have a good knowledge of German if this is necessary for conducting your research successfully; otherwise good knowledge of English will suffice.
You may not apply for the Humboldt Research Fellowship if you have already received sponsorship directly from the Humboldt Foundation (research fellowship or award).

24.selection_notes: The decision to award research fellowships is taken by a selection committee consisting of 60-70 researchers from various fields. Applications are academically evaluated by a peer review process based on: academic career and academic record to date (mobility, determination, thematic scope, academic productivity); quality of the key publications named in the application; originality and innovative potential of your proposed research; your future potential; and your independent research profile (for experienced researchers). The assessment also considers the individual life journey and educational background in terms of equal opportunities and accessibility. The Foundation expects 20-25% of the applications received to be approved.

purpose: Through the Humboldt Research Fellowship, the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation sponsors researchers with above-average qualifications from across the globe. As a fellow, you will benefit from individual support from the Humboldt Foundation and our diverse sponsorship portfolio.

The Humboldt Research Fellowship enables you to conduct your own research at various stages of your career in collaboration with a host at a German research institution of your choice. Hosts may apply for a subsidy towards research costs.

The package includes tuition and fees, on-campus room and board, health insurance, airfare, and a stipend for miscellaneous expenses. official_details.description: The King-Morgridge Scholars Program is a four-year, full-tuition scholarship at the University of Wisconsin-Madison for international students committed to applying their talents toward poverty alleviation around the globe. Scholars are selected from countries in Africa, the Caribbean, Latin America, South Asia and Southeast Asia for their drive, academic success and commitment to addressing poverty in their own countries, and six scholarships are awarded per year. 101.title: A*STAR Graduate Scholarship (AGS)
101.description: A*STAR Graduate Scholarship (AGS) funds up to four years of PhD or EngD study at an autonomous university in Singapore, jointly supervised by an A*STAR researcher and a university faculty member, with research conducted at an A*STAR Research Institute. Support published for up to 4 years comprises full tuition fees, a monthly sustenance allowance inclusive of CPF contribution where applicable, book, computer, conference and thesis allowances, and support for up to 12 months of overseas attachment. Monthly allowance is a published matrix by track and residency status: AGS (STEM) $4,500 for Singapore Citizens, $4,100 for Singapore Permanent Residents and $3,600 for International Students; AGS (Specialised Tracks: Semiconductor, Quantum, Computing) $6,200, $5,600 and $5,000 respectively.
101.deadline_display: Application period: 1 November to 1 February & 1 June to 10 August. First application cycle opens on 1 November and closes on 1 February of the following year; second application cycle opens on 1 June and closes on 10 August of the following year.

There will be at least 2 rounds of interviews involving the senior management of the Biomedical Research Council or Science & Engineering Research Council, and researchers from A*STAR's Research Entities. The nomination of supervisor(s) has to be approved by A*STAR; in most cases the main and co-supervisors should hold at least the designation of Principal Investigator or Principal Scientist at an A*STAR RI. Final approval of the PhD supervisor(s), research project and university for successful applicants is subject to A*STAR's approval. A*STAR makes a holistic assessment of each application and takes into consideration factors such as achievements in science/maths related competitions and CCAs; prior research experience helps but is not mandatory. The application process typically takes about 5 months from submission of a complete application to notification of results.

official_details.description: Whether you're looking to explore broad scientific fields or dive deep into a specialised area, AGS offers full funding, access to world-class research labs, and the chance to take on a 12-month overseas attachment during your PhD. purpose: A*STAR Graduate Scholarship (STEM): enabling aspiring researchers to pursue PhD studies in biomedical sciences, chemistry, physics, engineering, and related fields. Scholars gain research experience at A*STAR and contribute to impactful work.

A*STAR Graduate Scholarship (Semiconductor): supporting students in chip design, materials science, and semiconductor technologies. Scholars gain hands-on experience and help Singapore grow as a global hub for semiconductor talent and innovation.

A*STAR Graduate Scholarship (Quantum): advancing talents in quantum computing, communications, and sensing. Scholars drive cutting-edge research and discoveries that strengthen Singapore's position in quantum technologies.

A*STAR Graduate Scholarship (Computing): nurturing leaders in AI, cybersecurity, software engineering, and data science. Scholars tackle real-world digital challenges and build expertise to power Singapore's growth as a tech-driven nation.
AGS is a collaboration between A*STAR and local Autonomous Universities (AUs). Scholars will be jointly supervised by both the A*STAR and University supervisors.
The research proposal should align with your research interests and contribute to Singapore's Research, Innovation and Enterprise (RIE) ecosystem.

101.notes: Bond-free for Singapore citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents. Foreigners who are non-SPRs must serve a 3-year service commitment in Singapore-based companies, without commitment to any specific organisation; Singapore-based companies refer to local companies and international companies that have a base in Singapore and which is registered with the Accounting & Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA). Mid-term applicants receive the same terms of support as full-term AGS awardees from the point of the award, with retrospective payment for all tuition fees and/or any compulsory fees from Year 1 of study onward. It consists of a monthly stipend plus a tuition fee subsidy, with rates from 1 January 2026 of SGD 3,000 per month for PhD students and SGD 2,900 per month for Master's (Research) students, on top of a full tuition fee subsidy. Applicants must have at least Second Class Honours (Upper Division)/Honours (Distinction) or equivalent and be eligible for MOE Subsidy, and apply through GradApp by the relevant faculty deadline; the maximum award period is two years for Master's and four years for PhD candidates.

official_details.description: The Nanyang President's Graduate Scholarship (NPGS) is described by NTU as a competitive and prestigious scholarship scheme, the premier scholarship granted by NTU's President, intended for students taking their first step towards a leading research career by studying for a full-time PhD at NTU. All nationalities are eligible, and the published monthly stipend from January 2026 is S$4,300 for international students, S$4,800 for Singapore Permanent Residents and S$5,300 for Singapore Citizens, on top of full coverage of the annual tuition fee. The award is tenable for one year in the first instance, renewable subject to good progress to a maximum of 4 years, carries no bond, and comes with conference, book, IT and thesis allowances.

official_details.description: The TWAS-CSIR Postgraduate Fellowship Programme, run jointly by India's Council of Scientific and Industrial Research and UNESCO-TWAS, funds foreign scholars from developing countries to pursue research toward a PhD in CSIR laboratories and institutes in India. It is restricted to researchers aged 35 or under on 31 December of the application year, nationals of developing countries other than India who hold no residency visa in India or a developed country, holders of an MSc who are employed with a research assignment at home, and who can secure an official acceptance letter from a CSIR host. The fellowship pays a monthly stipend for living costs, food and health insurance plus subsidised accommodation, for up to 4 years full-time or 6 months to 3 years as a sandwich fellowship. The 2026 call closed on 3 June 2026 after an extension from 20 May.
official_details.program_type: South-South research fellowship (TWAS-CSIR, co-funded programme for PhD research in India)
official_details.region: India (with applicants from developing countries worldwide)
official_details.coverage: The fellowship pays a monthly stipend covering living costs, food and health insurance plus subsidised accommodation, but the stipend amount is not published, is not convertible into foreign currency, and accompanying family members are the fellow's financial responsibility, so it is not stated as full funding.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are 35 or under on 31 December of the application year and a national of a developing country other than India
Confirm you hold no visa for temporary or permanent residency in India or any developed country
Contact CSIR host institutions directly for a preliminary acceptance letter before applying - without it, the application is not considered
Only acceptance letters dated the same year as the application year are eligible, so do not rely on an old letter

170.title: Webster University Vienna Scholarships
170.description: Webster Vienna Private University offers the WVPU New Student Scholarship, a partial tuition award in three tiered levels for newly admitted bachelor's and master's degree students, on the basis of both academic achievement and financial need. Up to 20 awards are made per year at EUR 12,000/7,000/4,000 per academic year for bachelor's degrees and EUR 8,000/5,000/3,000 for master's degrees. The university states explicitly that these are partial scholarships and that the recipient must pay the remaining tuition fee. Application windows are 1 March to 31 May at 13:00 CET for the Fall semester and 1 October to 30 November at 13:00 CET for the Spring semester.

official_details.description: The Adelaide Academic Excellence Scholarship offers a 50% tuition fee reduction to international students commencing an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree who have achieved a high distinction average. Eligibility requires a minimum ATAR of 99 for undergraduate entry or a minimum overall GPA of 6.7 on a 7.0 scale for both levels, and a long list of health, veterinary and business programmes is excluded. Applications opened on 24 August 2026 and are reviewed on a rolling basis until allocations are exhausted, and recipients must maintain a minimum Program Term GPA of 5.5.

197.title: University of Sydney International Scholarship (USydIS)
197.description: The University of Sydney International Stipend Scholarship (USYDIS) is one of the awards in the Australian Government Research Training Program suite at the University of Sydney, listed for international students who are commencing or enrolled in a higher degree by research and are competitively awarded. The published value is AUD 44,293 per annum at the 2027 rate (AUD 42,754 at the 2026 rate), with a relocation and thesis allowance. Holders of a USYDIS are automatically awarded the University of Sydney Tuition Fee Scholarship, which covers 100% of tuition fees for up to 14 research periods. Applicants must apply for admission through Sydney Courses and separately submit the scholarship form by the deadline published in the Application and award timeline table for their research period.

210.title: KAIST Scholarship (KAIST International Undergraduate Admission)
210.description: KAIST awards its scholarship automatically to every admitted international undergraduate student, with no separate application: the applicant simply ticks "KAIST scholarship" on the Statement of Financial Resources section of the admission application. The award pays tuition exemption for 8 semesters, a living allowance of 350,000 KRW per month, and medical health insurance. It is not full funding: KAIST's own cost table shows the scholarship offsets 11,738,360 KRW of a 14,885,680 KRW essential annual budget, leaving roughly 3,359,000 KRW per year for housing, food and books.
210.deadline_display: Early Admissions (Spring Track, 2027): Application Period and Document Submission September 22 - October 22, 2026, 6:00 PM (KST); Recommendation Letter Submission October 29, 2026, 6:00 PM (KST). Regular Admissions (Fall Track / Fall Track Only, 2027): November 10, 2026 - January 14, 2027, 6:00 PM (KST); Recommendation Letter Submission January 21, 2027, 6:00 PM (KST).

official_details.description: KAIST offers the KAIST Scholarship to applicants of International Student Admission. official_details.description: The ISTA PhD program is described as a fully-funded, interdisciplinary, English-taught doctoral programme in which PhD students are employed by the Institute of Science and Technology Austria and receive internationally competitive salaries and full social security coverage, with no tuition fees and no application fee. Students enter with a Bachelor's or Master's degree in biology, neuroscience, mathematics, computer science, physics, chemistry or a related area, and choose among seven tracks. The programme runs in two phases around a qualifying exam, requires coursework of 30 ECTS (short route) or 42 ECTS (long route), teaching assistance, biannual progress reviews and annual thesis presentations, and a thesis defense typically within three to four years of passing the qualifying exam. Applications for the 2027 call open in late October and close on 8 January 2027.

benefits: A monthly payment of 992 euros
Travel allowance (upon application only)
One-off study allowance
Payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance cover
Possible monthly rent subsidy after the start of funding, on application
Possible monthly allowance for accompanying family members
In case of disability or chronic illness, a subsidy for justified additional costs, reviewed individually
Green Mobility Top Up support for climate-friendly travel, or reimbursement of carbon offset payments for air travel

eligibility: You can apply if you have gained a first university degree in the areas of Architecture, Interior Design, Monument Conservation and Building in Existing Contexts/Reconditioning of Old Buildings, Urban Design/Urban Development, Landscape Architecture or Landscape Planning at the latest by the time you commence your scholarship-supported study programme
As a rule, your last relevant university degree should not date back more than 6 years at the time of the application deadline
Your application cannot be considered if you have been resident in Germany for longer than 15 months at the application deadline

Degree programmes must provide a minimum number of ECTS credit points for Design/Projects: at least 45 CP for 120 CP programmes, at least 34 CP for 90 CP programmes, at least 23 CP for 60 CP programmes
Projects in the area of preservation of historical monuments and construction in existing buildings/restoration of old buildings are also supported
official_details.citizenship_residency: No nationality restriction is stated on the announcement. Eligibility is filtered by the DAAD scholarship database by the applicant's status and country, and DAAD states that if your status or country is not in the list, you cannot apply.
official_details.international_eligibility: Not stated as a citizenship rule on this page. The announcement is addressed to international students in the DAAD sense ('graduates', i.e. people who already have at least one first academic degree), and the applicant selects their status and country in the portal to see the programmes for which they are eligible.
official_details.subject_or_agency_requirement: Restricted to postgraduate architecture-related fields. The first degree must be in Architecture, Interior Design, Monument Conservation and Building in Existing Contexts/Reconditioning of Old Buildings, Urban Design/Urban Development, Landscape Architecture or Landscape Planning. Selected degree programmes must meet minimum Design/Projects ECTS thresholds (45 CP of 120, 34 CP of 90, or 23 CP of 60). Other DAAD scholarship programmes exist for applicants from the field of History of Architecture or applicants with a scientific project. Study visits abroad within a funded programme are only possible under narrow conditions.
official_details.application_method: Two-step submission, both required: (1) register on the DAAD portal, complete the online application in full and upload the item 1 documents to the portal's 'Attachments' section; (2) if the application passes the formal check, you receive a link to upload work samples to the DAAD media database by 23 October at the latest and must upload them by 4 November CET at the latest. If you already have an admission from a desired degree programme, complete the form anyway and upload it. Do not upload work samples or portfolios to the DAAD portal itself. The portal closes at 24.00 hrs CET/CEST on the last application day.

official_details.english_requirement: The language of instruction for study programmes in Germany is German. In international programmes, the language of instruction is English, or German and English. For English-language degree programmes you must already provide proof of language skills that meet the requirements of your chosen universities with the scholarship application. German-language architecture programmes generally expect at least B2, usually C1; for those, proof of German at a completed B1 level per the European Framework or TestDaF must be submitted.
official_details.english_requirement_note: DAAD sets no fixed TOEFL or IELTS score on this page; it defers to the requirements of each chosen university, which you must look up and satisfy. To be admitted to a German-language architecture programme you generally need at least B2, usually C1, German. Language certificates must be no more than three years old. A German language course before the scholarship period is compulsory if the language of instruction or working language at the German host institution is German.
selection_criteria: The academic qualification and architectural maturity, measured by study achievements and work samples
The quality of the project, as measured by the study plan and the letter of motivation
Aspects of equal opportunities, on which you can provide information in the application form
official_details.selection_weighting: No numerical weighting is published. Selection is by a special DAAD committee made up of professors from German universities, based on the written application and the work samples.
official_details.duration: Master's degree programme: between 10 and 24 months depending on the length of the chosen study programme or project, awarded for the standard period of study up to a maximum of 24 months. After the first year of study your academic achievements are assessed in a further funding procedure, and if they show you will complete the programme within a reasonable time, the scholarship continues as planned. Complementary studies not leading to a final qualification: one academic year. Start is usually 1 October of the year after the application, or earlier if a German language course is taken prior to the study programme.
award_holder_conditions: After the first year of study, academic achievements are assessed in a further funding procedure, and the scholarship continues only if you are expected to complete the programme within a reasonable period

A scholarship award does not automatically guarantee admission to a host university; if you are offered a scholarship but fail to be admitted to any of the universities named in your application, you may not make use of the award

If your programme includes a period abroad, funding for that period is usually only possible if the visit is essential to the scholarship objective, is not in your home country, and is no longer than a quarter of the scholarship period (up to 50% for joint and double-degree programmes where the study regulations specify this)
Individual fees, dorm damage, parking tickets, library charges and similar are your responsibility

257.description: The University of Otago Global Scholarships award NZD $15,000 with unlimited offers to new international Bachelor degree students commencing full-time undergraduate study who hold a passport from Bangladesh, China, Hong Kong, India, Indonesia, Macau, Malaysia, Singapore, South Korea, Sri Lanka, Taiwan, Thailand or Vietnam. 258.title: University of Otago Vice-Chancellor's Scholarship for International Students
258.description: The Vice-Chancellor's Scholarship for International Students is an Otago entrance scholarship worth NZD 10,000 for new international Bachelor students, awarded automatically during admission with no extra application. It is paid as a tuition-fee credit for one year and is not a living-cost award. Offshore applications close 10 December for a February start, while onshore applicants apply through the Entrance Scholarship route between 1 July and 15 August.

Intending to study from 100-level (first year) through to degree attainment
Studying on campus throughout the duration of their studies
Those enrolling into foundation certificate programmes are ineligible

Applications go directly to the consortium, not to the Commission.

selection_criteria: Academic excellence (weight 50%): as demonstrated by past academic results, transcripts, awards and distinctions. Indicators: academic record; scholarships and awards held; duration of previous studies; type of program and courses pursued; relative standing if available

Research potential (weight 30%): as demonstrated by research history, interest in discovery, the proposed research, its potential contribution to the advancement of knowledge in the field and any anticipated outcomes. Indicators: quality and originality of contributions to research and development; relevance of work experience and academic training to the field of proposed research; significance, feasibility and merit of proposed research; sound judgment and ability to think critically; ability to apply skills and knowledge; initiative and autonomy; research experience and achievements relative to expectations of someone with your academic experience

Personal characteristics and interpersonal skills (weight 20%): as demonstrated by past professional and relevant extracurricular interactions and collaborations. Indicators: work experience; leadership experience; project management including organizing conferences and meetings; ability or potential to communicate theoretical, technical or scientific concepts clearly and logically in written and oral formats; involvement in academic life; volunteerism and community outreach

official_details.description: The Canada Graduate Research Scholarship - Master's (CGRS M) is one of three programs in the Canada Research Training Awards Suite, jointly administered by CIHR, NSERC and SSHRC, and it supports up to 3,298 students annually across all disciplines. The value is $27,000 for 12 months, and the merit review is conducted by the host institution against published weights of academic excellence 50%, research potential 30% and personal characteristics and interpersonal skills 20%. Applicants must be Canadian citizens, permanent residents or Protected Persons as of the deadline, and must have completed 0 to 12 months of full-time study in the program for which funding is requested. Applications go through the Research Portal to up to three institutions by 1 December before 8:00 pm ET, and offers are available in the portal from 1 April with alternate offers possible until 31 January of the following year.
official_details.program_type: Tri-agency government research training award (institutionally administered merit scholarship)
official_details.region: Canada (eligible Canadian institutions only, without exception)
official_details.coverage: A $27,000 stipend for 12 months with optional supplements; the published value contains no tuition-fee component, and the pages do not state that tuition, living costs and required expenses are covered, so it is not recorded as fully funded.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your status is Canadian citizenship, permanent residency or Protected Person as of 1 December - this is a hard gate
Identify up to three Canadian institutions that hold a CGRS M allocation in your field of research; applications to institutions without an allocation in your field will be re-labelled or refused
Contact the faculty of graduate studies at each institution for their internal admission deadline, which is earlier than the agency deadline
Count your completed months of full-time study in the program for which you are requesting funding as of 31 December, and confirm you fall in the 0-12 month or the 4-12 month window
Confirm you have not held a Master's-level CIHR, NSERC or SSHRC scholarship, or an Indigenous Scholars Award and/or Supplement
Confirm you are applying to only one CRTAS program this academic year
Ask your institution how it applies the first-class average requirement, since institutions may at their discretion accept applicants who have not obtained one
Start the Research Portal application early - the agencies warn of portal congestion near the deadline and require all 11 steps to be complete
common_rejection_risks: Missing the institutional admission deadline while hitting the 1 December agency deadline - the agencies require you to respect the internal deadline
Applying to more than three institutions, or to institutions with no allocation in your field of research
Being outside the 0-12 or 4-12 month study window as of 31 December, or miscounting part-time study (part-time is calculated proportionally by percentage of full-time course load)
Holding or currently holding another Master's-level tri-agency scholarship, which is disqualifying
Applying to more than one CRTAS program in the same academic year, where only the first eligible application is retained
Portal congestion causing a late submission on 1 December - the agencies state that late applications will not be accepted and that the burden is the applicant's
Missing the English or French submission option, or omitting certified translations of documents in another language
Forgetting to check the Research Portal for results from 1 April onward, with alternate offers possible until 31 January
estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees - the $27,000 is a stipend with no published tuition component
Living costs above the $27,000 over 12 months
Bench fees, equipment, computing and fieldwork costs
Health insurance, where not provided by the province or institution
Conference and travel costs, unless you win the CRTAS Research Travel Supplements, which is the only concurrent award permitted

330.title: Danish State Scholarship
330.description: Aarhus University offers a limited number of Danish state scholarships to the most talented applicants from outside Europe who are liable to pay tuition fees. Students who are offered a waiver only are not notified by the university and are required to pay fees if no waiver offer arrives by 1 April / 1 November.
eligibility: Applicants liable to pay tuition fees (i.e. non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens without a fee-exempt residence permit). **No separate application** — the admission application is automatically assessed with a view to a scholarship. EU/EEA/Swiss students cannot apply for scholarships at AU. Priority is given to applicants with excellent academic qualifications; typically only one or two scholarships are offered per Master's programme. At some faculties strategic focus is placed on selected degree programmes or applicants from specific countries. Selection offers come with the letter of admission and carry a very short acceptance deadline.
330.eligibility_summary: Non-EU/EEA students admitted to a Master's programme at Aarhus University. Must be liable for tuition fees. Automatic consideration during admission application; no separate scholarship application required.
benefits: Content varies by faculty — a full or partial tuition waiver, in some cases including a monthly grant toward living expenses, typically but not always for the duration of the Master's. Stated types: Faculty of Arts and Aarhus BSS = tuition fee waiver + monthly living-expense grant; Faculty of Natural Sciences and Faculty of Technical Sciences = tuition fee waiver only. Where only a waiver is offered, the student must still show sufficient funds for the residence permit (SIRI self-support requirement). Waiver awards for Natural/Technical Sciences may also be made during March, up to the acceptance deadline of 1 April (summer) / 1 November (winter).

eligibility: Each September intake AAU grants a limited number of scholarships to individually selected applicants from non-EU/EEA countries based on strategic considerations and academic qualifications; **approximately 15 each year**. AAU advises not to rely on receiving a scholarship. AAU's FAQ states it is not possible to apply for a scholarship from AAU separately.
332.eligibility_summary: Non-EU/EEA students admitted to a Master's programme at AAU. Must be liable for tuition fees. Automatic consideration during admission application; no separate scholarship application required.
benefits: A scholarship consists of a **tuition fee waiver plus a monthly stipend** aimed at covering living expenses during the four semesters of the master's programme. Stipend rate for new students in 2026: **11,225 DKK / 1,503 EUR per month** (tax may apply). Stipend is paid for four semesters; no further stipend beyond the first two years.

352.title: France-South Africa Scholarship Programme 2027
352.description: The 2027 call of the France-South Africa Scholarship Programme is open, for students starting study in France in September 2027. All fields of study are eligible, with priority given to STEM and related humanities/social-science disciplines (digital technologies, AI, quantum technologies, biotechnology, health, environmental sciences, energy, low-carbon mobility, space, food systems, ICT). A shortlist is announced in December 2026 and final awards are confirmed in four waves between May and July 2027.
352.deadline_display: Application deadline: 8 October 2026 at 23:59 (South Africa time)
352.region: France (for study), open to applicants resident in South Africa, Lesotho and Malawi
352.duration: Master's: duration of the degree (typically 2 years); PhD: up to 3 years
eligibility: citizenship of South Africa, Lesotho or Malawi; dual French citizens are not eligible; a minimum average of 60% in the most recently completed degree. Master's applicants must plan to enrol in a French higher education institution (admission is not required at the time of application); PhD applicants must plan to pursue a PhD in France and have identified a prospective supervisor or research laboratory. Applicants may list a maximum of three study programmes in order of preference, and must supply links to programme pages, application dates and tuition fees. Proof of acceptance must be provided between February and July 2027. Applications must include a cover letter, copies of previous degree certificates, university transcripts covering at least three years, academic and/or professional recommendations and French language proficiency certificates (TCF, DELF, DALF etc.).
352.eligibility_summary: South African, Lesotho or Malawian citizens admitted or applying to a French higher education institution for a Master's or PhD starting September 2027. Born on or after 1 January 1996.
benefits: laureates attend intensive online French courses delivered through the Alliances Françaises network from February to July 2027; shortlisted candidates may be offered an internship with a French company or organisation in South Africa; depending on profile, placement is available in business, administration or the public sector. a monthly living allowance of **€900 for Master's students and €1,850 for PhD students**, subject to reassessment; **one return flight ticket** between the recipient's country of residence and France; eligibility to apply for additional housing support from the French Family Allowance Fund (CAF) of approximately **€150 per month** depending on individual circumstances. The award also carries France Excellence scholarship-holder status: social security coverage and health insurance, priority access to student housing, exemption from visa fees, support services from Campus France Paris, exemption from the Student and Campus Life Contribution (CVEC), and conditional exemption from registration fees for programmes at public universities applying the standard national non-EU tuition rate. **Tuition fees are not covered by the scholarship.**

363.title: Ireland Fellows Programme 2027/2028
363.funding: Fully funded (fees, flights, accommodation, living costs, insurance)
363.description: The Ireland Fellows Programme is one of Irish Aid's most longstanding programmes, offering people from around the world one year of study in Ireland. Applications are made through the applicant's local Irish embassy/UN office, and eligibility, courses and deadlines differ per strand and per country.
eligibility: Be a resident national of an eligible country for the strand
Hold a bachelor's-level qualification from an accredited, government-recognised institution with a minimum GPA of 3.0 (4.0 scale), awarded in 2015 or later
Not already hold a master's or higher qualification and not be undertaking a master's programme in 2026/27
Have a minimum of two or three years' substantial work experience directly relevant to the proposed programme, depending on the country
Demonstrate leadership abilities, commitment to the SDGs in their own country, and commitment to building positive relationships with Ireland
Have identified and selected three programmes from the Directory of Eligible Programmes
Not have applied to the Ireland Fellows Programme on more than one previous occasion
Be able to take up the Fellowship in academic year 2027/2028

benefits: one year of study in Ireland (study, research or professional training depending on strand); the programme has strand-specific additional awards — Kader Asmal (South Africa), Roger Casement (Nigeria and the Brazil/Colombia/Ecuador/Peru/Venezuela award), Seán McBride (Namibia), Archbishop Michael Courtney (Burundi), Frank Ferguson Fellowship in Engineering (Zambia), Cecilia Grierson (Argentina/Bolivia/Paraguay), Central America Award, and SIDS fellowships. the programme is fully funded by the Irish Government. official_details.description: The VU Fellowship Programme is a merit-based tuition fee waiver from Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, with the university having committed approximately one million euros to attract highly motivated and excellent students. It is intended for talented prospective non-EU/EEA students who hold a non-EU/EEA passport, are not eligible for the lower tuition fee, are not of Dutch nationality, prove a bachelor's GPA equivalent to a Dutch 8, and are conditionally or unconditionally admitted to the first year of a full-time English-taught Master's programme starting September 2027; February starters and joint programmes not administered by VU are excluded. 421.description: Poland My First Choice NAWA encourages talented young people from 44 listed developed countries and territories to study at Polish academic higher education institutions. It offers a scholarship for the statutory period of full-time second-cycle (Master's) studies at academic institutions, public and non-public, supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education, and additionally provides exemption from tuition fees at public universities. 423.description: Erasmus+ is the European Union programme supporting projects, partnerships, events and mobility in education, training, youth and sport. For individual students its main actions are studying abroad, traineeships abroad and the Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degrees. There is no central application form or central deadline: applications run through the sending university, which selects students fairly and transparently and applies for the funding. Students are exempt from tuition, registration, examination and laboratory/library fees at the receiving institution and receive a grant contributing to travel and daily living costs, with the amount set by national grant agreements.

official_details.deadline_note: There is no central application form or central deadline. The European Commission states: 'There's no central application form to study abroad with Erasmus+. You can reach out to the international or Erasmus+ office of your university or higher education institution to start the process. Your sending higher education institution is obliged to select applicants in a fair and transparent way.' The deadline therefore belongs to the sending institution, and each receiving institution has its own admission deadlines that may fall months before the mobility starts.

official_details.description: The Fulbright Program in Poland, initiated in 1959 and administered by the Polish-U.S. Fulbright Commission, is a merit-based exchange programme jointly funded by the governments of Poland and the United States. It runs distinct awards in both directions: grants to Poland for US citizens (Scholar, Student, English Teaching Assistant, Specialist, Schuman) and grants to the USA for Polish citizens (Graduate Student up to USD 47,000 for a first year, Junior Research, Polish Scholar, Polish Studies, STEM Impact). Benefits include a stipend, J-1 visa and SEVIS support, medical insurance, a travel allowance and additional allowances for host institution fees, relocation, research and family support, with application windows published as month ranges per award.

official_details.coverage: Covers a living stipend, J-1 visa and SEVIS fees, medical insurance, round-trip travel and additional allowances for host institution fees, relocation, research, conferences and family support, with amounts and duration varying by award; tuition is not stated to be fully covered across all awards.

official_details.description: CEEPUS, the Central European Exchange Programme for University Studies, is a multilateral exchange programme with Central and Eastern Europe that unites universities from 16 countries within networks of at least three institutions from at least two different contractual countries. 434.title: MOE Teaching Scholarship (Full-Term)
434.description: The MOE Teaching Scholarship/Award (Full-Term) sponsors Singapore Citizen students who intend to become teachers, covering undergraduate tuition fees and other approved charges plus a monthly maintenance allowance at a reputable local or overseas university, in exchange for a teaching service bond of 4 to 6 years. Applicants are considered across the full range of MOE Teaching Scholarships and Awards, and a parallel PSC Scholarship (Teaching Service) offers airfare and possible postgraduate sponsorship. Application windows are opened separately for each qualification type rather than on a single programme-wide date.

A well-rounded individual with good academic and co-curricular activities (CCA) records
GCE A-Level, International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma, Polytechnic Diploma, NUS High School Diploma or equivalent
Demonstrates strong leadership qualities
Possesses excellent interpersonal and communication skills

437.title: A*STAR International Fellowship (AIF)
437.description: The A*STAR International Fellowship supports up to 2 years of overseas postdoctoral training at a leading overseas university, research institution or deep-tech startup, in one of two tracks: AIF (Research) and AIF (Innovation). Support comprises a monthly overseas living allowance (SGD 5,000 for Singapore Citizens), a monthly sustenance allowance, annual return airfare, one-off and annual allowances, and personal insurance. Awardees must return to Singapore and contribute to A*STAR for 3 years after training.
437.region: Singapore (awarding body and post-award service commitment); host institution overseas
eligibility: Be Singaporean or Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR). Foreigners who are non-SPRs and with outstanding track records may be considered on an exceptional basis. Non-Singaporeans are required to have obtained Singapore citizenship prior to the commencement of the fellowship
Have completed a PhD within the last 4 years
Not have existing bonds to any institution
AIF (Research): possess excellent publication records; have applied or be applying for a relevant postdoctoral position at a top overseas university/laboratory
AIF (Innovation): demonstrate strong aptitude and aspiration to pursue roles in innovation and entrepreneurship (I&E); preferably with good publication records

Mid-Term AIF (Research) applicants must be Singaporean, already enrolled at a top overseas university/lab, have good publication records, and have their current postdoctoral supervisor as at least one of the two academic referees
437.eligibility_summary: Singapore citizens or Singapore PRs. Completed PhD within last 4 years. No existing institutional bonds. Must have secured postdoctoral position at leading overseas institution. Two tracks: Research and Innovation.

459.title: EPFL Bachelor Excellence Fellowships
eligibility: Master's Excellence Fellowship for students beginning a master's programme with remarkable academic results and notable extracurricular activity. Open to international applicants and applied for through the master's application form.
459.eligibility_summary: Holders of a Swiss high-school maturity diploma or Swiss vocational maturity diploma undertaking the CMS. Outstanding results and engagement in school and extracurricular activities.
benefits: CHF 10,000 per semester together with guaranteed housing
459.coverage: Provides CHF 10,000 in cash instalments over three years plus a residence room reservation that the student pays for, and does not state that tuition or all living costs are covered.
requirements: Application for admission to an EPFL Bachelor programme
Tick the excellence fellowship box on the Bachelor application form before 30 April
Meet one of the four published status or schooling conditions
Meet the published grade thresholds (5.3/6 general, 5/6 science and maturity project, 5.00 after CMS where applicable)
Present the maturity project or a subject of your choice to a jury of EPFL professors in a five-minute presentation with questions
The presentation assesses eloquence, synthesis, commitment and the ability to put thoughts into perspective
documents: s application form before April 30th
459.application_method: Tick the corresponding box on the EPFL Bachelor application form before 30 April and provide the requested application file. Where the applicant is eligible, an ad hoc form is issued and the listed documents are requested. Each section then pre-selects the best applications for a presentation of the maturity project (or another subject, if not applicable) before a jury made up in part of EPFL academic staff, in a short five-minute presentation followed by questions. The applications retained are then examined by the Central Committee for Bachelor Excellence Fellowships, which awards the fellowships.

official_details.application_method: Tick the corresponding box on the EPFL Bachelor application form before 30 April and provide the requested application file. Where the applicant is eligible, an ad hoc form is issued and the listed documents are requested. Each section then pre-selects the best applications for a presentation of the maturity project (or another subject, if not applicable) before a jury made up in part of EPFL academic staff, in a short five-minute presentation followed by questions. The applications retained are then examined by the Central Committee for Bachelor Excellence Fellowships, which awards the fellowships.

official_details.description: EPFL's Bachelor Excellence Fellowships are offered to holders of a Swiss high-school maturity diploma and holders of a Swiss vocational maturity diploma undertaking the CMS, and to any applicant to an EPFL Bachelor programme who meets one of four published status or schooling conditions. The fellowship is worth CHF 10,000 spread over three years, paid as six semester instalments, and comes with a guaranteed room reservation in an EPFL partner residence on request and at the student's own cost, plus an excellence certificate. Applications are made by ticking a box on the Bachelor application form before 30 April, followed by section pre-selection, a five-minute jury presentation of the maturity project, and a decision by the Central Committee for Bachelor Excellence Fellowships at the end of June.

472.title: East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship 2027
472.description: The East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship funds master's and doctoral study at the University of Hawai'i at Mānoa for citizens of the U.S., Asia and the Pacific. Applicants not already classified as graduate students at UH Mānoa must also apply to the university for the following fall semester by 1 December; supporting documents for both the UH admissions office and the department must be completed by 10 January.
472.duration: Up to 24 months; granted one year at a time and renewable
eligibility: citizens or permanent residents of the **United States**, or of listed countries in the Pacific Region (American Samoa, Australia, Cook Islands, Easter Island/Rapa Nui, Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, French Polynesia, Guam, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Nauru, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Niue, Northern Marianas, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tokelau, Tonga, Tuvalu, Vanuatu, Wallis & Futuna), Southeast Asia (Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste, Vietnam), South Asia (Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Iran, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka) and East Asia (China, Hong Kong, Japan, Macau, Mongolia, North Korea, South Korea, Russia, Taiwan). Must have obtained a 4-year bachelor's degree or equivalent from an accredited U.S. institution or a recognised institution abroad before the award starts; minimum GPA of 3.0 (4.0 = A) or equivalent over the last four semesters and in all post-baccalaureate work. Priority is given to applicants committed to the development of the Indo-Pacific region and to fields relevant to the Center's goals.
472.eligibility_summary: Citizens or permanent residents of the United States, or citizens of Asia-Pacific countries. Admission to University of Hawai'i at Manoa graduate program required by December 1. Priority given to applicants with commitment to Asia-Pacific region.
benefits: housing in an East-West Center residence hall for the academic year on a single-occupancy basis; Community Building Institute and advising at the start of the award; alumni and Foundation scholarships may supplement a Graduate Degree Fellowship; alumni are also considered for EWCA Alumni and Foundation scholarships. full-time graduate tuition and fees up to the equivalent of the general tuition charged for post-baccalaureate students at the University of Hawai'i at Mānoa toward master's or doctoral study; plus partial funding toward incidental expenses. Funding for field study and conference presentations is offered on a competitive basis. No single dollar figure is published; awards are made annually and initially for one academic year (fall + spring), renewable for one additional academic year subject to funding availability, satisfactory progress and Center requirements. Fellowships do **not** provide support for spouses/dependents.  (source for the award breakdown: https://www.eastwestcenter.org/education/ewc-graduate-degree-fellowship/gdf-award-details — this page could not be loaded directly (navigation timeout); its text was read from the live index of that same official EWC URL.)

475.title: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program (JJ/WBGSP) 2027 - Application Window #1 (Developing Country Nationals)
475.description: The JJ/WBGSP is a fully funded master's scholarship for mid-career professionals from listed World Bank developing countries who are already admitted to one of a fixed set of participating development-related master's programmes. For the 2027 cycle the World Bank states that a scholarship provides tuition, a monthly subsistence allowance to cover all living expenses while on campus, economy class round-trip airfare, basic medical insurance obtained through the university, and a US$600 travel allowance for each trip. The amount of the monthly subsistence allowance varies depending on the host country and is not published on the programme page. The Government of Japan solely funds the scholarship on an annual basis, and scholars commit to return to their home country after earning their degree.
475.deadline_display: Application Window #1 from January 18 to February 26, 2027. The programme also runs Application Window #2 from March 29 to May 21, 2027. The link to the JJ/WBGSP application form is only communicated to candidates admitted unconditionally (except for funding) to a participating master's programme and shortlisted as eligible by that university.

475.selection_notes: Two qualified assessors independently review each eligible application and score it from 1 to 10 on four factors: quality of professional experience (30% weight), quality of professional recommendations (30% weight), quality of commitment to the applicant's home country (30% weight), and quality of education background (10% weight). The Secretariat uses the average of the two assessors plus a reasonably wide geographical distribution of awards, a reasonable distribution across gender, unusual circumstances or hardships, and giving scholarships to applicants who otherwise have limited access to financial resources for graduate studies abroad. Finalists go to the JJ/WBGSP Steering Committee, composed of members of the World Bank Board of Directors and World Bank management, for approval.

official_details.description: The Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program funds citizens of listed World Bank member developing countries who apply to master's programmes in development-related topics at one of 44 participating master's programmes across 24 universities in the U.S., Europe, Africa, Oceania and Japan. For 2027, subject to available funding, the scholarship pays tuition and basic medical insurance, a monthly subsistence allowance for living costs while on campus, economy class round-trip airfare between the scholar's home country and the host university, and a US$600 travel allowance per trip. The award covers the duration of the graduate programme or two years, whichever is less, and the scholar commits to return to their home country after graduating. Window #1 runs from 18 January to 26 February 2027, and the application form link is issued only to candidates who already hold an unconditional (except for funding) admission from a participating university and who have been shortlisted as eligible JJ/WBGSP applicants by that university.
purpose: The JJ/WBGSP is open to citizens of certain developing countries with relevant professional experience and a history of supporting their countries' development efforts who are applying to a master's degree program in a development-related topic.

Subject to available funding, JJ/WBGSP offers scholarships for 44 Participating Master's Programs in 24 universities in the U.S., Europe, Africa, Oceania and Japan in key areas of development, including economic policy management, tax policy, and infrastructure management.
The JJ/WBGSP uses a review process aimed at identifying the candidates with the highest potential, after completion of their graduate studies, to impact the development of their countries.
After earning their degree, developing country scholars commit to return to their home country to use their new skills and contribute to their countries' social and economic development.

selection_criteria: Two qualified assessors independently review each eligible application and score it on a scale of 1 to 10, taking into account four main factors and the degree of cohesion among them: quality of professional experience (30% weight); quality of professional recommendations (30% weight); quality of commitment to your home country (30% weight); quality of education background (10% weight).

The JJ/WBGSP Secretariat uses the average score of the two assessors plus criteria for maintaining a reasonably wide geographical distribution of awards, maintaining a reasonable distribution of awards across gender, considering unusual circumstances or hardships, and giving scholarships to those applicants who, other things being equal, have limited access to financial resources for graduate studies abroad.
The aim is to identify candidates with the highest potential, after completion of their graduate studies, to impact the development of their countries.
The degree of cohesion among the four factors is itself taken into account in the scoring.
official_details.selection_notes: Each eligible application is independently reviewed and scored 1-10 by two qualified assessors against four weighted factors (professional experience 30%, professional recommendations 30%, commitment to home country 30%, education background 10%), with the degree of cohesion among the factors also considered. The Secretariat uses the average of the two scores together with four balancing criteria - wide geographical distribution, reasonable gender distribution, unusual circumstances or hardships, and preference for applicants with limited access to financial resources for graduate studies abroad. The list of finalists is presented to the JJ/WBGSP Steering Committee, composed of members of the World Bank Board of Directors and World Bank management, for approval, and winners are notified soon after Steering Committee approval.

application_readiness_checklist: Start with the programme list, not the scholarship. If you are not admitted to one of the 44 JJ/WBGSP Participating Master's Programs, you are not eligible to apply for a JJ/WBGSP Scholarship in 2027.

Check your employment arithmetic early: at least 3 years of paid development-related employment since your bachelor's degree, acquired within the past 6 years from the application deadline date, and in a paid full-time development-related position at the time you submit.
Confirm your degree timing: your bachelor's or equivalent must have been earned at least 3 years before the Application Deadline date.
Verify your nationality is on the eligible list and that you do not hold dual citizenship of any developed country.
Choose a host programme outside your country of citizenship and country of residence as listed when the call opened.

Contact the participating university early to ask whether it will shortlist you as an eligible JJ/WBGSP applicant, and which application window matches your programme's academic calendar - the scholarship form link depends on that shortlisting.
Upload your unconditional (except for funding) admission letter before you submit the scholarship application; it is a sequencing requirement, not an optional attachment.
Read the Application Guidelines for your window, because the World Bank states the detailed eligibility criteria in that document are strictly adhered to with no exceptions.
Note your own past history: if you were previously offered a JJ/WBGSP scholarship and declined it, or previously received one and did not graduate, you cannot apply again.
If you hold another scholarship or fellowship, prepare to send those documents to the Secretariat, because the JJ/WBGSP award supplements rather than duplicates other support.
important_advice_for_students: This is a two-stage application and people routinely miss the first stage. You must be admitted unconditionally (except for funding) to a participating programme AND be shortlisted by that university before you can even receive the scholarship form link. Start with the university, not with the scholarship.
Choose your window based on your programme's academic calendar, not your convenience. The two windows exist precisely because the 44 participating programmes start at different times.

The 30% weighting on 'quality of commitment to your home country' is the single most underweighted item applicants forget. With professional experience and professional recommendations also at 30% each and education background at only 10%, your development-related work history and your return commitment carry most of the score.

Budget for the gaps. Visa costs, family, computers, research and field trips, workshops, seminars, internships, extra travel, non-provided language training, the resident permit fee and extra-curricular courses are all outside the award.

The subsistence allowance is for living costs while on campus, and its amount varies by host country. Do not treat it as a fixed international figure, and check the host country's cost level before committing to an expensive city.
The award is the duration of the programme or two years, whichever is less. If your programme is longer than two years, you should plan for the remainder yourself.
Being financially disadvantaged is an explicit selection criterion, alongside geographical spread and gender balance. Do not obscure a genuine financial constraint.

There is a specific exception for nationals of Fragile and Conflict States listed in Annex 3, where limited employment opportunities are taken into account. If you are in that group, make sure the argument is made in the application rather than assumed.
common_rejection_risks: Not being admitted to one of the 44 Participating Master's Programs.
Holding a programme place that is conditional on funding, rather than unconditional except for funding.
Host programme located inside the applicant's country of citizenship or country of residence.

Failing to upload the letter of admission before submitting the scholarship application.
Not holding dual citizenship of any developed country - this is an absolute exclusion.
A bachelor's or equivalent degree earned less than 3 years before the Application Deadline date.

Fewer than 3 years of paid development-related employment since the degree, or employment not acquired within the past 6 years from the deadline date, or not in a paid full-time development-related position at the time of submission.
Previously being offered a JJ/WBGSP scholarship and declining it, or previously receiving one without graduating.
Being a World Bank Group Executive Director, alternate or staff member, or a close relative by blood or adoption.
A non-development-related research topic.
Applying in the wrong application window for the programme's academic calendar.

477.title: Boren Awards (Boren Scholarships and Boren Fellowships)
477.description: The Boren Awards fund intensive overseas language study for U.S. undergraduate students (Boren Scholarships) and research or language study for U.S. graduate students (Boren Fellowships). They pay a fixed grant of $8,000, $12,500 or $25,000 depending on the duration of overseas study, and the programme states plainly that the award "is not all-inclusive" and is designed to cover only the majority of an awardee's overseas expenses. In exchange, recipients commit to at least one year of federal service in support of U.S. national security after graduation.

477.selection_notes: Applications are evaluated by IIE-organized regional merit review panels made up of faculty members and administrators from colleges and universities across the United States, representing a wide array of fields of study. The panels make recommendations on each submitted, eligible application, with final decision-making authority held by the program's federal sponsor, DLNSEO. There is no semi-finalist or interview phase, so everything an applicant would want the selection committee to know must be stated in the essays and other application materials. Selection preference is given to veterans when other factors are equivalent.

official_details.description: The Boren Awards are a component of the National Security Education Program (NSEP) that funds the intensive study of language abroad by U.S. undergraduate and graduate students who commit to federal service. Boren Scholarships support undergraduates and Boren Fellowships support graduate students; both require a continuous period of overseas study with at least 15-20 weekly language contact hours. The award is a fixed grant tier determined by duration of overseas study ($8,000 / $12,500 / $25,000) and is explicitly not all-inclusive: the programme states that funding "is designed to cover the majority of an awardee's overseas expenses" and lists a closed set of eligible and ineligible costs.
purpose: The National Security Education Program (NSEP) awards Boren Scholarships and Fellowships to U.S. undergraduate and graduate students committed to long-term overseas study and to federal service
The Boren Awards fund the intensive study of language abroad by U.S. undergraduate or graduate students

The Boren Awards promote long-term linguistic immersion and regional experience; proposed programs of two or more semesters are strongly encouraged and preference is given to programs of at least 25 weeks
The Boren Awards invest in linguistic and cultural knowledge for aspiring federal government employees
One objective of the Boren Scholarship is to expand international educational opportunities for students who have not studied abroad and who may require financial assistance to do so
The Boren Awards award scholarships and fellowships that have launched alumni careers into the federal workforce

official_details.degree_award: Not a degree award. The Boren Awards fund overseas study or research undertaken alongside a U.S. degree programme; recipients must remain matriculated in a U.S. degree programme and may not graduate until the award is complete.
official_details.duration: 8 to 52 weeks of overseas study. Minimum 12 weeks for most applicants; a special exception allows undergraduate STEM majors to propose summer programmes of 8 weeks or longer. Preference is given to 25 weeks or more. 2027-cycle funding may be applied to programmes starting as early as June 2027 or as late as March 1, 2028.
official_details.application_cycle: Annual. The 2027-2028 cycle covers both Boren Scholarships and Boren Fellowships.

official_details.funding_label: Boren Scholarships: $8,000 for 8-11 weeks (summer programme, STEM majors only); $12,500 for 12-24 weeks; $25,000 for 25-52 weeks. Boren Fellowships: $12,500 for 12-24 weeks; $25,000 for 25-52 weeks. Regional Flagship Language Initiative: approved summer domestic cost PLUS $12,500 (12-24 weeks overseas) or $25,000 (25-52 weeks overseas).
official_details.tuition_coverage: Approved program tuition and fees are eligible, plus home institution matriculation fees up to $2,500 per semester ($5,000 overall cap). This is reimbursement against a closed list of eligible costs, not a tuition waiver at either institution.
official_details.living_cost_coverage: Room and board (housing and food) and books and supplies are eligible expenses, but the award is capped and the programme states the award "is not all-inclusive".
official_details.travel_coverage: Fly America Act compliant round-trip airfare at the lowest cost unrestricted class (basic economy). The page states explicitly that the Open Skies Agreement does not apply to Boren funding. Visa and visa-related costs, checked luggage (up to 2 bags), local transportation and one flight-change fee related to approved travel or approved date changes are also eligible.
official_details.tuition_rule: Nobody waives tuition. The applicant must remain matriculated at an accredited U.S. institution for the whole funded period, and overseas program tuition and fees plus home-institution matriculation fees (capped) are reimbursable eligible costs against the fixed grant.
official_details.home_tuition_rule: Home-institution obligations continue: Boren Scholars and Fellows must stay matriculated at their U.S. institution and may not graduate until the scholarship or fellowship is complete. selection_criteria: Boren Scholarships criterion 1: Does the applicant provide a clear and compelling explanation of the significance of their overseas destination, region, language, field of study, and overseas study to U.S. national security? Priority organizations (Tier One) are the Departments of War, State, and Homeland Security, as well as the Intelligence Community.

Boren Scholarships criterion 2: Does the applicant demonstrate an understanding of how they might fulfill the one-year federal service requirement and a longer-term commitment to the federal government? Consider the leadership potential the applicant would bring to the federal government.

Boren Scholarships criterion 3: Does the applicant demonstrate a serious commitment to language study, before, during, and after their overseas study? The Boren Awards require a minimum of 15-20 contact hours per week. Does the applicant have realistic expectations for the proficiency level obtainable abroad?

Boren Scholarships criterion 4: Has the applicant proposed a study plan in a preferred overseas destination, region, and language, with a preferred major or field of study, meeting the preferred duration of 25+ weeks? If not, have they made a compelling argument on the basis of U.S. national security?
Boren Scholarships criterion 5: Does the applicant possess the appropriate academic preparation, adaptability, flexibility, and maturity required to succeed abroad?

Boren Fellowships criterion 4 (additional): If proposing research in addition to language study, does the applicant have a comprehensive, clear and feasible overseas plan, with language study being the primary purpose of their overseas plan?
Veteran Preference: Veterans of the U.S. armed forces are encouraged to apply, and selection preference will be given to veterans when other factors are equivalent.

Preference factors: the Boren Awards give preference based on program duration, focus on intensive study of a preferred language in a preferred overseas destination, the applicant's field of study, and applicants with longer-term interest in a federal career.
official_details.selection_notes: Applications are evaluated on these criteria by IIE-organized regional merit review panels consisting of faculty members and administrators from colleges and universities across the United States, representing a wide array of fields of study. The regional panels make recommendations for each submitted, eligible application, with final decision-making authority held by the program's federal sponsor, DLNSEO. There is no semi-finalist or interview phase, so everything an applicant would want the selection committee to know should be stated clearly in the essays and other application materials. Applicants are notified if they have been selected in mid-to-late April.

application_steps: 1. Create a new application at https://apply.iie.org/borenscholarship (Boren Scholarships) or https://apply.iie.org/borenfellowship (Boren Fellowships)
2. Pass the Eligibility Determination section - you must answer all of these questions to unlock the rest of the application

3. Enter personal information (name, permanent and mailing address, email, telephone, sex as it appears on your birth certificate, birthdate, country of residence, veteran/reservist/active-service status)

4. Enter academic information (academic level, degree type, major, GPA, maximum possible GPA, institution location, dates attended/graduation date) and upload an UNOFFICIAL transcript of the current institution
5. List up to three relevant jobs and up to three relevant activities, 50-100 words each

6. Enter programme information: study abroad city, program sponsor, program name, proposed overseas institution, Study Plan Summary (max 250 words), upload the Study Abroad Program Description (max 5 pages), weekly contact hours of formal language acquisition, and any alternate study abroad program
7. Write and submit Essay 1 (National Security, max 800 words) and Essay 2 (Motivation and Public Service Careers, max 800 words for Scholarships / 1000 words for Fellowships)
8. Complete the Language Self-Assessment for the Boren language plus up to four additional languages

9. Complete Additional Information: up to three overseas countries, up to five honours and awards, optional other scholarships, ROTC participation, how you learned about Boren, prior NSEP participation
10. Add recommenders, select the type (Letter of Recommendation or Language Evaluation), and click 'Send to Recommender'
11. Read and agree to the Submission Agreement policies
12. Review the application, fix any errors flagged, and click 'Submit Application'

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are a U.S. citizen and will be 18 or older on the day you submit (not just on the deadline day - if you turn 18 shortly before, you must wait)

If your destination is marked with an asterisk on the Boren map, or your language is Arabic, Mandarin or Russian, line up a viable alternate programme in an unrestricted destination for the same language

If you are proposing French or Spanish, check the minimum proficiency rules (French ILR 2+ Speaking, or ILR 1+ via the African Flagship Languages Initiative; Spanish ILR 1+ Speaking, or ILR 1 if STEM) and expect proficiency verification by testing

important_advice_for_students: Start with essay 1 and essay 2, not the form fields - there is no interview round, so the essays carry the whole case
Research actual federal career opportunities before writing essay 2; the panel looks for realistic understanding of the hiring process, not enthusiasm
Apply even if you have never studied abroad; the programme explicitly encourages applicants with no prior overseas experience
Do not submit a budget - applicants do not need to submit a proposed programme budget with the application
Do not try to upload a recommender's letter yourself; the system only accepts letters submitted by the recommender, and you will not be able to read it
Do not apply to an online programme; all proposed study must occur in the overseas destination
Community college students (two-year and transfer) are explicitly encouraged to apply
If you are already enrolled in a Language Flagship undergraduate programme, you may apply to fund your Capstone year abroad using the same application
common_rejection_risks: Proposing a country that is Western Europe, Canada, Australia or New Zealand - always ineligible

A national security argument in essay 1 that contradicts the career plan in essay 2
Jargon-heavy essay 1 written for specialists instead of an educated generalist audience
Transcripts containing an unredacted Social Security number or date of birth
Recommenders who are family members or friends, or letters submitted by a relative

Not renewable as published - the award is a fixed one-time grant tier set by overseas duration, and requests to increase awards above the published maximums are contingent upon availability of funds. No return-home obligation is published; instead recipients must complete at least one year of federal service in support of U.S. national security after graduation, with preference given to a longer-term commitment. Internships conducted during a Boren-funded period may not be remunerated nor conducted with the U.S. or a foreign government, and Boren Fellows may not work as journalists while abroad, even freelance or unpaid. 479.title: NSF Graduate Research Fellowship Program (NSF GRFP)
479.description: The NSF GRFP funds full-time graduate students pursuing research-based master's or doctoral degrees in NSF-supported STEM fields at accredited, nonprofit U.S. institutions. Each fellowship provides three years of financial support over a five-year fellowship period: a $37,000 annual stipend paid to the fellow and a $16,000 annual cost-of-education allowance paid to the institution in lieu of all tuition and mandatory fees, so there is no tuition or mandatory-fee cost to the student. There is no post-graduate study service requirement, and fellows may transfer to a different institution after completion of the first fellowship year. Estimated 1,500 awards for the 2027 solicitation (NSF 26-526), pending availability of funds.
479.deadline_display: Reference letters due October 16, 2026 by 8:00 p.m. Eastern time. Application deadlines: October 19, 2026 (Life Sciences); October 20, 2026 (Computer and Information Science and Engineering; Materials Research; Psychology; Social Sciences); October 22, 2026 (Engineering); October 23, 2026 (Chemistry; Geosciences; Mathematical Sciences; Physics and Astronomy). All applications must be received by 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time on the deadline date for the Major Field of Study selected. November 15, 2026 is the last day to withdraw an application without it counting towards the number of times an individual may apply.
479.region: United States (applicants must be U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals or permanent residents; study must be at a nonprofit institution of higher education accredited in, and having a campus located in, the United States, its territories or possessions, or the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico)
479.duration: Five-year fellowship period with three years of financial support
479.application_period: The GRFP Application Module usually opens in July or August; applications for the 2027 competition close between October 19 and October 23, 2026 depending on Major Field of Study, with reference letters due October 16, 2026. The module opened in time for the 2026 application cycle; the 2027 application deadlines were published August 25, 2026.
479.official_source: U.S. National Science Foundation (NSF), Division of Graduate Education
