Must intend to enroll or be enrolled full-time in an eligible research-based master's or doctoral degree program in an eligible field of study in STEM.
Must never have previously accepted an NSF Graduate Research Fellowship.
Must have declined any previously offered NSF Graduate Research Fellowship by the deadline (if applicable).

Must have completed less than one academic year in a graduate degree program according to the institution's academic calendar; non-degree coursework must be clearly identified in the transcript and does not count toward this limit.
Must not be a current NSF employee.

Degree programs must be at a nonprofit institution of higher education accredited in, and having a campus located in, the United States, its territories, or possessions, or the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico.
An eligible applicant can submit only one application per annual competition.

Fellowships may only be used for an eligible graduate degree program at a nonprofit academic institution accredited in, and having a campus located in, the U.S., its territories, possessions, or the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico.

479.selection_notes: Applications are reviewed by disciplinary and interdisciplinary scientists, engineers and STEM experts selected by NSF Program Officers, with care taken to ensure no conflicts of interest. Applications are reviewed in broad areas of related disciplines based on the Major Field of Study selected by the applicant, using the two NSF Merit Review Criteria: Intellectual Merit (potential to advance knowledge) and Broader Impacts (potential to benefit society and contribute to specific, desired societal outcomes). Intellectual Merit factors include the ability to plan and conduct research, work independently, work as part of a team, interpret and communicate research, take initiative, think creatively, solve problems, persist and overcome challenges, and demonstrated intellectual ability as indicated by grades, coursework and awards. Broader Impacts factors include increasing participation in STEM, improving STEM education through outreach and mentoring, increasing public scientific literacy, increasing collaboration among academia and industry, improving educator development, improving societal well-being, developing a globally competitive STEM workforce, improving national security, increasing U.S. economic competitiveness, and enhancing research and education infrastructure. GRFP was established to recruit and support individuals who demonstrate the potential to make significant contributions in STEM.

official_details.description: The purpose of the U.S. National Science Foundation Graduate Research Fellowship Program (GRFP) is to help ensure the quality, vitality, and strength of the scientific and engineering workforce of the United States. Since 1952, the program recognizes and supports outstanding graduate students pursuing full-time research-based master's and doctoral degrees in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) fields. GRFP was established to recruit and support individuals who demonstrate the potential to make significant contributions in STEM. Each Fellowship provides three years of support over a five-year Fellowship period. For each of the three years of support, NSF provides a $37,000 stipend and a $16,000 Cost of Education allowance provided to the institution of higher education (IHE) in lieu of all tuition and mandatory fees for each Fellow using the support in a Fellowship year. While the Fellowship is offered to the individual, the Fellowship funds are awarded to the IHE at which a Fellow is enrolled, and the IHE is responsible for disbursement of the stipend to the Fellow.

Because the fellowship is offered to the individual but the funds are awarded to the IHE, the institution is responsible for disbursement of the stipend to the fellow.

document_format_rules: PDF format only for the statement documents.
Official transcripts should be uploaded in PDF format.

Page limits: Personal, Relevant Background, and Future Goals Statement three pages; Graduate Research Plan two pages. The page limits include all references, citations, charts, figures, images, and lists of publications and presentations.
Page size: standard 8.5" x 11" page size.

Margins: 1" margins on all sides, with no text inside the 1" margins (no header, footer, name, or page number). Remove page numbers; stray images or shapes can violate the margin rule even when the page margin is set to 1 inch.

Fonts: Arial (not Arial Narrow), Courier New, or Palatino Linotype in 10-point or larger; Times New Roman or Computer Modern family, 11-point or larger. Symbol or Cambria Math fonts are accepted for Greek letters or special characters. Smaller than 10-point fonts are accepted for mathematical formulas, equations, figures, tables or diagram captions.
Spacing: no less than single-spacing (approximately 6 lines per inch). Do not use line spacing options such as "exactly 11 point," that are less than single spaced.
Equations and symbols should be inserted as a non-editable image to bypass compliance checking and avoid font type and size errors.
Provide descriptive alternative text (alt text) for all images, graphs and charts, and use sufficient colour contrast for legibility.
Do not include links to supplemental materials (papers, videos); reviewers are instructed to evaluate only the evidence provided within the application.

Google Docs may not properly export bulleted text and should not be used; OpenOffice inserts an unallowable font for superscripts and subscripts; certain LaTeX-generated PDF elements are not yet supported and LaTeX fonts in formulas are not supported; Microsoft Word 2007 or earlier may produce font errors.
In Microsoft Office, "Select All" does not include inserted images, shapes, numbered lists or bullets, which carry their own fonts and must be updated to accepted fonts and sizes.
If text is inside an image, it must be part of the image and not editable, otherwise font errors can result.
Do not use 'Print as PDF'; use 'Export' / 'Create PDF'. On Mac, avoid 'Save as PDF' set to 'Best for Printing'; choose 'Best for electronic distribution and accessibility'.
To check fonts: open the PDF, right click the document content, select 'Document Properties', open the 'Fonts' tab and review the font types.
Blank pages within a PDF cause upload errors; export the PDF to Word, delete the blank page and re-save as PDF.
Applications are automatically checked by the GRFP Application Module for compliance; documents that are not compliant will not be accepted.
selection_criteria: Intellectual Merit: the potential to advance knowledge.
Broader Impacts: the potential to benefit society and contribute to the achievement of specific, desired societal outcomes.
official_details.selection_notes: Applications are reviewed by disciplinary and interdisciplinary scientists, engineers, and experts in STEM fields. Reviewers are selected by NSF Program Officers charged with oversight of the review process, and care is taken to ensure that reviewers have no conflicts of interest with the applicants. Applications are reviewed in broad areas of related disciplines based on the Major Field of Study the applicant selected, using all available information in the completed application. Intellectual Merit factors may include the applicant's ability to plan and conduct research, work independently, work as a part of a team, interpret and communicate research (e.g. through publications or presentations), take initiative, think creatively, solve problems, persist and overcome challenges, and demonstrated intellectual ability as indicated by grades, coursework and awards. Broader Impacts factors may include the likelihood that the applicant's activities will increase participation in STEM, improve STEM education in schools through outreach and mentoring, increase public scientific literacy and public engagement with STEM through community outreach, increase collaboration among academia, industry and other types of organizations, improve education and educator development at any level in STEM, improve the well-being of individuals in society, develop a globally competitive STEM workforce, improve national security, increase the economic competitiveness of the U.S., and enhance infrastructure for research and education. NSF does not provide past applications or statements. GRFP funds people, not specific projects; the plan demonstrates potential, not a binding commitment. The program is highly competitive. NSF typically notifies applicants in the spring. Estimated number of awards under the 2027 solicitation: 1500, pending availability of funds.

479.notes: No post-graduate study service requirement. Fellowship funds are awarded to the institution of higher education at which the fellow is enrolled, and the institution is responsible for disbursing the stipend to the fellow; the fellowship is therefore only usable at an eligible accredited nonprofit U.S. institution. The fellowship period is five years with three years of financial support, so fellows must plan for two unfunded years. Fellows may transfer to another institution after completing the first fellowship year. Practice-oriented professional degree programs (medical, dental, law, public health, MBA, MPH, MSW, JD, MD, DVM, DDS) are excluded at any time during the fellowship, as are joint science-professional degree programs. Applicants may submit only one application per annual competition, and only in the first year of their first graduate degree program (joint bachelor's-master's students are limited to one application). No clinical or medical-school pathway is eligible.

483.description: ISSS administers a set of distinct named scholarships for international students, split into spring/summer-term awards (Oct 1 – Nov 1 window) and fall/academic-year awards (Feb 1 – Mar 1 window). Applicants search "ISSS" in LASSO.

eligibility: Applicants must already be **enrolled full-time at UT Austin** and must have **completed an entire course of study for two academic semesters** at UT Austin (minimum cumulative GPA above 2.0 undergraduate / 3.0 graduate), and demonstrate financial need or the award-specific criteria. Specific awards add conditions: e.g. STEM Scholarship limited to Cockrell Engineering, Dell Medical School and most College of Natural Sciences programmes; TAMS and GNS are administered on behalf of the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board. Applications are submitted via the university-wide **LASSO** system.
483.eligibility_summary: International students meeting eligibility criteria for specific scholarships. Apply via LASSO university-wide scholarship system using keyword 'ISSS'. Must be admitted or enrolled at UT Austin.
benefits: Scholarships are **one-time awards and are not guaranteed in subsequent years**. 14% of cash awards is withheld for US tax purposes unless a tax treaty applies or the recipient is a resident alien. Cash awards are applied automatically to outstanding UT debts, with the excess paid to the student's direct deposit account. Varies per award — spring/summer: Carlos and Clara Quintanilla USD 5,000; Ethel Loving de Diaz USD 4,500; SIAWE USD 3,500; Dr. David Nilsson USD 2,000; General ISSS Financial Aid (cash, amount not stated); IEFS (amount not stated); TAMS (non-resident tuition waiver). Fall/academic year: STEM Scholarship USD 4,800; African Leadership Bridge USD 5,000 (USD 2,500 per semester) plus non-resident tuition waiver; Iimura Peace USD 5,000; Jerry D. Wilcox USD 3,500; Khalid Alhilali USD 2,500; General ISSS Financial Aid (cash); IEFS; TAMS; Good Neighbor Scholarship (one year's tuition — fall, spring and summer — for students born in and resident in a Western Hemisphere nation; excludes fees, health insurance and the ISSS support fee).
483.coverage: Each named award is either a one-time cash scholarship, a tuition scholarship, or a waiver of the nonresident portion of tuition; none is presented as covering tuition, living costs and all required expenses.

All award-specific eligibility criteria must be met to apply

500.title: Grants for the USA - swissuniversities
500.description: This swissuniversities hub covers two scholarship programmes for study or research in the United States: the US State Department-sponsored Fulbright Program (both the Foreign Student Program for Swiss graduates and Ph.D. students and the Visiting Scholar Program for Swiss researchers) and the Medicus Student and Scholar Exchange Program funded by the Swiss Benevolent Society of New York. The Fulbright Foreign Student Program awards about USD 20,000 for a 4-10 month non-renewable grant, plus J-1 visa sponsorship, insurance up to USD 100,000 per incident, and IIE university placement. The 2027-2028 Fulbright competition closed on 3 August 2026; Medicus applications for 2027-2028 are due in March 2027.

official_details.description: This swissuniversities hub covers two scholarship programmes for study or research in the United States: the US State Department-sponsored Fulbright Program (both the Foreign Student Program for Swiss graduates and Ph.D. students and the Visiting Scholar Program for Swiss researchers) and the Medicus Student and Scholar Exchange Program funded by the Swiss Benevolent Society of New York. The Fulbright Foreign Student Program awards about USD 20,000 for a 4-10 month non-renewable grant, plus J-1 visa sponsorship, insurance up to USD 100,000 per incident, and IIE university placement. application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you hold Swiss citizenship, or contact the Fulbright Commission or US Embassy in your country of citizenship instead

Ask your registrar now to send certified transcripts directly to swissuniversities in a sealed envelope; this is the step most likely to be missed
Arrange three referees who will upload their letters into the IIE portal themselves
common_rejection_risks: Submitting the online form without the sealed hard-copy transcripts arriving by the deadline - the application is explicitly incomplete until both are received
Fields of medicine, dentistry or veterinary medicine, and any study involving clinical or patient/animal contact
Holding a pre-arranged affiliation with a specific US university, or intending a double degree with a named university
Already holding admission to a US programme for 2026-2027 and intending to defer it - not eligible
Listing only highly selective US universities, which counts against you
Omitting the Fulbright-mission dimension from the personal statement, which is a stated selection criterion
Extensive recent experience of living or studying in the US, which reduces your score
estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition beyond what the grant and any negotiated partial tuition waiver cover
Living costs in excess of the grant for a multi-year programme, since the grant covers only the first year and is not renewable
Family travel - DFAT-equivalent funding here covers individual Fellows only and the Fulbright programme does not fund or support family members
Language testing costs, offset only by vouchers awarded after selection
document_audit: Verify every transcript and degree document is in English or accompanied by an original English translation
Confirm the institution's postal/courier delivery will arrive by 3 August 2026, not merely be posted
Check the IIE portal shows all three reference letters as received before the deadline
Have TOEFL/IELTS booked early enough for results to reach IIE by mid-October 2026, even though the test can follow the application deadline

527.title: Ibrahim Leadership Fellowships 2027
527.description: The Ibrahim Leadership Fellowships place three Fellows per year for 12 months in the executive offices of the African Development Bank (Abidjan), the UN Economic Commission for Africa (Addis Ababa) or the International Trade Centre (Geneva). Fellows work on research and policy design and receive direct mentorship from the head of the host organisation. purpose: Identify and mentor the future generation of outstanding African leaders. The Ibrahim Leadership Fellowships were established in 2011 for this purpose (Mo Ibrahim Foundation fellowships page).

Prepare the next generation of outstanding African leaders by providing unique work opportunities at the most senior level of prominent African institutions or multilateral organizations whose mandate is to improve the economic and social prospects of Africa, thereby creating a pipeline of future African leaders (AfDB vacancy notice).
Allow talented individuals to increase and enhance their professional capacity with the intention of contributing to the governance and development of their countries (AfDB vacancy notice).

Enable young African professionals to develop leadership capacity in a large institution, gain knowledge of the functioning of the United Nations, better understand Africa's socio-economic challenges and contribute to the analytical, advocacy and policy advisory work of the Commission (UNECA 2027 Mo Ibrahim Fellowship Programme notice).
sdg_requirement_details: No SDG or development-alignment requirement is published for applicants. The UNECA notice states that ECA's mission is informed by the 2030 Agenda and Agenda 2063 and lists ECA's five strategic directions (including green growth, innovative financing for infrastructure, peace and security, and gender equality), but it does not require applicants to align their proposal with, or report against, any specific SDG.
The Mo Ibrahim Foundation's own fellowships page attaches no development or SDG designation to the Fellowship.

Research and policy design assignment, not a taught course of study

official_details.tuition_rule: Not applicable. No tuition is charged and none is waived, because no course of study is funded. The AfDB notice states that the Foundation 'will finance the costs associated with the position' and that 'this position is not a regular position of the African Development Bank'.
covered_expenses: Annual stipend of $100,000, paid monthly by the host organisation out of funds provided by the Foundation (AfDB: 'The fellow will receive an annual stipend monthly paid by the Bank out of the funds provided by Foundation')

The host's staff medical insurance and retirement plans: the Fellow 'shall not participate in the Bank's staff medical insurance and retirement plans' (AfDB notice; UNECA notice states the same exclusion)

The Fellow's own medical insurance, child education and retirement plan arrangements: 'The Fellow will cover his/her own medical insurance, child education and retirement plan arrangements for the period he/she will be working at ECA' (UNECA notice); the Foundation's role is only to ensure the Fellow has such arrangements (AfDB notice)
Any tuition, course or study cost of any kind

general_eligibility: National of an African country (Mo Ibrahim Foundation fellowships page). AfDB route: must be a national of an AfDB member country, residing anywhere in the world. UNECA route: must be a national of an ECA member State, residing anywhere in the world.
At least 7 years of relevant work experience (Foundation page, AfDB notice and UNECA notice all state this).

Master's degree as a minimum: the Foundation page states 'Master's degree'; the AfDB notice requires 'outstanding academic credentials backed by a minimum of a Master's Degree from a recognized institution in banking, business, economics or other social sciences, finance, international development, or in any other discipline relevant to the Bank's business'; the UNECA notice requires 'at least a Master's degree or higher in Economics, Social Sciences, International Development, Business Administration, Law, Finance, Engineering, or any discipline relevant to the work of ECA'.

Relevant and demonstrable work experience, strong communication skills, demonstrated leadership skills and the ability to work with others (AfDB notice).
Competency in professionalism, teamwork, client orientation, planning and organising, and leadership potential (UNECA notice).
Sound knowledge of the internet and basic software for word processing, spreadsheets and presentations (UNECA notice).
UNECA route only: fluency in either English or French, with working knowledge of the other language desirable, and the application must be in either English or French.
ineligibility_conditions: Not an active, non-active, retired or separated staff member of the African Development Bank (AfDB route)
No close family relations with an active or non-active staff member of the Bank, such as mother, father, sister and brother (AfDB route)
Government officials, active military personnel and political party leaders are not eligible (AfDB route)
Not a national of an AfDB member country (AfDB route: 'To apply for this position, you need to be national of one of AfDB member countries')
Must not be an employee of the United Nations Secretariat or ECA (UNECA route)
Aged 40 or over on the application deadline date, unless the applicant is a woman under 45 with children (UNECA route)
Applications received after 20 November 2026 at 11:59 p.m. (23:59) Addis Ababa time are not reviewed, and 'no exceptions will be made' (UNECA route)
Incomplete submissions are not considered 'under any circumstances'; where several submissions are received from the same applicant only the most recent is reviewed (UNECA route)

masters: A Master's degree is the minimum academic qualification on all three host routes. AfDB: 'outstanding academic credentials backed by a minimum of a Master's Degree'. UNECA: 'at least a Master's degree or higher'. The Mo Ibrahim Foundation's own page states only 'Master's degree'.

The AfDB notice additionally requires the discipline to be relevant to the Bank's business; the UNECA notice lists Economics, Social Sciences, International Development, Business Administration, Law, Finance, Engineering or any discipline relevant to the work of ECA.
phd: No separate PhD-level rule is published for the 2027 cycle. The UNECA notice requires 'at least a Master's degree or higher', so a doctorate satisfies the education minimum, but no additional academic standard is set for PhD holders and no doctoral funding is described.

host_requirements: AfDB route: the Fellow performs the functions and duties of the position at the headquarters of the Bank in Abidjan, Republic of Côte d'Ivoire, 'or in any other location from which the Bank carries out its operations'.
AfDB route: the Fellow takes leadership guidance from the President, the Managing Directors, the Chief of Staff and Director of Cabinet and/or a designated Representative.

UNECA route: duty station Addis Ababa, Ethiopia; the Fellow is mentored by the Executive Secretary of ECA and/or a designated Representative in the Office of the Executive Secretary (OES) and supports the OES programmatic and administrative functions.
ITC route: the Foundation's page quotes the ITC Executive Director describing the programme as an opportunity to work alongside the Executive Director and her team in Geneva.
The Fellow signs a contract with the host before commencing of service (AfDB and UNECA notices).

For the duration of the contract the Fellow must comply with the Staff Regulations and Rules of the host for all operational purposes and purposes of conduct, and only the host, not the Foundation, may direct and instruct the Fellow.
The Fellow may be required to travel to different locations on the host's instructions (AfDB notice).

For the AfDB route, the host's own recruitment system applies the same standards as staff recruitment, including that the Bank does not accept dual nationality and requires supporting government-issued IDs such as a passport or national identity card.
document_format_rules: UNECA route: all documents must be submitted as PDF attachments. The notice states 'any other document/attachment types will not be accepted'.
UNECA route: large documents may be combined or compressed into a .zip file if necessary. The notice states 'Please do NOT use any other file compression formats (e.g. RAR)'.
UNECA route: the application must be in either English or French.
UNECA route: all required documents must be submitted at one time and in one email; the notice states that only the most recent submission from an applicant will be reviewed.

UNECA route: the UN Administrative Profile (AP) must be generated as a PDF from the Inspira system (https://inspira.un.org) and attached to the email. The notice states that ECA does not have the ability to retrieve draft or created APs from Inspira, so an email submission without a complete AP as a PDF attachment is considered incomplete and will not be reviewed.

UNECA route: the cover/motivation letter is created inside the online AP creation process in Inspira and appears on page 1 of the AP PDF under the heading 'Cover Letter/Motivation Statement for this Application'.
UNECA route: take a screenshot showing that the online survey responses have been sent, and include it in PDF format.

UNECA route: letters of recommendation must be addressed to the '2027 ECA Mo Ibrahim Leadership Fellow Selection Committee'. Referees must send the letters directly to the applicant, who then includes them in the email submission; letters transmitted directly from referees to ECA will not be considered.

UNECA route: copies of academic degree certificates for master's degrees and doctorate/terminal degrees only. The notice states that copies of academic certificates that are not degrees, and copies of high school diplomas/transcripts, are not required, and that first-level (baccalaureate) documentation is not required because a master's is the minimum.

AfDB route: the online form on the Bank's website must be completed and submitted with a comprehensive CV indicating date of birth, nationality, education and relevant experience, plus copies of academic transcripts and three letters of recommendation attached.
No file size limit, accepted file type, page limit, translation rule or signature rule is published on the AfDB notice, the UNECA notice or the Foundation page. These remain unconfirmed.
official_details.selection_notes: AfDB route: the Bank's Human Resources Department carries out an initial vetting of applications to develop a short list of ten (10) applicant files to be further reviewed by the Foundation; a short list of three (3) candidates is presented to the President of the Bank or his designate for final selection. Only applicants who fully meet the Bank's requirements and are considered for interview will be contacted, and the President reserves the right to appoint a candidate at a lower level. UNECA route: due to an anticipated high volume of applications only finalists are contacted and no feedback is given to unsuccessful applicants; received applications are acknowledged within one week; an update is posted to the ECA fellowship page once selection concludes. The Mo Ibrahim Foundation page does not publish a selection method of its own beyond routing applicants to the hosts.
application_steps: Choose the host organisation route from the links published on the Mo Ibrahim Foundation fellowships page: African Development Bank (Abidjan), International Trade Centre (Geneva) or UNECA (Addis Ababa).

AfDB route: go to the vacancy page for the 2027 Mo Ibrahim Foundation Leadership Fellowship Program and complete the online application form on the Bank's recruitment system (external candidates apply at https://afdb.jobs2web.com/job-invite/2343/).
AfDB route: prepare a comprehensive CV that states date of birth, nationality, education and relevant experience, and attach copies of academic transcripts and three letters of recommendation.

UNECA route: create an account on the UN Inspira system (https://inspira.un.org), then build a draft Administrative Profile with no linked Job Opening and generate it as a PDF; the cover/motivation letter is created as part of that process and appears on page 1.
UNECA route: complete the required online survey and take a screenshot showing the responses were sent, in PDF format.
UNECA route: obtain three letters of recommendation addressed to the '2027 ECA Mo Ibrahim Leadership Fellow Selection Committee'; referees send them to the applicant, not to ECA.

important_advice_for_students: This is a job, not a scholarship. Budget your relocation to Abidjan, Addis Ababa or Geneva on the assumption that the $100,000 stipend is the only guaranteed income: no official page states that it covers housing, meals or day-to-day living costs, and no housing allowance is published.

You must fund your own medical insurance, your children's education and your retirement plan for the whole 12 months. On the UNECA route the notice states this in terms; on the AfDB route the Foundation only ensures that you have these arrangements, it does not pay for them.
Apply on the host page you actually want, and treat that host's deadline as binding. The three routes are three different systems with three different forms and document lists.

On the UNECA route, letters of recommendation must come to you, not to ECA. A letter the referee emails directly to ECA is not counted, and a submission with fewer than three letters is treated as incomplete and not reviewed.
On the UNECA route, submit everything in one email as PDFs. Splitting the package across emails is explicitly not accepted, and where several emails arrive only the last is read.

Do not send undergraduate transcripts or high school documents on the UNECA route. The notice says they are not required and that baccalaureate-level documentation is unnecessary because a master's is the minimum.

Budget extra time for the Inspira Administrative Profile. ECA cannot pull a draft AP from Inspira, so if the PDF is not attached your application is never opened. Contact kassahunb@un.org for technical support well before the deadline.
There is no feedback if you are unsuccessful. Only finalists are contacted.

Do not assume a Fellowship leads to a job at the host. On the AfDB route you are barred from applying for a Bank staff post for a year after the Fellowship, and there is no presumption of future employment.
All three hosts place their emphasis on private-sector experience and development-policy analysis. A CV that is purely academic or purely governmental reads as a weaker fit than the notice asks for.
questions_to_ask_host: What is the exact closing date and time on this specific host's system, and does it differ from the 20 November 2026 date the Foundation publishes?
What file formats and maximum file sizes does the host's portal accept for the CV, transcripts and recommendation letters?
Is there a stated page limit or word limit for the CV, and must the CV follow a host template?
Does the host require the three recommendation letters to be on letterhead, signed, or in any specific language?
What are the net-of-tax implications of the monthly stipend in the host country, and does the host deduct anything at source?
Where is the Fellow expected to live, is accommodation arranged or subsidised in any way, and what are typical local living costs against the stipend?
Does the host provide any supplementary health cover beyond the Fellow's own policy, and what does staff medical insurance cost locally?
What are the host's rules on the Fellow's dependants accompanying them, and on schooling for children?
Who pays for a return visit home during the 12 months, and what happens if the Fellowship ends early?
What is the exact reporting line and the expected weekly time commitment, given that the Fellow complies with the host's Staff Regulations and Rules?
Does the host provide a completion certificate or reference at the end of the 12 months?

528.selection_notes: The Foundation looks for young leaders who aspire to leadership, reconciliation, education and entrepreneurship, and who demonstrate the combination of intellect and character. Applicants are screened in rounds: a notification by mid-July indicates whether the applicant reached Round Two, by end of July for Round Three, and by end of August whether they are invited to a Final Round interview. Final Round interviews are conducted in South Africa in October, and final-round applicants based outside South Africa are flown in for an in-person interview with the selection committee. Selected scholars are notified by the end of October.

528.notes: The scholarship cannot be deferred: you must accept it for the year it is offered. Attendance at the residential workshops and regional pods is mandatory and a condition of the scholarship, and the Foundation will not accept travel outside South Africa, even for research purposes, as a reason for absence. You may not hold other scholarships or funded opportunities and may not do paid work for more than 12 hours a week. The award is conditional on you being offered a place at a South African institution, and the Foundation does not apply to universities for you. If you are not accepted by a South African institution in time, you cannot accept the scholarship. The Foundation does not pay visa application costs, and states that a delayed visa may mean you cannot start on time and could lose the scholarship. Applicants from outside South Africa may need SAQA verification, which the Foundation states can take 4-8 weeks and is not covered by the award. Any amount you owe prior to becoming a Scholar is your sole responsibility. The Foundation does not fund MBAs, block courses, or courses delivered predominantly online, and distance learning is not allowed.

529.title: TEF Entrepreneurship Programme
529.degree: Not a degree programme (entrepreneurship training and seed funding)
529.description: The TEF Entrepreneurship Programme is the Tony Elumelu Foundation's flagship annual programme for African entrepreneurs, combining business management training, mentorship, coaching and a USD 5,000 non-refundable seed capital award. The application is completed on the TEFConnect digital platform and the business assessment test score determines eligibility. Selected participants complete training modules on TEFConnect, submit a business plan, financial projection and pitch video, and then provide business registration, tax and banking documents before the seed capital is paid into their business account. This is a business grant and training programme, not a scholarship, so no tuition or living costs are paid.

529.selection_notes: Independent third-party experts review eligible applications. A minimum score in the business assessment test is required or the applicant is notified as ineligible and encouraged to reapply the following year. Eligible applicants undergo LSEG World-Check global compliance screening and a physical verification exercise by authorised enumerators, which may be in person or virtual. Shortlisting is evaluated on business feasibility, market opportunity, financial understanding, scalability, and leadership and entrepreneurial skills. In the investment readiness phase an independent audit consulting firm reviews the business plan, financial projection and pitch video and ranks participants for investment readiness. Shortlisted participants are notified of participation on the 22nd of March each year.

selection_criteria: Business feasibility: the viability of the business idea in its current environment, including practicality, sustainability and associated risks, with a clear value proposition, a well-defined business model and the ability to address an existing problem or need

Market opportunity: a well-defined target market with substantial demand, assessed on size, accessibility and growth potential, plus how the business differentiates itself from competitors, with market research insights and a clear customer-acquisition strategy

Financial understanding: a strong grasp of financial management and the ability to make informed financial decisions, covering cost structures, revenue streams, pricing models, profitability projections, resource management and expense tracking
Scalability: whether the business model can be replicated, expanded into new markets or attract investment over time, with capacity to increase revenue while maintaining or improving efficiency
Leadership and entrepreneurial skills: leadership qualities, resilience and a proactive mindset, with demonstrated innovation, problem-solving ability and commitment to long-term success
Minimum score in the mandatory business assessment test: applicants who do not reach it are classified ineligible and are not reviewed further

purpose: Empower African entrepreneurs and entrepreneurship on the continent. The Tony Elumelu Foundation Entrepreneurship Programme is described as 'the largest African philanthropic initiative committed to empowering African entrepreneurs and entrepreneurship on the continent'.
Select and build the most promising African entrepreneurs so that only those with the greatest potential to drive economic growth and create jobs receive training, mentorship and funding.
Provide training on the TEFConnect digital hub and direct funding so entrepreneurs can start, manage and scale their businesses, and so they create direct and indirect jobs.

official_details.selection_notes: The process runs in six phases after application. Applications are immediately and automatically reviewed when the window closes and applicants are notified via TEFConnect and email of their category. Independent third-party experts review applications deemed eligible, assessing the business idea for feasibility, scalability, market potential and financial viability. Shortlisted applicants undergo LSEG World-Check screening, a global risk-intelligence database, to ensure compliance with global financial and business regulations, then a Physical Verification Exercise by authorised enumerators to confirm identity and the legitimacy of the business documents provided, conducted by physical visit or virtually. Only applicants who pass application review, global compliance and physical verification are considered for the cohort. Successful applicants are notified of participation confirmation on 22 March each year. In the investment readiness phase, an independent audit consulting firm reviews the business plan, financial projection and pitch video, indicates areas of improvement, and ranks participants on investment readiness. In the seed capital phase the TEF Audit and Finance team reviews the disbursement documents.
application_steps: The application portal opens on 1 January and closes at midnight on 1 March each year on the TEFConnect digital platform.

Register on TEFConnect and complete the programme's application form with valid and accurate responses, across four sections: personal information; business idea and experience information; business assessment test; declaration.
Complete all mandatory fields in the online application form.

Attach the requested documents: a valid government-issued ID displaying date of birth and photo, and a high-resolution headshot. Ensure the name and personal details on TEFConnect exactly match the government-issued ID.
Submit the form.
Receive a notification on screen and by email confirming eligibility status and next steps.
Applicants classified ineligible may reapply the following year; there is no appeal route in the published process.

If confirmed as a participant, attend the onboarding session, physical or virtual, and then complete 100% of all training modules on TEFConnect, participate in coaching sessions and engage with the assigned mentor.
Submit a business plan, financial projection and a 2-3 minute pitch video using the templates supplied, for independent audit review and investment-readiness ranking.
Open a business account at one of the partner banks the Foundation lists, so fund tracking and disbursement are easier.

Submit the seed capital documents: government-issued ID, Business Registration Certificate, evidence of tax registration in the business name, a bank reference letter, a Partner Consent form if a co-owner, and a medical report from a reputable hospital if living with a disability.
Sign the TEF Entrepreneurship Programme seed capital undertaking so that payment can be processed into the business account.
Receive the acknowledgement form, the Certificate of Completion and Achievement, and onboarding into the TEF Alumni network.
applicant_submission_route: The applicant submits their own application directly. There is no institutional nomination, university submission, referee-mediated submission or intermediary: registration and submission are on the applicant's TEFConnect account.
Physical verification may involve an authorised enumerator visiting the applicant, or being conducted virtually, so the applicant must be reachable at the address and number given on the application.
The seed capital is paid into the business account the participant provides, so the participant must personally control and open that account.
official_details.application_portal: www.TEFConnect.com - the TEFConnect digital platform. The Foundation states the application portal for the flagship programme opens on 1 January and closes at midnight on 1 March on this platform.
timeline_rules: The application window opens on 1 January and closes at midnight on 1 March every year.

Shortlisted participants are invited to an onboarding session, physical or virtual, after which they are referred to as TEF Entrepreneurship Programme Participants.
The Training Phase follows onboarding and requires 100% completion of all modules on TEFConnect before progression.
The Investment Readiness Phase requires submission of the business plan, financial projection and pitch video, followed by independent audit review and ranking.
The Seed Capital Phase follows successful investment-readiness ranking, with document submission, Audit and Finance endorsement, signature of the seed capital undertaking, and disbursement.
No fixed dates are published for the training, investment readiness and seed capital phases; they are cohort-relative and announced at onboarding.

important_advice_for_students: Treat 1 March midnight as a hard stop. The window closes automatically and late applications are not accepted, so build your application to be submitted and confirmed weeks earlier.

Do not apply if you have ever received anything from a previous Tony Elumelu Foundation programme, or if you already applied in the same window this year. Both are stated disqualifiers, and a first-time application that is wrong costs you a full year.

Make your TEFConnect name and personal details character-for-character identical to your government-issued ID. The Foundation states this exact-match requirement and it also has to hold at the seed capital stage, where your bank reference letter, business name and ID must all agree.

The business assessment test is pass/fail. Applicants who miss the minimum score are classed ineligible with no appeal. Practise before you sit it inside the form, and leave time inside the window to retake it.

Take the shortlist criteria seriously rather than writing a generic business plan: feasibility, market opportunity, financial understanding, scalability and leadership are each separately scored, with market research and financial projections explicitly expected.

Prepare the seed capital documents before onboarding, not after. Business registration, tax registration in the business name, a bank reference letter and the co-owner consent form can each take weeks in some jurisdictions, and every one of them gates the $5,000.

Open the business account at one of the Foundation's partner banks. The Foundation says this makes fund tracking and disbursement easier, and the money is paid into that account, not to you personally.
Complete 100% of the training modules. Partial completion does not progress you to seed capital, whatever else you have done.

If you are a co-owner, the Partner Consent form is mandatory. If you live with a disability, get the medical report from a reputable hospital ready. Both are conditional documents that applicants often leave out.

Budget the $5,000 as capital for the business, not as income for yourself. It is non-refundable and there is no published second tranche, so it does not replace a business plan with real unit economics.
Expect physical or virtual verification by an enumerator after the window closes. Keep your phone reachable and your premises accessible, because this sits between you and the shortlist.

programme_verification.source_freshness_rule: The cycle is annual and calendar-driven, with the window fixed at 1 January to 1 March. Anything describing a cohort year older than the current one is stale, and because the window opens on 1 January, a record written early in the year must be re-checked once the window opens for the following cohort.

529.notes: The seed capital is non-refundable and is not a scholarship: it does not pay tuition or living costs, and applicants must fund their own living expenses throughout the cycle. The portal is only open for two months a year, 1 January to midnight 1 March; there is no rolling intake, so missing the window means waiting a full year. You cannot have previously benefited from any TEF programme, and you cannot reapply within the same application window of the same year, which the Foundation states explicitly. Programme participants whose documents are found inauthentic, contain discrepancies, or match the document details of past TEF Entrepreneurship Programme beneficiaries are immediately disqualified. Seed capital payment requires signing the seed capital undertaking and is processed into the business account you provide.

requirements: Complete all questions in the Foundation's Online Application System (OAS)
Enter name, address and latest contact information correctly
For the 'Topic of your project' field, describe the fellowship activity in a few lines so that it correctly represents the nature of the project
Statement of purpose and work plan must be completed in the Foundation's own format and uploaded as PDF only
Your Statement of purpose and work plan must not exceed 1000 words each
The statement of purpose must outline the applicant's personal and professional trajectory very briefly, and the motivation for taking up the project and how it contributes to social change

The work plan must include a title of the proposed work with a concise description of the work or research planned during the fellowship, the expected outcomes, and in detail the manner in which the project will be undertaken with a clear timeline for 2 years
Two letters are required: a Mentor endorsement letter and a Recommendation letter

The Mentor endorsement letter must include a brief description of the mentor's work experience, the mentor's contact details (email and official address), a statement of why the mentor endorses the applicant's work plan, a statement that the mentor agrees to supervise the applicant's work during the fellowship, willingness to review and comment on quarterly and annual progress reports, and willingness to hold periodic meetings with the Foundation so it can assess the fellow's progress

The Recommendation letter must be from a person who has supervised the applicant's work for at least 6 months; this cannot be the same person as the mentor. For fresh graduates, an academic letter of recommendation is acceptable

official_details.citizenship_residency: International students who are enrolled at a German public or state-recognised university, or who apply from abroad for such a place
purpose: Support international students at a German higher education institution during their studies, materially and ideologically: 'Mit dem FES-Stipendium möchten wir Studierende während ihres Studiums unterstützen - materiell und ideell.'

Enable scholarship holders to concentrate on their studies without financial worries and to have more time for their civic engagement: 'Wir tragen dazu bei, dass unsere Stipendiat:innen sich ohne finanzielle Sorgen auf das Studium konzentrieren können und mehr Zeit für ihr Engagement haben.'
Give international students the chance to complete their studies at a German university. The Foundation states it is particularly pleased when it can give students from abroad that opportunity.

Promote education equity: 'Bildungsgerechtigkeit bedeutet gleiche Chancen für alle.' Selection gives particular weight to applications from people who are the first in their family to study (Erst-Akademiker:innen) and/or have a migration background, from women, and from students at universities of applied sciences and in STEM subjects.

Cultivate a values-oriented environment in which holders exchange ideas and become able to gather sufficient information, act thoughtfully, make decisions and thereby strengthen their social participation.
The Foundation is convinced that commitment to society works best when achieved together.
sdg_requirement_details: No SDG, development-goal or impact-alignment requirement is published. The Foundation states its own commitment to the fundamental values of social democracy and asks applicants to identify with those values, which is a political-values test rather than a development-goal test.

The published selection emphasis is on education equity (Bildungsgerechtigkeit), particularly first-generation students, students with a migration background, women, students at universities of applied sciences and STEM students, rather than on any named international goal.

official_details.degree_award: A full degree at a German higher education institution, not a short-term award. The Grundförderung covers Bachelor's, Master's and Diplom degree programmes and programmes leading to the Staatsexamen. No degree is awarded by the Foundation itself.

Where the Foundation's stipend is described, it is described as support for living during the study, not as a fee waiver.
official_details.home_tuition_rule: Not applicable as a published rule. The programme requires the applicant to be already studying at a German institution, and the Foundation explicitly does not fund study abroad programmes outside the EU or short-term stays abroad.

undergraduate: Bachelor's, Diplom, Magister and Staatsexamen programmes are included in the Grundförderung.

Application window: after the first semester and up to three semesters before the end of the standard period of study. The Foundation's English page states this as until three semesters before finishing the standard period of study, giving the examples 'if 6 semesters by the end of 3rd semester; if 7 semesters by the end of 4th semester'.
Bachelor's students must submit their first graded performance records before applying.
Medicine has its own window: after the fourth semester or after the Physikum, to the end of the sixth semester. The Foundation does not fund medical studies up to and including the Physikum.
Second degrees are not funded unless the applicant already holds an FES scholarship.
masters: Master's and postgraduate programmes are included in the Grundförderung.

Application window: before or at the start of the first higher education semester of the Master's programme, stated as by 30 November for a winter semester start and by 31 May for a summer semester start. The Foundation's English page states the same window as by the end of the first semester.

A short-term course of study of less than three semesters, for example a two-semester Master's programme, is not funded. An applicant who does not qualify for a Master's programme is pointed to the Bachelor/Diplom/Magister/Staatsexamen route.
The German page states that graduates and postgraduates are directed to the separate Promotionsförderung für Ausländer:innen doctoral programme instead.
phd: Not funded under the Grundförderung. Doctoral study is handled by a separate programme, Promotionsförderung für Ausländer:innen, which funds foreign doctoral candidates admitted to a state or state-recognised German university and funds all dissertation projects except medicine.
The Foundation explicitly does not fund doctoral degrees, postdoctoral projects, or the final stages of a doctoral degree.

host_requirements: The applicant must already be enrolled at a German public or state-recognised university, higher education institution or university of applied sciences (an einer deutschen, staatlichen oder staatlich anerkannten Hochschule oder Fachhochschule).
Enrolment must be confirmed by an Immatrikulationsbescheinigung, and university entrance qualification and certificates are among the documents requested at the second stage.
The applicant's study must be a full-time degree programme; extra-occupational and part-time courses of study are not funded.
Scholarship holders with children receive an additional monthly amount, which requires a declared family situation.
The Foundation's English page notes particular importance for students at universities of applied sciences, so those institutions are an accepted host type rather than a second-tier route.
document_format_rules: The application is made in the online application form, using the form published for the Grundförderung für Ausländer:innen at https://www.fes.de/oas/portal/pls/portal/bewsti2014.bewmaske?pFprog=2&pkn=A. The online form is required as the first step and is checked by FES staff against the formal and substantive criteria.

The first-step online form requires general personal information, information on professional and family background, the applicant's motivation to become an FES scholarship holder, and information on socio-political engagement.
Applications must be submitted in German.

Second-stage documents requested by email: a detailed CV covering previous education and socio-political engagement; certificates, university entrance qualification, enrolment certificate (Immatrikulationsbescheinigung) and other evidence; a detailed letter of motivation; and two references (Gutachten) from university lecturers, or from teachers for first-year students.

For the Grundförderung, the Foundation publishes a dedicated document and reference checklist as a downloadable file at https://www.fes.de/index.php?eID=dumpFile&t=f&f=160624, which is the governing list of required documents and guidance for this programme specifically.
Applicants have three weeks to assemble the documents and up to six weeks for the references, and the Foundation sends a receipt confirmation on receipt.

If an applicant is invited to a selection interview and has incurred travel costs, those costs can be reimbursed by submitting the Foundation's travel-cost reimbursement form for the Grundförderung (Fahrtkostenerstattung_BMFTR_Grundförderung), published at https://www.fes.de/index.php?eID=dumpFile&t=f&f=165947.
Applicants can log back in at any time before submitting to continue an unfinished online application, and can upload further documents through the same login once they advance a stage.
The Foundation informs every applicant by email about the result of each stage, and the final decision is communicated at the latest one week after the selection committee's meeting.

No file size limit, accepted file-type list, translation rule, certification rule or document-expiry rule is published on the pages read. The documents checklist PDF and the reference-writing guidance are published as separate files and were not downloaded.
official_details.selection_notes: The procedure has five published steps. Step 1: complete the online application form; FES staff check it against formal and substantive criteria, and within two to four weeks of receipt the applicant receives either a rejection or a request to submit documents and references. Step 2: submit documents and references; the file is reviewed and the applicant receives either a rejection or notification that the application has been passed to a Vertrauensdozentin or Vertrauensdozent. Step 3: the first selection interview, a subject-related discussion with a Vertrauensdozentin or Vertrauensdozent, from which a Gutachten is produced and attached to the file; the applicant then receives either a rejection or notification that the file has gone to a member of the selection committee. Step 4: the second selection interview with a person from the selection committee, producing a further Gutachten attached to the file and tabled at the committee's meeting. Step 5: decision by the selection committee, which meets eight to ten times a year; once both Gutachten are available the application is presented in detail to the committee at the relevant meeting and the members decide on admission to the funding programme. The Foundation informs the applicant of the final decision at the latest one week after the meeting, whether that is an offer or a rejection, and states that the whole process from application to decision can take three to seven months.
application_steps: Apply early. The Foundation states the best time to apply is as early as possible, because it wants scholarship holders to benefit from the scholarship for as long as possible, and the deadlines are listed per programme.

Check your degree-stage window. Master's: before or at the start of the first semester of the Master's programme (winter semester by 30 November, summer semester by 31 May). Bachelor, Diplom, Magister, Staatsexamen: after the first semester and up to three semesters before the end of the standard period of study. Medicine: after the fourth semester or after the Physikum, to the end of the sixth semester.

Complete the online application form for the Grundförderung für Ausländer:innen at https://www.fes.de/oas/portal/pls/portal/bewsti2014.bewmaske?pFprog=2&pkn=A, in German, covering general personal information, professional and family background, your motivation to become an FES scholarship holder, and your socio-political engagement.
Submit the form. FES staff check it against the formal and substantive criteria.
Wait two to four weeks. You will receive either a rejection or an email requesting your documents and references.

If invited, submit within the stated windows: three weeks for the documents and up to six weeks for the references. Documents: a detailed CV covering your previous education and socio-political engagement; certificates, university entrance qualification, enrolment certificate and other evidence; and a detailed letter of motivation. References: two Gutachten from university lecturers.
Consult the Foundation's published Grundförderung document and reference checklist at https://www.fes.de/index.php?eID=dumpFile&t=f&f=160624 for the full required list for this programme.
Use your FES login at https://www.fes.de/oas/portal/pls/portal/bewsti2014.login to upload further documents when you advance to the next stage. FES confirms receipt of the documents.
If the file passes, attend the first selection interview, a subject-related discussion with a Vertrauensdozentin or Vertrauensdozent. A Gutachten is produced and attached to your file.
If you advance, attend the second selection interview with a member of the selection committee. A second Gutachten is produced.
If you have travelled for an interview, submit the Foundation's travel-cost reimbursement form for the Grundförderung to claim reimbursement of your travel costs.

Await the decision. The selection committee meets eight to ten times a year and you will be informed by email at the latest one week after the meeting, whether the outcome is an offer or a rejection. The full process from application to decision can take three to seven months.
applicant_submission_route: The applicant submits directly. The online application form, the documents and the references are all submitted by the applicant to the Foundation, with no institutional nomination and no employer or university acting as an intermediary.
Applications may be submitted formally from Germany or from abroad: 'Bewerbungen sind formell sowohl aus Deutschland als auch aus dem Ausland möglich.'

The two Gutachten must be written by university lecturers, or by teachers for first-year students, and submitted by the applicant with the document package within the stated six-week window. The Foundation publishes guidance on preparing the references separately.
After the first stage, further documents are uploaded by the applicant through the Foundation's own application login.
The Foundation's contact addresses for Auslandsförderung are published for questions, not as a submission channel; submission is through the online system.
official_details.application_portal: The Foundation's online application system at https://www.fes.de/oas/portal/pls/portal/bewsti2014.bewmaske?pFprog=2&pkn=A (the Grundförderung für Ausländer:innen form), with applicant login at https://www.fes.de/oas/portal/pls/portal/bewsti2014.login.
arrival_rules: The applicant must already be living in Germany and studying at a German university at the time of application, and applications may formally be submitted from Germany or from abroad. Consequently there is no arrival provision: the applicant is already in Germany when applying.
No arrival date, latest-arrival rule, visa support arrangement or relocation funding is published. Study abroad programmes outside the EU and short-term stays abroad are not funded.
Enrolment must be confirmed by an Immatrikulationsbescheinigung, and the Foundation's stage-two document request includes the enrolment certificate.
timeline_rules: The best time to apply is as early as possible, because the Foundation wants scholarship holders to benefit for as long as possible.

Application windows by degree stage: Master's, before or at the start of the first semester of the Master's programme (winter semester by 30 November, summer semester by 31 May); Bachelor, Diplom, Magister and Staatsexamen, after the first semester and up to three semesters before the end of the standard period of study (English page: until three semesters before finishing the standard period of study, so by the end of the 3rd semester on a six-semester programme or the end of the 4th semester on a seven-semester programme); medicine, after the fourth semester or after the Physikum to the end of the sixth semester. The Foundation's English page also states diploma, magister and state examination by the end of the 6th semester.

There is no single annual closing date: applications are accepted on a rolling basis within the stage-specific windows, which is why the record's deadline_date is only meaningful as the 30 November master's-stage date.
Step 1 to first outcome: within two to four weeks of receiving the online application, the applicant receives either a rejection or a request to submit documents and references.
Step 2: three weeks to assemble the documents and up to six weeks for the references, with a receipt confirmation on arrival.
The selection committee meets eight to ten times a year, and the applicant is informed of the final decision at the latest one week after the meeting.
Total elapsed time from application to decision: three to seven months.
The Foundation informs all applicants by email about the result of each individual stage.
Applicants who have not yet submitted their online application can log in at any time and continue editing it.
official_application_route: Complete the online application form published for the Grundförderung für Ausländer:innen at https://www.fes.de/oas/portal/pls/portal/bewsti2014.bewmaske?pFprog=2&pkn=A, in German.
The form is checked by FES staff against the formal and substantive criteria, and a decision or a document request follows within two to four weeks.

On invitation, submit the document package and two academic references through the Foundation's application login within three weeks for documents and up to six weeks for references, using the Grundförderung checklist at https://www.fes.de/index.php?eID=dumpFile&t=f&f=160624 as the governing list.
Attend the first selection interview with a Vertrauensdozentin or Vertrauensdozent if invited.
Attend the second selection interview with a member of the selection committee if shortlisted.
Submit the Foundation's travel-cost reimbursement form for the Grundförderung if you have incurred interview travel costs.

The decision is communicated by email at the latest one week after the selection committee's meeting. The Foundation does not publish a postal submission route for the Grundförderung; the online system is the route.

important_advice_for_students: You must already be enrolled at a German university when you apply. This is the first gate, and it is not waivable — an offer of admission is not enough, enrolment is. Plan around being in Germany before the window closes.

German is mandatory, not optional. B2 is the level the Foundation states it accepts, and it accepts it without a certificate, but the application must still be written and submitted in German. Even if you study in English, you must prove German.

Check your degree-stage window before anything else. The windows are different for Master's, Bachelor, and medicine, and they are expressed relative to your semester count rather than as a calendar date. Applying in the wrong window is the most likely reason for an automatic rejection.

Check the funding-exclusion list against your course. A two-semester Master's, medical study up to the Physikum, any doctoral or postdoc stage, a research visit, physiotherapy or psychotherapy training, part-time study, and study outside the EU are all excluded. If your programme is short or part-time, this is the wrong scheme.
A second degree or a language course is not funded unless you already hold an FES scholarship. If you are planning to change course, check whether the new course would be a second degree.
Have your first graded performance records in hand before you apply. They are a stated prerequisite, and Bachelor's students must submit them.

Do the two academic references early. You have three weeks for documents but up to six weeks for the references, so the references are the long pole. University lecturers, not teachers, write them unless you are a first-year student.

Write the civic engagement part seriously. Soci-political commitment and identifying with the values of social democracy are two of the three baseline yes/no questions, and the Foundation looks for students who identify with social democracy and treat volunteering as self-evident.

Play to the Foundation's published priority groups if any apply to you: first in your family to study, migration background, women, universities of applied sciences, STEM. The Foundation states it gives particular weight to these applications.

Budget for what is not covered. The published package is 992 Euro per month plus health insurance costs, with an additional amount for children. Tuition and semester fees at your institution are not listed as covered. Ask your university what the semester contribution is and keep it in your own budget.

Watch the offset rule. The Foundation's English page states that any income exceeding 400 Euro per month is credited against the scholarship, so part-time earnings above that threshold reduce your stipend.
Claim interview travel costs if you have them. The Foundation reimburses travel costs for applicants invited to a selection interview, using its own form. Submit it.

Allow three to seven months. The process runs from the online form through a document request, two interviews with two separate Gutachten, and a committee meeting, and the committee only sits eight to ten times a year.

Talk to a scholarship ambassador before you apply. The Foundation points applicants to its stipendien-botschafter:innen for questions and for encouragement before applying, and these are former holders who answer questions they would rather answer themselves.
questions_to_ask_host: What is the current semester contribution fee at my institution, and does the university offer any waiver for scholarship holders? The Foundation does not publish that it pays it.
What health insurance plan will I be enrolled in, and does its cost vary with my age, marital status or dependants? The Foundation says it covers health insurance costs but publishes no figure.
What counts as the 'first graded performance records' required at application, and does my university issue them in a form I can upload directly?
Does my university offer a thesis supervisor or academic mentor willing to write a Gutachten, and how long do they take?
What is the standard period of study for my programme, so that I can calculate the three-semester application window correctly?
Is there a German course requirement attached to my programme that I should start now, given that applications must be submitted in German?
Does my institution have a scholarship-holder network or working group that FES scholarship holders join, and what does it expect of me in terms of time?
How much do the 18 thematic working groups and the political education seminars take in study time, on top of my coursework?
Is my course one of the excluded categories by another name — for example is it run part-time, is it a two-semester Master's, or is it a research stay rather than a degree programme?
What is the Foundation's offset calculation in practice if I have part-time income, and over what period is it assessed?
How do I apply for the additional amount for scholarship holders with children, and what is the current monthly figure?
Can I change my host institution or my subject after being awarded, and does that affect the stipend?

programme_verification.source_conflict_rule: The programme page for Grundförderung für Ausländer:innen governs this specific scheme's scope, package and degree-stage windows, and the online application page governs the procedure, document list and deadlines. The Foundation's English 'Information in English' page is a cross-programme summary covering all FES schemes; where it differs from the programme page, the programme-specific German page governs, and every difference is recorded in institution_check_required rather than silently resolved. Where the English page is the only source for a rule, such as the 400 € income offset, it is cited explicitly as the English page.
programme_verification.source_freshness_rule: The cycle is continuous and the windows are semester-relative rather than calendar-anchored, so there is no single annual date to go stale; what does change is the stipend rate, the family or children's allowance, the fee schedule at German institutions and the exclusion list. All of these must be re-read each academic cycle before an applicant budgets, and the selection committee's eight-to-ten-meetings-per-year cadence means a rejection is not final until a specific meeting date has passed.

534.description: The Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung's refugee scholarship programme funds Bachelor's, Master's and PhD students who hold a German residence permit. The page is published bilingually in English and Ukrainian. For undergraduate and graduate students the financial support is up to 752 Euro per month depending on income plus 300 Euro for study-related expenses; for PhD candidates it is 1,350 Euro per month plus 100 Euro for research-related expenses. 535.title: Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung Promotionsförderung für Ausländer:innen (FES doctoral scholarship for international doctoral candidates)
535.description: The Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung funds doctoral candidates from abroad who are admitted to a German university, paying 1,500 euros a month plus a supplement for statutory health insurance, together with an extensive political education programme. Applicants must have very good German skills (B2 accepted, also without a certificate, and required even when the dissertation is written in English), socio-political engagement, identification with the values of social democracy, an above-average and fast degree result, and a research project that makes a significant contribution to research. The scholarship does not have to be repaid.
535.deadline_display: No fixed calendar deadline is published. The programme page states the right time to apply is up to about two years before submission of the dissertation ('bis circa zwei Jahre vor Abgabe der Dissertation'), and the application page directs applicants to the individual scholarship programme for the deadlines. The online application form for Promotionsförderung für Ausländer:innen is published and open.

Funding confirmed and quantified: 'Stipendiat:innen der Promotionsförderung für Ausländer:innen erhalten monatlich 1.500 Euro und einen Zuschuss zur
535.region: Germany (doctoral candidates from abroad already admitted to a German university)
535.duration: As a rule three and a half years; in justified exceptional cases it can be granted for longer, but at the latest until the final examination
535.application_period: Continuous/rolling: applications are accepted while the doctoral thesis can still be completed within the funding period, in principle from about two years before submission of the dissertation. The selection committee meets eight to ten times a year and the final decision is communicated at the latest one week after the relevant meeting.

535.selection_notes: The FES checks the online application for formal and content criteria. In selecting, it particularly considers applications from people who are the first in their family to study and/or have a migration background, as well as from women and from students at universities of applied sciences and in MINT subjects. Suitable applicants are passed to a trust lecturer for a specialist interview that produces an opinion; shortlisted applicants then have a second interview with a member of the selection committee, whose opinion goes to the committee's meeting. The selection committee meets eight to ten times a year and decides on admission; the applicant is informed at the latest one week after the meeting. All applicants are informed by email at each stage. 'Above average' refers to the average grade in the subject at the university location or in the training occupation.

536.title: Development-Related Postgraduate Courses (EPOS)
536.description: The DAAD EPOS programme funds individual scholarships for graduates from developing and newly industrialised countries to take a development-oriented postgraduate (mostly Master's) course at a state or state-recognised German university, and in exceptional cases a doctoral degree. The award is a monthly payment of EUR 992 for graduates or EUR 1,300 for doctoral candidates (EUR 1,400 from February 2026), plus payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance and a flat-rate travel allowance. Under certain circumstances scholarship holders may additionally receive a monthly rent subsidy and a monthly allowance for accompanying family members. Scholarships are awarded subject to funding being provided by the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ).

537.title: MOPGA 2027: Visiting Fellowship Program for Early Career Researchers
537.description: MOPGA is a French Government visiting fellowship that pays a monthly allowance to early-career foreign researchers to carry out a 12-month research project in a French host laboratory on climate and environmental themes. Each fellowship covers a monthly allowance of EUR 2,500, a EUR 500 settling-in allowance, and health, civil liability and repatriation coverage. Host laboratories receive no funding under the programme; the money is intended solely to cover the invited researcher's living expenses, and international travel costs are not covered.

purpose: The goal of this PhD is (i) to develop efficient methods for detecting 3D changes and expressing them with simple geometric shapes, and (ii) to analyze the spatio-temporal distribution of these geometric changes at large scales, from city districts to the entire country

Contribute to the JUNN Digital Twin of France and its Territories project, which uses unprecedented remote sensing data on the whole French territory, including airborne LidarHD campaigns and satellite Digital Surface Models, to update 3D city models over time and to understand the long-term evolution of urban landscapes
Address a key scientific challenge: designing methods for efficiently analysing geometric changes and understanding the evolution of urban attributes such as urban growth and architectural variations

Investigate change detection methods that operate directly on concise geometric primitives such as planes and 3D polygons rather than on 3D point clouds, motivated by efficiency and interoperability, since such primitives feed the building reconstruction methods of the JUNN project for efficient 3D model updates

Develop models for analysing the spatio-temporal distribution of planar shapes at large scales and seek correlations on attributes characterising city evolution in terms of shape, physics or functionality

541.title: JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship for Research in Japan (Standard Program)
541.description: JSPS funds postdoctoral researchers from overseas to conduct collaborative research in Japan under the guidance of a Japanese host researcher at a university or other eligible research institution. Financial support is a maintenance allowance of JPY362,000 per month, a round-trip air ticket, a settling-in allowance of JPY200,000, and overseas travel insurance. A Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research for JSPS Research Fellows can also be applied for through the host institution to cover cooperative research-related expenses. Because this is a research appointment rather than a degree programme, there is no tuition to pay and the award is not presented as tuition funding.

official_details.description: JSPS funds postdoctoral researchers from overseas to conduct collaborative research in Japan under the guidance of their hosts in universities and other research institutions in Japan. Financial support is a maintenance allowance of JPY362,000 per month, a round-trip air ticket, a settling-in allowance of JPY200,000, and overseas travel insurance. A Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research for JSPS Research Fellows is available for cooperative research-related expenses.
purpose: Enable overseas postdoctoral researchers to conduct collaborative research in Japan under the guidance of a Japanese host researcher, thereby advancing science in Japan and in other countries
Advance the subject research through the host-candidate collaboration, on the published selection policy

Contribute to the training of young researchers and to the formation of new international research networks, as reflected in the published document-review criteria (establishment of new research networks)

selection_criteria: Selection of applicants (host researcher) and candidates (invited overseas researchers) is done by the JSPS International Program Committee, made up of Japan's frontline researchers

Graduated scoring system on a scale of 1 to 5: 5 superlative, 4 excellent, 3 good, 2 fair, 1 poor

Marks are made on a comprehensive basis, taking into account research achievements, the research plan, estimated research capacity, future potential of the research, and establishment of new research networks
The averaged score in the document review is used as the primary screening criterion in the panel review
Panel review selects a specified number of applicants in each panel review section

The host researcher selects the screening category from the Review Section Table; Review Section Sets pair each review section with the reviewers who screen it, and reviewers are selected in a balanced manner for a diverse range of perspectives
