Published selection policy: not only the score of the document review but also the examiners' reasons and comments are to be given adequate consideration

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you obtained your PhD on or after April 2 of the year six years before the fiscal year, adjusting for maternity or parental leave
Confirm you have never held and started a JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship for Research in Japan (Standard or Pathway)
Confirm you are not a Japanese citizen and do not hold Japanese permanent residence status
Identify and secure a willing host researcher at a KAKENHI-eligible Japanese institution who can apply for a KAKENHI grant
Ask the host institution for its internal deadline, which can be more than a month before the JSPS deadline
Decide the research plan with the host in writing before applying, because prior contact and a concrete plan are published selection requirements
Prepare FORM2 and a one-page recommendation letter in English or Japanese
Submit to the host researcher roughly two months before the JSPS deadline, when the Electronic Application System opens
important_advice_for_students: Do not try to apply on your own. There is no candidate-facing portal: the host researcher enters the application and the head of the host institution transmits it to JSPS. Begin the host relationship first.

Treat the host institution's internal deadline as the real deadline. JSPS itself warns that an institution may set its own deadline more than one month before the JSPS deadline, so waiting for the published April or August date can already be too late.
Ask the host researcher how many applications they still have available, because each host researcher may submit only three applications per recruitment.
Do not budget on the Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research. It is applied for by the host researcher through the institution and is not a personal entitlement, so it should be treated as contingent.
If you already live in Japan with a mailing address, do not plan on the airfare or the JPY200,000 settling-in allowance; neither is paid in that case.
Check the six-year PhD window yourself before approaching hosts, and remember that every four weeks of maternity or parental leave counts as one month of relief.
Prepare your referee early: the letter must fit on one page and be in English or Japanese, and it travels through the host rather than directly to JSPS.
There is no English test score requirement published for this programme, so do not spend money on one for the application, but expect to work in a Japanese research environment after arrival.

542.title: JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship for Research in Japan (Short-term Program for North American and European Researchers, PE)
542.description: This programme brings PhD students and PhD researchers from North America and Europe to Japan to conduct collaborative research under the guidance of a Japanese host for between one and twelve months. Financial support is a maintenance allowance of JPY362,000 per month for PhD holders or JPY200,000 per month for non-PhD holders at the start of the research in Japan, a round-trip air ticket, a settling-in allowance of JPY200,000 for fellows with three or more months of tenure, and overseas travel insurance. A research support allowance for cooperative research-related expenses is applied for by the host researcher. The award is a research fellowship, not a degree scholarship, so no tuition is funded.

selection_criteria: Selection of applicants (host researcher) and candidates (invited overseas researchers) is done by the JSPS International Program Committee, made up of Japan's frontline researchers
Two-stage selection: a document review in the first stage and a panel review in the second
Document review is conducted by three examiners per application, with experts in the document review section assigned according to the contents of the application
Graduated scoring system on a scale of 1 to 5: 5 superlative, 4 excellent, 3 good, 2 fair, 1 poor
Marks are made on a comprehensive basis, taking into account research achievements, the research plan, estimated research capacity, and future potential of the research
The averaged score in the document review is used as the primary screening criterion in the panel review
Panel review selects a specified number of applicants in each panel review section

The host researcher selects the screening category from the Review Section Table; Review Section Sets pair each review section with the reviewers who screen it, and reviewers are selected in a balanced manner for a diverse range of perspectives
Published selection policy: the implementation of the fellowship contributes to promoting exchange between Japan and countries of North America and Europe
Published selection policy: the fellowship helps to advance both the candidate's and the host's research work
Published selection policy: the host and candidate have established close communication and devised a concrete research plan
Published selection policy: the host institution has adequately prepared a system for receiving the candidate
Published selection policy: in the research plan, consideration is given to honing the research skills of pre-doctoral candidates
Published selection policy: as much as possible, preference is not given to host institution or field of specialization in making selections
Published selection policy: not only the score of the document review but also the examiners' reasons and comments are to be given adequate consideration
Published selection policy: two selection judgements are made, Selected and Not-selected

Integrity rules: any reviewer with a potential conflict of interest is removed from the Review Committee for the relevant review, and all Review Committee members are obliged to comply with a confidentiality and non-disclosure agreement

important_advice_for_students: Do not try to apply on your own. There is no candidate-facing portal: the host researcher enters the application and the head of the host institution transmits it to JSPS. Start the host relationship first, and note that this programme publishes three rounds a year, so a missed host deadline only costs you one round, not a whole year.

Check the country rule carefully before anything else. Citizenship alone is not the only route: three or more continuous years of research at an institution in an eligible country also qualifies, but Japanese resident-card holders with a Japanese mailing address at the JSPS deadline are excluded outright.
Plan the length of your stay deliberately. A tenure under three months forfeits the settling-in allowance, and a pre-doctoral candidate is paid JPY200,000 per month rather than JPY362,000.

The published selection policy says preference is not given to host institution or field of specialization, and it requires the research plan to show how a pre-doctoral candidate's research skills will be honed. Write the plan accordingly rather than assuming prestige of the host carries weight.
The published selection policy states that a person who has never done research at a Japanese university would be most preferable. If you have, do not hide it, but do not lead with it either.
The Research Support Allowance is applied for by the host researcher, not by you. Ask the host whether they intend to apply, since it is contingent and affects what research budget you can plan.
No English test score is published for this programme, so do not spend money on one for the application.

544.title: POSCO Global Scholarship in Korea (Global Future Leaders Scholarship Program)
544.description: The POSCO TJ Park Foundation awards a scholarship to international students admitted to a master's or doctoral programme at a designated Korean graduate school and recommended by that institution. Benefits published are full tuition, living expenses of KRW 1,000,000 per month, a one-time settlement fee of KRW 1,000,000, National Health Insurance premium, Korean language education support, and cultural programmes. Master's students receive full tuition for 4 semesters and living expenses for 22 months; doctoral and integrated master's and doctoral students receive full tuition for 6 semesters and living expenses for 36 months. Twenty students are selected per year, subject to change.
544.deadline_display: Selection cycle: graduate school admission around November, recommendation submission by the graduate school around December, foundation interview around January, final selection announcement around February. The page publishes month-level timing only, with no day-level deadline, and applications are submitted by the admitting institution rather than by the applicant.
544.verification_notes: Re-verified against the official source: Selection Procedure published exactly as stored, at month level only with no day-level date: '01 Graduate School Admission (~Nov) / 02 Recommendation submission by Graduate School (~Dec) / 03 Interview By Foundation (~Jan) / 04 Final Selection Announcement (~Feb) / 05 Certificate Award Ceremony (Mar)'. official_details.description: The POSCO Global Scholarship in Korea, also called the Global Future Leaders Scholarship Program, funds international students admitted to a master's or doctoral programme at a designated Korean graduate school and recommended by that institution. Published benefits are full tuition, living expenses, a settlement fee, insurance premium, and Korean language and cultural support.
purpose: An inbound scholarship supporting global talents to complete Master's and doctoral programs in Korea, published as 'For Next Generation Global Leaders'
The programme empowers promising global leaders by offering full tuition and living expenses as they pursue Master's or doctoral degrees at top Korean universities

Unlike traditional Korean scholarships aimed at supporting domestic students abroad, the programme uniquely welcomes outstanding individuals from around the world to study in Korea and build meaningful connections with Korean society
Through academic coursework and immersive experiences including industry visits and cultural programs, awardees gain in-depth knowledge of Korea's economy, society and values
As they complete their degrees, awardees are equipped to become globally-minded leaders who bridge their home countries with Korea and contribute to a more interconnected world

Umbrella rationale published by the Foundation: POSCO Global Scholarship is founded on the belief that deeper mutual understanding among individuals leads to stronger global connections, ultimately contributing to peace and shared prosperity around the world
The Foundation operates the programme to promote mutual understanding through global talent exchange and collaboration, and to help build a global network of next-generation leaders

important_advice_for_students: Start with university admission, not with the scholarship. Admission to a designated graduate school is stage 01 of the Foundation's own five-stage procedure, so an application strategy that starts with the Foundation cannot work.

The single most common failure point is forgetting the recommendation. The applicant cannot submit it; the graduate school does. Ask the department, in writing, when it will send the recommendation to the Foundation, and check back in November rather than assuming.

Treat the eligible-country and eligible-university lists as provisional. The Foundation marks both as tentative and separately marks the 20-student quota as subject to change, so confirm the current year's lists with asiafellowship@postf.org before you commit to a university.

Do not plan to arrive in January. Every Foundation stage date is published with a tilde, from around November to around February, and the only fixed date in the cycle is the March certificate award ceremony.

Budget from the caps, not the headline. Tuition is full only for 4 semesters (Master's) or 6 semesters (doctoral or integrated), and living expenses only for 22 or 36 months. If your programme runs longer, the extra time is your own cost.
Insurance is handled: the National Health Insurance premium is a published benefit. Airfare is not on the published benefit list, so fund your own travel.
Both eligible-country and eligible-university lists are published as tentative on the official site, so do not rely on a list you read from a secondary source.

545.title: Apoyo Complementario SECIHTI-OEA 2026
545.description: A complementary support awarded jointly by the OAS and Mexico's Secihti to students who already hold a Secihti National Scholarship for a full-time postgraduate programme in Mexico. The OAS contribution is a single payment of USD 1,200 for settling-in expenses in Mexico, paid in Mexican pesos at the official exchange rate on the day OAS deposits it, and the number of supports depends on OAS funds. Secihti adds its monthly support under the Secihti 2026 National Scholarship Scale plus ISSSTE medical service. The call does not establish tuition, travel or full living-cost coverage, so this is not full funding.

545.region: Mexico (beneficiaries must be nationals of OAS Member States other than Mexico)

545.official_source: Secretaría de Ciencia, Humanidades, Tecnología e Innovación (Secihti) and Organización de los Estados Americanos (OAS)
eligibility: Declarar en su perfil único tener la nacionalidad de alguno de los Estados Miembros de la OEA, con excepción de México.

Haber obtenido una Beca Secihti Nacional in one of the six named calls: Becas Nacionales para Estudios de Posgrado programas elegibles 2025 segundo periodo; Becas Nacionales para Estudios de Posgrado en Humanidades y Ciencias de la Conducta 2025 segundo periodo; Becas Nacionales para Estudios de Posgrado en Entidades Federativas con Mayor Rezago Social 2025 segundo periodo; Becas Nacionales para Estudios de Posgrado para Especialidades en Áreas de la Salud 2025 segundo periodo; Becas Nacionales para Estudios de Posgrado en programas que pertenezcan a las áreas de Físico-Matemáticas y Ciencias de la Tierra, Biología y Química, Ingenierías y Desarrollo Tecnológico 2025 segundo periodo; or Becas Nacionales para Estudios de Posgrado 2026, término de referencia A, programas elegibles escolarizados, primer periodo.
Ser persona becaria nacional vigente en un programa de posgrado escolarizado.

Estar admitido e inscrito en las áreas de Física, Matemáticas y Ciencias de la Tierra, Biología y Química, Ingenierías, Medicina y Ciencias de la Salud (a excepción de la formación de especialidades y subespecialidades médicas), Biotecnología y Ciencias Agropecuarias.
545.eligibility_summary: Applicants must already be current Secihti National Scholarship holders admitted and enrolled in a full-time postgraduate programme in a listed subject area, and be nationals of an OAS Member State other than Mexico.
benefits: The OAS portion is explicitly stated to be independent from the scholarship granted by Secihti.
coverage: OAS: single contribution of USD 1,200 for gastos de instalación (settling-in expenses) in Mexico, paid in Mexican pesos at the official exchange rate of the day OAS deposits to the beneficiary's bank account.
Secihti: monthly economic support according to the 'Tabulador de Becas Nacionales 2026'.
Secihti: medical service provided by ISSSTE, on registering as a beneficiary under ISSSTE rules.
requirements: The beneficiary must send the information and documentation that the OAS requests for formalisation and disbursement, on time and in full.

Under article 17-A of the Ley Federal de Procedimiento Administrativo, a failure to send that information triggers a single emailed prevención with a term of no fewer than five business days; if it is not corrected, the support may be cancelled and reassigned.
application_method: There is no public application form for new applicants: participation requires already being a current national scholarship holder selected under one of the calls listed in the eligibility section.
Secihti validates the applications of persons who were beneficiaries under the listed calls and sends the compliant list to the OAS on 28 August 2026.
The OAS Award Committee deliberates on 3 September 2026 and Secihti and the OAS notify selected students directly between 4 and 10 September 2026.
Results of the assigned applications are published on the OAS website and notified by email from both Secihti and the OAS.
Formalisation is carried out by signing the corresponding instrument between the OAS and the selected beneficiary.
Disbursement is made once the support has been formalised, following the timetable and procedure the OAS communicates by email.
545.selection_notes: The OAS selects among the Secihti national scholarship holders using ten published criteria: being admitted and enrolled in a listed subject area; being a current national scholarship holder in a full-time postgraduate programme selected by Secihti; geographic balance by country of origin; the applicant's country Human Development Index; gender; area of study; geographic distribution of the host institution in Mexico; level of study (doctorate over master's); dual nationality and residence in Mexico; and proportion of candidates per country. The number of supports depends on the availability of OAS funds.
545.best_fit: Non-Mexican nationals of OAS Member States who are already current holders of a Secihti National Scholarship for a full-time postgraduate programme in one of the listed STEM, health, biotechnology or agricultural sciences areas in Mexico.

important_advice_for_students: Do not spend any time on this 'application'. There is nothing to file. The only route is to be a current Secihti national scholarship holder whose name Secihti put on the list it sent to the OAS on 28 August 2026. If you are not already inside the Secihti system, this programme cannot help you.

Understand what you are actually getting: a one-off USD 1,200 for settling-in expenses in Mexico, paid in pesos at whatever the exchange rate is on the deposit date. It is not a tuition payment and not a living stipend. Budget your programme on the Secihti scholarship itself, not on this top-up.

The published selection and notification stages are already over. The deliberación was 3 September 2026 and direct notification ran 4 to 10 September 2026, both before this record's verification date. The 30 November 2026 date is the close of the process, not a deadline you can still apply against. If you are reading this for the first time, check your email and your Secihti file rather than your calendar.

Treat the emailed prevención as final. Article 17-A gives you exactly one notice, with a correction term the OAS sets and which may not be shorter than five business days. Miss it and the support is cancelled and reassigned to someone who was not favoured for lack of budget.

Your name will be published. Beneficiary names go into the padrón on Secihti's website under the transparency law. If you send anything you consider confidential, you must declare it in writing and say which documents or sections and why; and if you send classifiable information anyway, the consequences are entirely on you.
Know that the audit trail is long: the support can be reviewed or audited during the award and for five years after it ends, without needing your authorisation.

Do not expect the OAS to help with immigration. The call states in terms that Secihti does not intervene in the migratory situation of the national scholarship holder or their economic dependents, so that is entirely yours to arrange.

Two factors are published that people forget: doctoral candidates are ranked above master's candidates, and the geographic distribution of your host institution in Mexico is itself a criterion. If you have any choice of campus, it is not neutral.

546.title: 2026-2027 OAS - Universidad del Desarrollo Scholarship Opportunity (dLab Global)
546.description: The GS/OAS and the Universidad del Desarrollo in Chile fund USD 3,400 of the USD 3,800 total course fee for a 4-month online certificate in Global Innovation and Entrepreneurship (dLab Global 2026), focused on SDG 13 climate action. The selected candidate remains responsible for USD 400 of the course fee, plus study materials or equipment, internet access, and any additional fees not included in the offer. Living costs, travel and insurance are not addressed at all in the announcement, so this is not full funding and there is no stipend to live on.

official_details.description: The General Secretariat of the Organization of American States and Universidad del Desarrollo in Chile award scholarships to pursue a certificate in Global Innovation and Entrepreneurship through the dLab Global 2026 programme. The total course fee is USD 3,800, of which the GS/OAS and the University contribute USD 3,400 per selected candidate, leaving USD 400 for the selected candidate. The overriding theme is sustainability and climate change, focused on UN SDG 13. Study materials, equipment and internet access are not covered.
purpose: The General Secretariat of the OAS (GS/OAS) and Universidad del Desarrollo decided to support outstanding individuals from the Americas by awarding scholarships to pursue a certificate in Global Innovation and Entrepreneurship

The overriding theme of the course is Sustainability/Climate Change and how innovation can be used to reduce the effects of what is happening, as well as helping to prevent and mitigate this phenomenon

The programme focuses on the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, namely SDG 13, which focuses on taking urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts, and the innovative projects developed centre on this subject

The GS/OAS supports Member States in creating policies and implementing programs that promote the development of human capabilities at all educational levels, strengthening democratic values and security within the framework of regional integration
Participants are connected with the innovation and entrepreneurship ecosystem at UDD and in Chile, with experts in innovation invited to speak about their projects
sdg_requirement_details: SDG 13: Climate Action - the overriding theme of the course is Sustainability/Climate Change, and the announcement states that the innovative projects developed will centre on this subject
Applicants are explicitly invited to read around SDG 13 and to think about areas of interest for a group project
Innovative resilience building business concepts closely linked to climate or environmental resilience are especially encouraged

important_advice_for_students: Get the single-file rule right first. Only one upload is permitted and every required document must be inside one PDF of no more than 5 MB. Splitting files across uploads, or exceeding 5 MB after scanning photos at full resolution, is the most common way to fail here.

Translate everything properly. Every document must be in English or carry an official English translation, and incomplete applications are not accepted at all, so a missing translation is a rejection, not a request for more information.

The English test route is flexible and cheaper than people assume. If you completed studies at an English-speaking university or college within the past five years, an official transcript is accepted instead of a test score, which saves you the exam fee if you qualify.

Budget for the USD 400 yourself and prove it. The scholarship covers USD 3,400 of USD 3,800, and you must additionally fund study materials, equipment and internet access, none of which the award touches.

Read the eligibility criteria as a filter, not a formality. Four of the eleven published conditions are behavioural: 'think outside the box' and critical thinking, a quest for discovery, demonstrable ability to lead and inspire, and 4.5 hours a week for a whole semester. If you cannot commit the time, do not apply.

Expect an interview, and expect it in English. Pre-selected candidates are contacted by email to take part in an interview with the selection committee in English if necessary, so treat English interview fluency as part of the assessment, not just the written evidence.

The course is anchored on UN SDG 13. If you read the announcement and cannot say how your project touches climate change or climate resilience, you are not the profile they are selecting for, and the business concept statement is where that has to come through.
Do not wait for feedback if you are rejected. The announcement states that unsuccessful applicants will not be contacted.

547.title: Convocatoria de Becas OEA - UNIR, EP NEWMAN y UNIR Mexico (Curso Academico 2026, 2a convocatoria)
547.description: The SG/OAS awards tuition discounts for online postgraduate study with UNIR (Spain), the Escuela de Posgrado Peruana de NEWMAN (Peru) and UNIR Mexico. Up to 885 places are offered, with a 60% discount on total tuition for official master's programmes and official degrees, and a 50% discount for UNIR Formación Permanente programmes, applicable only to the value of the study programme. Admission fees, translation and notarisation, study materials, titulation and degree-awarding procedures, and any other cost not listed are explicitly excluded, and recipients must personally demonstrate the financial capacity to cover the uncovered programme costs, so this is not full funding.

benefits: Up to 885 places available across the three institutions for the 2026 academic course.
coverage: 60% discount on the total tuition (colegiatura) for UNIR official master's programmes and official degrees, and for EP NEWMAN and UNIR Mexico official master's programmes.

application_method: Step 1: Follow the admission process for the chosen programme directly with the institution, submitting all documentation the institution requires, and pay the admission fee.

Step 3: UNIR, EP NEWMAN, UNIR Mexico and the OAS form a specialised committee to select the scholarship holders.
Step 4: Await publication of results at www.oea.org/becas, announced from November 2026 for the 2a convocatoria.

official_details.description: The SG/OAS and three partner institutions (UNIR Spain, EP NEWMAN Peru and UNIR Mexico) sponsor tuition discounts for distance/online postgraduate study. Up to 885 places are offered: a 60% discount on total tuition for official master's programmes and official degrees, and a 50% discount for UNIR Formacion Permanente programmes, applicable only to the value of the study programme. Admission fees, translation and notarisation, study materials, titulation and degree-awarding procedures, and any other cost not listed are explicitly excluded, and the holder must cover the uncovered 40% (or 50%) personally and demonstrate that financial capacity in a set period before starting, so this is not full funding.
purpose: The Secretariat General of the Organization of American States (SG/OAS) and UNIR, EP NEWMAN and UNIR Mexico decided to support outstanding individuals from the Americas through the sponsorship of these academic scholarships, in order to continue their postgraduate studies.

UNIR, EP NEWMAN and UNIR Mexico state a mission of integral student training to form professionals with the competencies society currently demands, and specifically target those who, for various circumstances, cannot access in-person centres or who prefer more open and innovative online solutions offered by emerging technologies.

The SG/OAS, through its Department of Human Development, Education and Employment (DDHEE), supports its Member States in creating and running programmes that promote human development at all educational levels, working to strengthen democratic values and regional security and to improve the quality and equity of education.
study_type: Postgraduate study (maestrias/master's degrees and grados/official undergraduate degrees)
Distance (virtual) study only, delivered in Spanish
Formacion Permanente (permanent training) programmes, which are not degree-awarding
official_details.degree_award: Mixed. Official master's programmes and official degrees (Grados Oficiales) award a recognised title; Formacion Permanente programmes are professional training and are not presented as degree-awarding. The call states that neither the OAS nor the institutions take any responsibility for acceptance of titles or diplomas in the student's country of origin.
official_details.duration: UNIR Maestrias Oficiales 12 months; UNIR Grados Oficiales 4 years (programas de Grado), with the beca de Grado applying only to the first teaching year; UNIR Formacion Permanente 21 to 34 weeks depending on the programme; EP NEWMAN maestrias 12 months; UNIR Mexico maestrias 18 or 24 months
official_details.application_cycle: Curso Academico 2026 with two calls: 1a convocatoria Primavera 2026 (closed) and 2a convocatoria Otono 2026 (open at the time of reading). Each institution publishes its own deadline inside the same convocatoria, and results are published on different dates for each institution.
official_details.deadline_central_display: 2a convocatoria: 19 de octubre de 2026 (UNIR Maestrías Oficiales y Grados Oficiales, and EP NEWMAN); 26 de octubre de 2026 (UNIR Mexico); 30 de octubre de 2026 (UNIR Formacion Permanente)
official_details.deadline_institutional: Three different institutional deadlines fall inside the same convocatoria: 19 October 2026, 26 October 2026 and 30 October 2026, depending on the institution and programme. The 1a convocatoria equivalents were 16 March 2026 (UNIR Maestrías Oficiales y Grados Oficiales), 31 March 2026 (UNIR Formación Permanente) and 10 April 2026 (EP NEWMAN and UNIR México).
official_details.deadline_note: There is no single central deadline. Each institution's table publishes its own closing date for the 2a convocatoria: 19 October 2026 for UNIR official master's and official degrees and for EP NEWMAN, 26 October 2026 for UNIR Mexico, and 30 October 2026 for UNIR Formacion Permanente. Results are also published per institution: October 2026 for UNIR official master's and degrees, November 2026 for UNIR Formacion Permanente, EP NEWMAN and UNIR Mexico. Programme start for the 2a convocatoria is October/November 2026 depending on the programme. The SG/OAS reserves the right to cancel this announcement at any moment during the process.

550.title: HBKU Graduate Tuition Waiver and Stipend
550.description: HBKU graduate scholarships may include a tuition waiver applied to reduce tuition costs and a stipend paid directly to the student, and HBKU states that graduate students receiving a stipend would generally also be provided with a tuition waiver. Tuition waivers are standardised across HBKU and range from 100% for PhD STEM and PhD SHAPE and S.J.D. programmes down to 0% for LL.M. programmes, MS Economics and certificate programmes. Stipends are awarded to selected graduate students, with published monthly and annual rates for Qatari, international and local PhD and Master's students, over durations of 45 months for PhD and 21 months for Master's. Awards depend on the availability of funds, are not guaranteed, and are made on a merit or need basis only.

official_details.description: Hamad Bin Khalifa University states it is dedicated to assisting students in navigating financial support for their degrees. Graduate student scholarships may include a tuition waiver applied to reduce the tuition costs for the students and a stipend paid directly to the student, and generally graduate students receiving a stipend would also be provided with a tuition waiver. Tuition waivers are standardised across HBKU, with published waiver percentages that vary by programme type from 100% down to 0%. Stipends are awarded to selected graduate students, at published monthly rates split by student category (Qatari, international, local) and degree level (PhD and Master's), for 45 months at PhD level and 21 months at Master's level. Crucially, students are responsible for covering the cost of their housing, whether in Qatar Foundation dormitories or external accommodation, paid from the monthly stipend or personal funds, and HBKU does not provide direct payment for student housing.
purpose: HBKU states the university is dedicated to assisting students in navigating financial support for their degrees, and this page outlines the financial support provided to graduate students at HBKU.

The graduate funding scheme is built on an explicit partnership between funding and work: stipends are awarded to full-time graduate students who serve the university as research assistants and/or teaching assistants, so the award funds graduate study in exchange for supervised research and teaching labour.

It explicitly does not cover housing, which the student pays from the stipend or personal funds, and meal plans are not separately included. Tuition is not waived at all for LL.M., MS Economics and certificate programmes.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm the tuition waiver percentage published for your specific programme, since it ranges from 100% to 0%
Check whether you are in the Qatari, local or international stipend category, as the published rates differ sharply
Note that international applicants have a 1 February 2027 deadline while Qatari and resident applicants seeking funding have until 15 March 2027
Apply through the HBKU graduate portal from 1 October 2026; no separate scholarship application exists
Decide in advance whether you can commit to 10 hours per week of research assistant work with a supervisor, which is a condition of the stipend
Budget for housing yourself, since HBKU pays no direct housing cost
Read the scholarship agreement once offered, since it sets the academic standing you must maintain
important_advice_for_students: Being admitted does not mean being funded. HBKU states plainly that scholarships are not automatically awarded to admitted students, are offered on merit or financial need, and depend on the availability of funds. Treat the award as genuinely uncertain.

Sort out the deadline by your residency status, not by your programme. The 15 March 2027 funding deadline is published for Qatari and resident applicants only. As an international applicant you are bound by 1 February 2027, six weeks earlier.

Budget for housing in Qatar before you accept. The stipend is expected to absorb it, and HBKU makes no direct housing payment. This is the single largest gap between the headline stipend and a realistic budget.

Check your programme against the waiver table before you apply. If you are considering the LL.M., MS Economics or a certificate programme, your tuition waiver is 0% and the stipend is the only support you get.

Plan your workload before accepting. The stipend requires 10 hours a week of supervised research-assistant work, and 20 hours a week is the hard ceiling. If you plan to work as a professional or exceed 40% of full-time hours in outside work, you lose stipend eligibility.
You can earn on top of the stipend, within limits: teaching-assistant work at 50 QAR an hour for 10 hours a week, plus up to 10 more hours through the Student Employment Program.
Do not defer lightly. HBKU states deferral of admission may affect scholarship eligibility and directs you to your college, so ask before you defer rather than after.
The award is reviewed every year against your academic progress and the funds available, so it is renewable but never secure.
common_rejection_risks: Funds being exhausted, since tuition waivers and stipends depend on availability of funds
Not being awarded on merit or need, since awards are not automatic for admitted students
Working more than 40% of full-time hours as a professional, which disqualifies stipend eligibility
Failing to maintain the academic standing in the scholarship agreement at annual review
Applying to LL.M., MS Economics or certificate programmes, which carry a 0% tuition waiver
Missing the earlier 1 February 2027 deadline as an international applicant by assuming the later funding deadline applies
Expecting housing to be paid, which HBKU explicitly does not do
Submitting more than two applications in an academic year
Holding external funding, which excludes the holder from the published stipend rates and from these guidelines
Exceeding 20 hours per week of total work while holding a stipend
estimated_uncovered_costs: All housing costs, whether in Qatar Foundation dormitories or external accommodation, paid from the stipend or personal funds
The remaining percentage of tuition for programmes with a 60% or 75% waiver
Full tuition for LL.M., MS Economics and certificate programmes, which carry a 0% waiver
Living costs beyond the monthly stipend, including any costs for dependants, since awards do not vary with marital status or number of family dependents
Flights other than the single round-trip airfare provided to international students
Costs for anyone relying on self-sponsored discounted tuition of 2,000 QAR per credit hour
Meal plans beyond what the stipend can absorb, since meal plans are not separately included
document_audit: Graduate admission application submitted through the HBKU portal, with the college and program selected accurately because the tuition waiver rate depends on the programme
Supplementary documents and reference contact details submitted after submission via the confirmation email instructions
Scholarship agreement: review the academic standing requirement once it is issued, because annual review depends on it
Neither the scholarship page nor the graduate admissions page publishes a file type, size limit, translation or document date rule, so confirm format requirements with your college before uploading

alerts.message: The online graduate admission application opens to the public today. HBKU allows up to two applications per academic year, so choose your college and programme carefully.
International graduate applicants must have their admission application in by this date. The 15 March funding deadline does not apply to you.
Qatari and resident applicants who wish to apply for funding have this later deadline.
Confirm which stipend category and tuition waiver rate your programme and residency status attract; the published rates differ by category and by college.
Scholarships are reviewed each year against academic progress and available funds, so treat the award as renewable but not secure.

alerts.trigger: If you are considering deferring your admission
alerts.message: HBKU states deferral may affect scholarship eligibility and directs you to contact your college. Ask before deferring.

submission_workflow: Create an account on the HBKU Apply Now portal
Select the college and programme, applying to no more than two programmes per academic year
Submit the application and keep the confirmation email for the follow-up step
Log back in and submit supplementary documents plus reference contact details
Submit well before 1 February 2027 if you are an international applicant, or before 15 March 2027 if you are a Qatari or resident applicant seeking funding
Prepare to meet the 10-hour-per-week research assistant commitment if a stipend is offered
Arrange your own housing budget once you know whether a stipend was awarded

referee_tracking.instructions: After submitting the application you receive a confirmation email with instructions to log back in, submit supplementary documents, and provide contact details for your references. The number of references and their format are not stated on the pages read, so confirm with your college during the application process. Note that a reference is required for admission, not specifically for funding, since funding is decided inside the admissions process.

Not a referee but a mandatory work relationship: a student receiving a stipend must work as a research assistant with their primary supervisor for 10 hours per week. Identify a supervisor whose research you actually want to do, since you will be committed to them.

post_award_requirements: Work as a research assistant with the primary supervisor for 10 hours per week
Stay within the 20-hour-per-week total work limit
Maintain good academic standing as specified in the scholarship agreement, reviewed annually
Cover housing costs personally from the stipend or personal funds
Declare any external funding, which may affect eligibility and is excluded from the published stipend rates
Accept that a stipend funded from an external source such as a research grant falls outside the published rates and outside these guidelines
questions_to_ask_host: What is the actual tuition waiver percentage for my specific programme and college, and what is the per-credit fee I will be charged on the remainder?
Which stipend category will I fall into, and is the amount guaranteed for the full 45 or 21 months, or is it reviewed annually?
What is realistic housing cost in Doha against the monthly stipend, and do I need to apply separately for a Qatar Foundation dormitory place?
Is my potential supervisor taking funded graduate students, and what is the expected research-assistant workload in practice?
Does the scholarship carry any obligation to work after graduation, or to repay anything?
What happens to my funding if I defer admission, and how long is a deferral likely to take?
If I hold external funding, does it disqualify me from the published stipend rates entirely, or is it netted off?
What are the tuition waiver and stipend arrangements for a student who switches programme mid-degree?

programme_verification.source_conflict_rule: Where the scholarship guidelines page and the admissions page disagree on dates or eligibility, the admissions page is authoritative for deadlines and the scholarship guidelines page is authoritative for award amounts and conditions; neither overrides the other on its own subject.

data_quality.source_level: Official provider pages (HBKU scholarship guidelines and graduate admissions)

550.notes: Students are responsible for covering the cost of their housing, whether in Qatar Foundation dormitory facilities or external accommodation; this expense is paid from the monthly stipend or personal funds, and HBKU does not provide direct payment for student housing. Meal plans are not separately included; the stipend is a fixed amount meant to cover general living expenses including meals. Stipend awards do not depend on the student's marital status or the number of family dependents. Stipends for local students are limited. Stipends funded from external sources, including research grants, are excluded from the published rates. Self-sponsored graduate students are only eligible for a discounted tuition rate of 2,000 QAR per credit hour based on financial need, and these scholarship guidelines do not apply to students funded by external sources. Receipt of external funding may affect eligibility. Deferral of admission may affect scholarship eligibility. LL.M. programmes, MS Economics and certificate programmes carry a 0% tuition waiver.

551.title: MOFA Scholarship Program
551.description: The UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs runs a scholarship programme for Emirati students to study a Bachelor's degree at one of the world's top universities approved by MOFA, specialising in fields that meet the needs of the UAE diplomatic corps. MOFA states in its FAQ that the programme covers all tuition costs in accordance with the programme's policies, and the applicant must already hold an unconditional direct academic acceptance from an approved university indicating the programme start and end dates and the total cost. The programme is not a general study-abroad scholarship: it carries a service obligation, requiring the holder to join the MOFA diplomatic corps for a period equivalent to the number of academic years covered by the scholarship and to join the Anwar Gargash Diplomatic Academy upon graduation.
551.deadline_display: No application deadline is published on the program page; applications are registered through the online service and the review and final approval process typically takes between 3 to 5 months, with updates communicated by email or SMS
551.verification_notes: Re-verified against the official source: Scholarship Overview: 'The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA) provides a scholarship program for outstanding Emirati students who wish to pursue their academic journey abroad at one of the world's top prestigious international universities'. official_details.description: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA) provides a scholarship program for outstanding Emirati students who wish to pursue their academic journey abroad at one of the world's top prestigious international universities, with the aim of specializing in fields that meet the needs of the UAE diplomatic corps, and enriching it with qualified Emirati personnel and a generation trained to the highest standards. It is not a conventional academic scholarship: it funds a Bachelor's degree abroad at an MOFA-approved university, then a post-graduate diploma at the Anwar Gargash Diplomatic Academy, then appointment to the diplomatic corps. The FAQ states that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs covers all tuition costs in accordance with the program's policies, and no living-cost, accommodation, airfare or stipend provision is published anywhere on the programme page.

To be part of the UAE Government vision to prepare a generation of leaders in the field of diplomacy.

application_readiness_checklist: Check your nationality against the Annex 1 invited list for this cycle before anything else. If your country is not on it, nothing else matters.
Confirm you are no more than 40 years old at the time you apply.
Confirm you hold at least a Master's degree or equivalent in a field relevant to your proposed research, and be ready to show strong academic and research potential.
Secure an academic supervisor at a Japanese university or research institution who will accept you and oversee the research - this is an eligibility requirement, not a formality.

Establish the language of instruction or supervision at your proposed host, and get the language certificate ready, using the UNESCO Certificate of Language Knowledge in Annex 5 where that is the route.
Choose exactly one primary research area and one corresponding sub-area from the five published areas; the full indicative sub-areas are in Annex 2.
Read the Application Guide before drafting anything, because it holds the requirements for eligible candidatures and the submission procedures.
Contact your National Commission for UNESCO immediately and find out their internal deadline, because you must submit to them at least 2 weeks before 15 October 2026.

Prepare the full document set: application form (Annex 3), academic documents, recommendation letter, host institution acceptance letter, language certificate and research proposal (Annex 4 template).

Remember the sequence: your application goes to your National Commission, not to UNESCO, and only once they nominate you do you email the online form and documents to keizoobuchi.fellowships@unesco.org.
important_advice_for_students: You cannot apply to UNESCO directly. Every application must be nominated by your National Commission, so your real first deadline is theirs, roughly two weeks before 15 October 2026.

There is no tuition. The grant is a lump sum for a research stay, and it explicitly does not cover tuition fees, equipment including computers, publication costs, or conferences unless the participation is integral to the research and makes a direct and significant contribution.

The US$10,000 is a ceiling, not a fixed award, and medical insurance is deducted from it before disbursement. Plan for the net amount and for the fact that it must cover travel, accommodation, subsistence and research costs together.

The whole award is one lump sum for a stay of three to nine months. If you plan a nine-month stay, the per-month value is roughly a third of what a short stay would offer, so set the stay length before you build the budget.
The stipend covers subsistence in Japan only for the approved stay from February 2027 to December 2027. It does not fund your life outside Japan, and it does not fund your degree at home.
Mind the age limit and the degree requirement together: this is a young-researcher scheme, capped at 40 at the time of application and requiring at least a Master's already.

Pick your research area carefully. The 2026 cycle is heavily weighted toward artificial intelligence - four of the five areas are AI areas - alongside heritage conservation. If your work is heritage-focused, your sub-area must sit within the heritage area; if it is AI-focused, choose which of the four AI areas fits and be precise about the sub-area.

The final decision is made by the Japanese authorities on the Committee's recommendation, with due consideration to gender equality and diversity, so the substance of the proposal and who is applying both matter.

Submitting to UNESCO directly without a National Commission nomination, which UNESCO will not accept.
Proposing a research topic that does not fall within one of the five Cycle 2026 research areas, or failing to select a single primary area and sub-area.

556.description: This is the Japanese-nationals track of the Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program, which the World Bank states is fully funded by the Government of Japan. It funds up to two years for a limited number of Japanese mid-career professionals dedicated to the alleviation of poverty and enhanced shared prosperity in developing countries who have been admitted to or are currently enrolled in a master's or PhD programme outside Japan in a development-related field. Benefits include one economy class air travel to the host university and a $600 travel allowance at the start, one economy class return travel and a $600 travel allowance at the end, tuition, basic medical insurance obtainable through the university, and a monthly subsistence allowance to cover all living expenses while on campus. The amount of the monthly subsistence allowance varies by host country and is not published on the page.

official_details.description: The Japanese nationals window of the Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program awards scholarships of up to two years to a limited number of Japanese mid-career professionals who are committed to alleviating poverty and enhancing shared prosperity in developing countries and who are admitted to, or currently enrolled in, a master's or PhD programme outside Japan in a development-related field. The scholarship is fully funded by the Government of Japan and pays one economy class flight to the host university plus a US$600 travel allowance if the scholar is not already attending, one economy class flight back to Japan or a developing country where the scholar has secured employment plus a US$600 allowance on completion, tuition and basic medical insurance for the duration, and a monthly subsistence allowance while on campus. The 2027 window opens on 15 February and closes on 16 April 2027.
purpose: The JJ/WBGSP provides scholarships for up to two-years to a limited number of Japanese mid-career professionals who are dedicated to the alleviation of poverty and enhanced shared prosperity in developing countries, and who have been admitted to or are currently enrolled in a master's or PhD graduate degree program outside of Japan and in development-related fields.

After earning their degree, Japanese national scholars are expected to advance their professional career with a keen focus on the alleviation of poverty and enhanced shared prosperity in developing countries.

The JJ/WBGSP uses a review process for applications from Japanese nationals aimed at identifying the candidates with the highest potential, after completion of their graduate studies, to impact international development.

important_advice_for_students: This is a mid-career scheme for Japanese professionals, not a scholarship for fresh graduates. The three-year post-degree employment requirement and the three-year degree-timing rule are the two filters that catch people out.

Weight your application around commitment. Commitment to an International Development Career carries 40% of the score - double each of the other three factors at 20% - so your development orientation and how you evidence it matter more than your grades or your references.
Plan around the two-year cap. The award covers the duration of the programme or two years, whichever is less, so a three-year PhD is only two years funded unless the programme itself is shorter.

The return flight depends on completion. If you have not completed all requirements to earn the degree by the end of the scholarship period, the funded flight back to Japan or a developing country is not available, so plan your completion date.

The subsistence allowance is paid only while you are on campus, and its amount varies by host country. Check the host country's cost level before you commit, and budget for time away from campus that the allowance does not cover.

You must disclose other funding. The award supplements rather than duplicates other support, and you are required to inform and document any other scholarship funds once you are notified as a semi-finalist or awardee.

Note the Government of Japan employment bar, which includes JICA, local governments and the Central Bank, and applies from the moment the application process opens. Leaving a Japanese government post to take this scholarship is not permitted under the published rule.

Do not expect the scholarship to cover your extra costs. Visa fees, family, computers, field trips, workshops, seminars, internships, additional travel, non-provided language training and the resident permit fee are all yours.

submission_workflow: 1. Verify eligibility: Japanese nationality; bachelor's or equivalent earned at least three years before the Application Deadline; at least 3 years of paid development-related employment acquired since the degree and within the past six years from the deadline; unconditional admission (except for financing) or current full-time enrolment in a development-related graduate programme outside Japan, or current full-time development-related employment pertaining directly to developing countries.

2. Confirm you hold no Government of Japan or related agency employment - JICA, local governments, the Central Bank - and no World Bank Group role or close-relative relationship, on or after the relevant opening dates.
3. Read the 2027 Application Guidelines for Japanese Nationals and the 2027 FAQ.
4. From 15 February 2027, email the JJ/WBGSP Secretariat at scholarshipapplicants@worldbank.org to express your interest.
5. Complete and submit the scholarship application before 16 April 2027.
6. If notified as a semi-finalist or awardee, inform and document any other sources of scholarship funds to the Secretariat.
7. Await the two-assessor review, the Secretariat's selection and the JJ/WBG Steering Committee approval; winners are informed by mid-July.
post_award_requirements: Study the development-related graduate programme outside Japan for the duration of the programme or two years, whichever is less.
Advance your professional career after the degree with a keen focus on the alleviation of poverty and enhanced shared prosperity in developing countries, as the programme expects.
Complete all requirements to earn the graduate degree by the end of the scholarship period if you want the funded return flight.
Receive the monthly subsistence allowance only while on campus, and budget for time away from campus separately.
Do not accept funding that would duplicate rather than supplement this scholarship, and disclose and document any other scholarship funds to the Secretariat as required.

Cover personally all costs the scholarship excludes, including visa application costs, family expenses, extra-curricular courses and training, additional travel, research and supplementary educational expenses, field trips, workshops, seminars, internships, computers, non-provided language training, courses below the minimum credit requirement, and the resident permit fee.
questions_to_ask_host: Does my programme's award sit inside the two-year cap, and does it count as the full duration of the programme for funding purposes?
Is the scholarship period measured from my enrolment date, and does an academic leave or a research trip outside the host country reduce it?
What is the host country's monthly subsistence allowance, and is the allowance affected by time spent off campus?
What is the deadline for completing all degree requirements, given that the funded return flight depends on it?
What is the process for basic medical insurance through the university, and when is it deducted from the award?
What are the institution's expectations for a mid-career visiting researcher, and are there additional costs the institution expects scholars to cover?
What is the resident permit fee at this host, given that the scholarship does not cover it?

556.notes: The scholarship does NOT cover visa application costs, expenses to bring and/or support family members, extra-curricular courses or training, courses below the minimum credits required for the degree, language training not provided by the graduate program, additional travel during the study program, research or supplementary educational materials, field trips, workshops, seminars or internships, educational equipment such as computers, and the resident permit fee. The scholarship may only supplement, and does not duplicate, any other source of financial support; if you are notified of being a semi-finalist or are awarded, you must inform and document other scholarship funds to the Secretariat. After earning their degree, Japanese national scholars are expected to advance their professional career with a keen focus on the alleviation of poverty and enhanced shared prosperity in developing countries. The air travel benefit at the end of the scholarship period is conditional on having completed all requirements to earn the graduate degree, and the return ticket is to Japan or to a developing country where the scholar has secured employment. The published US$600 is a per-trip travel allowance, not the award total. The 2026 window for Japanese nationals closed on Friday 17 April 2026, so only the 2027 window is live.

557.title: Albert Einstein Distinguished Educator Fellowship (AEF) Program
557.degree: Not a degree programme - professional fellowship for K-12 STEM educators
557.description: The AEF Programme places accomplished K-12 STEM educators for eleven months in federal agencies or U.S. Congressional offices, working on national education programmes and policy. Each fellow receives a monthly living stipend of $8,200, a travel allowance of up to $5,000 for approved travel requested by the host agency, an education allowance of up to $1,000 for approved professional development expenses, relocation reimbursement of up to $3,500 for fellows relocating from outside the Washington, DC area, and a health insurance stipend of up to $550 per month on an individual plan or $1,300 per month on a family plan. The DOE sponsors up to five congressional office placements. The programme is a single eleven-month appointment; it is not a degree award and involves no tuition.
557.deadline_display: Application deadline 8:00pm Eastern, November 5, 2026. Online application opened August 3, 2026. The application period typically opens in mid-August, with applications due in mid-November.
557.verification_notes: Re-verified against the official source: Programme page banner: 'The Albert Einstein Distinguished Educator Fellowship Program is now open for applications. Applications are due November 5, 2026 at 8:00pm ET.'
