Amounts may not be increased between the two steps: increases are not authorised, and projects that do not respect the aid limits or that do not conform to any budgetary adjustments requested by the ANR are declared ineligible. The 20 000 € European-preparation supplement is conditional on adequate planning and activities within the M-ERA.NET project (a dedicated Work Package and budget under the responsibility of an ANR-funded partner), on the activities actually leading to a research proposal involving consortium members in continuity with the M-ERA.NET work, and on the follow-up proposal targeting clearly identified FP10 calls (not co-funded by the ANR) coordinated by the ANR-funded French partner; it is a subject of a final assessment and a supplementary deliverable to the ANR. Beneficiaries commit to immediate open access to peer-reviewed publications under CC-BY, deposit of the accepted manuscript or publisher version in HAL, a FAIR approach to research data, a PGD within 6 months of the scientific start, deposit of data in a reference thematic repository or recherche.data.gouv, and free-licence release and Software Heritage archiving of software. Any change affecting the whole project (extensions, consortium modifications) must be approved by all partners, their funding agencies and M-ERA.NET. Proposals may be transmitted to other administrations, control bodies and partner funders, and certain national funders are obliged to publish submitted pre-proposals/proposals, which may disclose intellectual-property or business-secret content; applicants are warned to be careful with what they include. The ANR applies the PPST protection of the scientific and technical potential of the nation to projects with foreign public or private partners, and a negative SHFDS/MESR opinion prevents selection without reasons being given.

570.title: Estonian Scholarship Programme for international students, researchers and academic staff — Scholarship for degree and exchange study in Estonia
570.description: A monthly stipend for foreign students who already hold an admission confirmation from an Estonian higher education institution for the 2026/2027 academic year. The rate is EUR 350 per month for first-cycle (BA) and master's studies and EUR 660 per month for doctoral studies. The Board pays the scholarship to the host university, which then disburses it. The scheme is funded under bilateral intergovernmental or inter-ministerial agreements and is run through the Estonian Scholarship Programme.

Page 'Last updated: 01.10.2026', so the round is currently open (verification date

571.title: Nordic Scholarship Programme (Nordic Africa Institute)
571.description: A one-month funded research stay at the Nordic Africa Institute in Uppsala for Africa-focused researchers and students already based at a university or research centre in Sweden, Finland, Denmark or Iceland. The scholarship covers return travel at the least expensive fare, free centrally located accommodation in Uppsala, a desk and computer in a shared office at the Institute, and a subsistence allowance of SEK 450 per day. It is a short-term research stay award, not a degree programme.

573.title: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for 2027 - Research Students (Embassy Recommendation)
573.description: The MEXT Scholarship research-student route funds postgraduate research study at a Japanese graduate school: it exempts tuition, pays a monthly scholarship of ¥143,000-¥145,000, and provides round-trip travel expenses (airfare). Recipients are selected by the Japanese embassy or consulate general in their country after sitting that mission's Japanese and English qualifying examinations, and are then placed at a graduate school. This record covers the Embassy Recommendation route for the 2027 cohort; the separate University Recommendation route is administered by individual Japanese universities.
573.deadline_display: No central deadline is published. MEXT states that all procedures for the Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarships are conducted through Japanese embassies, consulates in your countries, or institutions of higher education in Japan; candidates should contact the Japanese embassy (or consulate general) in their own country for the application date, and the Study in Japan page states that the type and field of application may vary from country to country and that applicants should check with the Japanese embassy or other Japanese diplomatic mission for any openings.

official_details.description: The Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship supports foreign students who study in higher education institutions, selected on the recommendation of Japanese Embassy/Consulate General, University, or Authority. This record covers the 2027 Research Student track under Embassy Recommendation. The Study in Japan types table gives research students: level of studies 'Graduate school level'; duration '[Embassy Recommendation] Irregular course: within 2 years; Regular course: standard school year (when necessary, 6 months preliminary education will be added)'; preliminary training of Japanese etc. '6 months (Only those who need this training)'; field of study 'Major in field of specialty at a graduate school etc.'; scholarship '¥143,000~¥145,000 per month'; tuition 'Exempted'; travel allowance 'Round-trip travel expenses (airfare) provided'.
purpose: The national scholarship system exists to accept excellent students from overseas, thereby promoting international exchange and friendship, contributing to the development of human resources in foreign countries, advancing the internationalisation of universities and other institutions in Japan, improving educational and research capacity, and contributing to the internationalisation and vitalisation of society as a whole and to the development of Japan and the world.
For Embassy Recommendation, scholarship recipients are recruited and initially screened by a Japanese embassy (or consulate general, depending on the country).

574.title: JSPS Invitational Fellowships for Research in Japan - Short-term (FY2027, 2nd Recruitment)
574.description: The JSPS Invitational Fellowships for Research in Japan invite mid-career and senior overseas researchers to Japan for lectures, discussions and exchange activities hosted by a Japanese researcher. The short-term option runs 14 to 60 days and covers a round-trip economy air ticket, a maintenance allowance of JPY 18,000 per day, overseas travel insurance and a host-applied research support allowance of up to JPY 150,000. The candidate does not apply directly: a host researcher in Japan submits the application through the head of their institution.

eligibility: Candidate eligibility (both conditions must be satisfied at the time of application, at the time of selection, and during the fellowship period): (1) Be a citizen or permanent resident of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan. (Taiwan and Palestine are treated in this manner.) Persons of Japanese nationality are eligible to apply if they have resided at the time of application in a foreign country for 10 years or longer and are judged at a host research institution to have played an active role in that country's scientific community. (2) Be a full-time researcher or person with full-time researcher status at a university or research institution in a foreign country and have a position equivalent to a professor, associate professor or assistant professor in Japan (including positions such as professor emeritus). Researchers of other status may apply if it has been six years or longer since they obtained their doctoral degree and the host research institution judges them to have continuously conducted research at a foreign university or research institution.

Host researcher (applicant) eligibility: be affiliated with a research institution specified in Article 2 of the Procedure for the Handling of Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research (KAKENHI) issued by MEXT, be eligible to apply for a KAKENHI grant, and wish to host an overseas researcher.

Host researcher eligibility: be a full-time researcher. However, researchers who are not employed full time may be eligible if the host institution judges them able to execute their responsibility to carrying out the program uninterruptedly throughout the Fellow's tenure including providing them a suitable research environment (e.g. laboratory, space, facilities and personnel) in the same way that a full-time researcher would be able to do.
Selection policy requires that the applicant (host researcher) and candidate have established contact in advance and created a concrete activity plan.
574.eligibility_summary: The candidate must be a citizen or permanent resident of a country with diplomatic relations with Japan (Taiwan and Palestine treated likewise) and must hold a position equivalent to a Japanese professor, associate professor or assistant professor at a foreign university or research institution.

JSPS supports the Science Dialogue Program, enabling fellows to give lectures in English on their research work at high schools in the vicinity of their Japanese host institutes.
Access to the JSPS Fellows Plaza network and alumni follow-up activities after the fellowship.

application_method: Agree a concrete activity plan with the prospective host researcher in Japan; JSPS requires that the two 'have established contact in advance and created a concrete activity plan'.
The host researcher selects the appropriate category from the FY2027 Review Section Table, checking the FY2027 Review Section Set for the paired reviewers.
The host researcher obtains approval from the head of their institution and collects the candidate's S-3 Curriculum Vitae, then completes S-2 jointly with the candidate.
The host researcher submits the application through the JSPS Electronic Application System by the host institution's internal deadline, which may be more than one month before the JSPS deadline.
The host institution transmits the application to the president of JSPS by the JSPS deadline (5 p.m. JST on 23 April 2027 for the FY2027 2nd recruitment).
JSPS conducts a document review by three examiners, then a panel review; results are published in early August 2027 for the 2nd recruitment.
The fellow arrives in Japan within the published arrival period (1 October 2027 - 31 March 2028 for the 2nd recruitment).
574.selection_notes: Selection of the applicant (host researcher) and the candidate (invited overseas researcher) is done by the JSPS International Program Committee, made up of Japan's frontline researchers. Selection is carried out through a document review in the first stage and a panel review in the second. Reviewers with a potential conflict of interest are removed, and all Review Committee Members must comply with confidentiality and non-disclosure agreements. Document reviews are conducted by three examiners per application, using a graduated 1-5 scale (5 superlative, 4 excellent, 3 good, 2 fair, 1 poor), taking into account research achievements, the research plan, estimated research capacity and future potential; the averaged document-review score is the primary screening criterion for panel review. Two selection judgements are made: Selected and Not-selected.
574.best_fit: Established overseas researchers holding a position equivalent to a Japanese professor, associate professor or assistant professor (or researchers more than six years past a doctorate who have continuously conducted research), who already have an agreed collaboration plan with a Japanese host researcher and can spend 14 to 60 days in Japan.

official_details.description: The programs provide excellent researchers from other countries an opportunity to conduct collaborative research, discussions, and opinion exchanges with researchers in Japan. These programs are intended to help advance the overseas researchers' research activities while advancing science and promoting internationalization in Japan. JSPS Invitational Fellowships for Research in Japan consists of two options of Long-term, and Short-term. Grantees are selected by going through the selection process following the submission of applications by a host researcher in Japan who wishes to invite a researcher from overseas via the head of their university or institution. The recruitment and selection for the Long-term program is announced and conducted once a year, and twice a year for the Short-term.

576.title: KAIST Scholarship (KAIST International Graduate Admission)
576.description: KAIST's own scholarship for international graduate students, selected as part of the admission application rather than as a separate scholarship application. It covers full tuition fees plus national health insurance and a monthly stipend, and 94% of KAIST's international student body receive it. Two higher tiers are awarded automatically to those selected: the KAIST Global Presidential Scholarship (KRW 1,000,000 per month for 4 regular semesters) and the KAIST Prestige Scholarship for International Ph.D. Students (KRW 300,000 per month for 8 regular semesters). The published cost-of-study table shows the student still carries on-campus housing, food, books, travel and telecommunications costs.

576.english_requirement: KAIST's official language of communication and instruction for international students is English. All applicants must provide at least one English proficiency test score, and the scores must be valid as of the online application deadline. Published minimums: TOEFL iBT 83 (taken before 21 Jan 2026) or 4.5 (taken on or after 21 Jan 2026); IELTS Academic 6.5 band; TOEIC 720 (Listening & Reading, TOEIC Public Testing Program); TEPS 326. TOEFL institutional code 0195, department code 99; Home Edition accepted; iBT MyBest Scores are NOT accepted; IELTS Online is accepted but IELTS One Skill Retake is NOT accepted; test scores from Institutional Testing Program (ITP) are NOT accepted. Exemption: no EPT score is required if you hold citizenship of, or have physically studied and completed a bachelor's-equivalent or higher qualification at an institution physically located in, Antigua and Barbuda, Australia, the Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Canada, Dominica, Grenada, Guyana, Ireland, Jamaica, Malta, New Zealand, St Kitts, St Lucia, St Vincent, Trinidad and Tobago, the U.K. or the U.S.A. A further exemption applies if you hold citizenship of one of a listed group of countries AND have physically studied and completed a qualification equivalent to a bachelor's degree or higher in English as the medium of instruction at an institution physically located in one of those countries, in which case a certificate from the school attended indicating English as the medium of instruction (e.g. English Lecture Certificate) must additionally be provided. Applicants expecting to graduate from regular KAIST degree programmes in the semester before the intended course also do not need to provide a score. Programs that do not require an EPT score: GDI-ITTP track, KINS-KAIST.

576.selection_notes: Scholarship status is decided inside the admission process: applicants who select the KAIST scholarship as their financial resource in the application are automatically considered for the KAIST Scholarship and, where the degree programme matches, for the KGPS or the KPS. For the KGPS, no separate application is made and only highly competitive applicants will be recommended by the department head. For the KPS, applicants demonstrating outstanding academic and research achievements receive recommendations from the department head, with final selection by the college dean. KAIST states that 94 percent of its international students benefit from the scholarship and that the scholarship rate may vary by student.

International applicants who select the KAIST scholarship as their financial resource during the admission application process will be automatically considered for the following scholarship programs, based on their chosen degree program or major.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you do not hold Korean citizenship; if you are of Korean descent with foreign citizenship, start the renunciation paperwork or confirm that all of Grades 1-12 were completed outside Korea with certified certificates and transcripts
Confirm your bachelor's (master's/Master's-Ph.D.) or master's (Ph.D.) qualification will be complete by the start of the course
Book your English proficiency test early - TOEFL iBT, IELTS Academic, TOEIC or TEPS - and make sure the score is still valid on the online application deadline date

Check whether you qualify for a published EPT exemption before paying for a test; if you use the citizenship-plus-English-medium-instruction exemption, obtain an English Lecture Certificate from your school
Pick your entry term against the published windows: Spring (mid August - early September), Fall Early (early December - late December), Fall Regular (early March - late March)
Avoid iBT MyBest Scores, IELTS One Skill Retake and Institutional Testing Program results, all of which are rejected
Confirm your intended department accepts KAIST Scholarship applicants; the Global Technology Innovation Program (GDI-GTIP Track) does not
Agree the recommendation letter timetable with your referee well before the submission window closes, because the letter cannot be changed after the deadline
Review the College of Engineering's own stipend terms if you are applying to Engineering, since the base stipend varies by college
important_advice_for_students: There is no separate scholarship form to file - the scholarship is chosen inside the admission application, so prioritise the admission deadline

Do not expect a single stipend figure: the base stipend depends on research involvement and varies by college, and only the KGPS (KRW 1,000,000/month for 4 regular semesters) and KPS (KRW 300,000/month for 8 regular semesters) tiers have published amounts
Do not assume housing or food are covered; the published cost table shows you must budget for both
If you are a Master's-Ph.D. integrated entrant, the KPS stipend does not start until you begin the Ph.D. programme
Do not rely on a MyBest TOEFL score or an IELTS One Skill Retake result; both are explicitly rejected
Do not file before your English test result is out and valid, or you will not meet the published condition
Use ApplyWeb rather than any emailed route; KAIST publishes an online system for both the application and the recommendation letter
common_rejection_risks: Holding Korean citizenship, or being of Korean descent with foreign citizenship without the renunciation documentation or the fully-foreign Grades 1-12 record
Studying part of primary or secondary school in Korea, which breaks the completed-outside-Korea condition without exception; international schools inside Korea do not count
Missing the degree qualification deadline for the course start
An English test score that expires before or on the online application deadline
Submitting iBT MyBest Scores, IELTS One Skill Retake, or an Institutional Testing Program score
Claiming an EPT exemption without the additional English-medium-of-instruction certificate when the published conditions require it
Applying to the Global Technology Innovation Program (GDI-GTIP Track) expecting KAIST Scholarship support
A late or missing recommendation letter - it cannot be modified after the deadline
Assuming KGPS or KPS is applied for separately; it is automatic, and KGPS still needs department-head recommendation of highly competitive applicants only

577.title: ICSSR Participation in International Seminar Abroad (Travel Grant Scheme)
577.degree: Doctoral, Postdoctoral, Research (faculty and doctoral/postdoctoral scholars)
577.description: This scheme gives partial financial assistance to Indian social science scholars who have been formally invited to present a paper at an international conference abroad. Assistance covers air travel, visa fee, travel insurance, local conveyance, maintenance for the stay, and registration fee up to US$200. Regular faculty receive up to 50 percent of the total cost of the visit, while SC/ST faculty, persons with benchmark disability, and postgraduate/doctoral/postdoctoral researchers without salary protection may be considered for the full cost of the visit.
577.deadline_display: Applications can be submitted online throughout the year. The applications should be uploaded at least three months before the due date of the Conference.
577.verification_notes: Re-verified against the official source: Section 3 HOW TO APPLY: '3.1 Applications can be submitted online throughout the year. 3.2 The applications should be uploaded at least three months before the due date of the Conference followed by the hard copy of the application.' Section 5.1: faculties get 'financial assistance up to 50 percent of the total cost of visit'; 5.2 full assistance for SC/ST, Benchmark Disability and 'Post-Graduate
577.region: India (Indian social science scholars; conferences held outside India)
577.duration: Period of stay abroad not exceeding the actual days of the conference plus travel dates
577.application_period: Rolling - applications are submitted online throughout the year, and must be uploaded at least three months before the due date of the Conference.
577.official_source: Indian Council of Social Science Research (ICSSR), Ministry of Education, Government of India
577.image_alt_text: Indian Council of Social Science Research emblem
eligibility: Faculties with regular service in public funded Universities/Deemed-to-be-Universities/Colleges, Institutes of National Importance as defined by MoE / UGC, and ICSSR Research Institutes/Recognized Institutes having a PhD degree are eligible to apply.
Post-Graduate (Regular)/PhD/PDF scholars in Social Science disciplines who are in the advanced stage of their studies/research are eligible to apply.

Independent scholars having served as Civil servants, officers from Defence services, and other professionals with a social science perspective having not less than 20 years of regular service and demonstrable research experience through publications of books/research papers/reports/policy documents, etc. may also apply.
577.eligibility_summary: Indian social science scholars in regular service at a UGC-recognized university/deemed university/college, an Institute of National Importance, or an ICSSR research or recognised institute, holding a PhD, or post-graduate/PhD/post-doctoral scholars at an advanced stage of study, or certain independent senior professionals.
benefits: Preference is given to younger scholars, scholars attending a conference or seminar for the first time, and scholars from remote and backward areas.

Invitations from global subject associations, reputed international organisations, universities or institutions are given preference, and due consideration is given to the peer review process used by the conference organisers.
coverage: Air travel (economy class, purchased through the three government approved travel agencies)
Visa fee
Travel insurance
Local conveyance
Maintenance costs for the period of stay abroad (not exceeding the actual days of the conference plus travel dates)
Registration fee up to US$200

Up to 50 percent of the total cost of the visit for regular faculty; the full cost of the visit may be considered for SC/ST faculty, persons with benchmark disability and PG/doctoral/postdoctoral researchers without salary protection, and for faculties from ICSSR Research Institutes/Recognised Institutes
requirements: The application will be considered only when the paper for oral presentation has been accepted by the organiser of the Conference through a formal invite. A formal invitation letter should be submitted along with the application. A simple email will not be considered as a formal invite.
The submission of the full length paper to be presented is mandatory and it should be either in English or Hindi.

Applications should be uploaded at least three months before the due date of the Conference; the application will not be entertained or considered in any case after participation and presentation of the paper in the Conference.
If the paper is co-authored, priority will be given to the first author, but a No Objection Certificate(s) from the second author(s) may be procured and attached with the application.
Air tickets (economy class) must be purchased only from M/s Ashoka Travels and Tours (ATT), M/s Balmer Lawrie & Company Ltd (BLCL), or Indian Railways Catering & Tourism Corporation Ltd (IRCTC).
Application for the second time will be considered only after a gap of three years, and a scholar can avail of the award only twice in his/her lifetime.
It is mandatory to buy tickets through the three government approved travel agencies; it is the scholar's own responsibility to arrange travel, visa and accommodation.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your paper has been formally accepted for ORAL presentation, and obtain a formal invitation letter - an emailed acceptance that the ICSSR does not accept as a formal invite is the single most common disqualifier.

Check you are in one of the eligible categories: regular faculty in a public funded university/deemed university/college, an Institute of National Importance, or an ICSSR research/recognised institute with a PhD; or a PG/PhD/postdoctoral scholar at an advanced stage of research; or an independent scholar with 20+ years of regular service as a civil servant, defence officer or similar professional with social science research output.

Make sure you are not applying for a poster presentation, to chair a session, as a convener or rapporteur, or to attend a workshop, training, refresher, summer or winter course - all of these are expressly ineligible.
Work backwards from the Conference due date: the online application must be uploaded at least three months before it.
Write or finalise your full-length paper in English or Hindi - submission of the full paper is mandatory.
If the paper is co-authored, you are most likely first author; obtain No Objection Certificates from the other author(s) and attach them.
Get your Head of Department or supervisor to forward/sign the hard copy application - applications not duly forwarded are rejected.
Register an account on https://app.icssr.org/ well before the three-month cut-off; postal delays are not the responsibility of the ICSSR.

If you are claiming full assistance (SC/ST, benchmark disability, or PG/doctoral/postdoctoral without salary protection), be ready to demonstrate you have received no financial assistance from other sources.
Plan your budget on the assumption that regular faculty receive up to 50 percent of total visit cost, with registration fee capped at US$200.
important_advice_for_students: Do not wait for a published ICSSR deadline - this scheme is open all year, but your real deadline is the Conference date minus three months.
Do not spend effort chasing a generic 'call for applications'; ICSSR advertises these travel grants on an open, rolling basis.
Do not apply if your participation is a poster, a chair role, or a course/workshop attendance; that is published as ineligible.
Do not buy air tickets yourself before you know the award position, and when you do, use only Ashoka Travels and Tours, Balmer Lawrie & Company, or IRCTC - economy class.
Do not skip the hard copy. The online submission is not sufficient; the printed application with all documents must reach ICSSR, and ICSSR is not responsible for postal delay or loss.
Remember the lifetime cap: you can take this award at most twice, and a second application is only considered after a three-year gap.
If you are a first-time conference presenter, younger scholar, or from a remote or backward area, say so in your application - these are published preference criteria.
common_rejection_risks: Applying without a formal invitation letter, or with only an informal email acceptance from the organiser.
Applying for a poster presentation, session chair, convener/rapporteur role, or a workshop/training/refresher/summer/winter course.
Submitting the application less than three months before the Conference due date.
Submitting after the paper has already been presented at the Conference.
Not attaching the mandatory full-length paper, or attaching it in a language other than English or Hindi.
Incomplete application, or one not duly forwarded by the Head of Department/Supervisor or institution.
Conference organised by an Indian organisation conducting seminars/conferences abroad - not eligible under this scheme.
Claiming full financial assistance without confirming no other financial assistance has been received.
A second application inside the three-year gap, or a third application in a lifetime.
estimated_uncovered_costs: For regular faculty, 50 percent or more of the total visit cost remains with the applicant.
Any part of the registration fee above US$200.
Costs of upgrades above economy class air travel.
Any travel or hospitality costs outside the components listed by ICSSR (for example, personal expenses, meals not covered by the conference, incidentals).
Pre- and post-conference personal travel, accommodation and visa costs beyond the sanctioned visit period.

578.title: University of Sharjah Research Assistant (RA) and Teaching Assistant (TA) Scholarship for Master's Students
578.description: The University of Sharjah offers work-based Research Assistant and Teaching Assistant scholarships to eligible master's students, who must commit 20 hours per week at the University and may not be employed elsewhere during the scholarship period. The award is awarded by the concerned academic department based on its academic and research needs and available opportunities. The official page read does not publish the benefit amount, whether tuition is waived, or any list of expenses the scholarship covers, so this record is deliberately left unquantified rather than assumed to be full funding.
578.deadline_display: Applications for Master's programs will be open from 5 October 2026 to 12 November 2026.
578.verification_notes: Re-verified against the official source: "Applications for Master's programs will be open from 5 October 2026 to 12 November 2026." Eligibility: "Hold a Bachelor's degree with a minimum CGPA of 3.20 out of 4.00 (or equivalent) for UAE national students, and 3.60 out of 4.00 (or equivalent) for non-national students" and "Be committed to working 20 hours per week at the University as part of the scholarship requirements." 578.application_period: Master's applications are open 5 October 2026 to 12 November 2026 for the published 2026/2027 intake. The University publishes no separate RA/TA scholarship application window; it states that meeting the minimum eligibility requirements does not guarantee a scholarship and that selection is subject to departmental evaluation, availability and approval.
eligibility: Hold a Bachelor's degree with a minimum CGPA of 3.20 out of 4.00 (or equivalent) for UAE national students, and 3.60 out of 4.00 (or equivalent) for non-national students.
Be committed to working 20 hours per week at the University as part of the scholarship requirements.
Not be employed outside the University during the scholarship period.
Meet any additional requirements established by the concerned academic department and the University.

Regular master's admission also requires a bachelor's degree or equivalent from a university recognized by the UAE Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research (MoHESR), a minimum CGPA of 3.00 out of 4.00, and a bachelor's degree in a field relevant to the intended master's program.

579.title: Programa Portugal-Berkeley (Visiting Student Researchers at UC Berkeley)
579.description: The Programa Portugal-Berkeley is an FCT call, run with FLAD and UC Berkeley, that supports doctoral students to spend a research stay as Visiting Student Researchers at UC Berkeley for up to six months. FCT launches the call to promote the internationalisation of Portuguese science and to foster research exchange between Portuguese universities and UC Berkeley in areas of mutual scientific interest. The selected candidate's home institution (CPS) is responsible for the administrative procedures to acquire the Visiting Student Researcher status and pays the University Services Fee, the DS-2019 visa processing fee and the Institute of European Studies administrative fees at UC Berkeley. The selected candidate must arrange and financially cover their own travel, accommodation and health insurance, and the call publishes no direct stipend or award figure.

579.selection_notes: Assessment is carried out by an academic committee appointed by FCT and FLAD. Criterion A: candidate's curriculum, considering academic grades, track record and scientific achievements including peer-reviewed publications, scholarships, prizes, conferences and project participation (40%). Criterion B: scientific quality, innovative character of the work plan and feasibility of the research activities to be developed (30%). Criterion C: motivation letter explaining the relevance of the stay and the work to be developed for the scientific ambition of the doctoral work plan, and the expected impact of the stay on the candidate's career (30%). Selection is based on the analysis of these criteria, producing a positive or negative opinion, with final classification CF = 0.4 A + 0.3 B + 0.3 C.

601.title: SA-TIED Request for Research Proposals: Public revenue mobilization; Poverty, inequality, and labour markets
601.description: UNU-WIDER and the South African National Treasury invite proposals under the third phase of the Southern Africa - Towards Inclusive Economic Development (SA-TIED) programme for research using South African tax administrative data. Accepted proposals are paid a research honorarium in the range of US$3,000-10,000 on delivery of a working paper of 10,000 words or fewer, and the resulting papers are published in the SA-TIED research paper series. This is research funding rather than a degree scholarship: the deliverable is a policy paper, and the honorarium is expected to cover all expenses of the research.

602.selection_notes: Eligible proposals are assessed on the scientific quality and potential of the project, the applicant's profile and potential, the quality of the Host Institution, supervision and training environment, and the expected impact of the project. AFdoc follows a bottom-up approach: proposals from all fields of research and technological development are eligible, and projects do not need to align with Luxembourg's National Research Priorities provided they fall within the expertise of the supervisors, the Host Institution and, where applicable, the company partner. The 2026 call is a pilot for a self-assessment on potential research security aspects.

Because funding goes to the Host Institution and the candidate is employed, the award is a salary rather than a stipend; the beneficiary has an employment relationship with the host, not with the FNR.

603.title: Flanders Trainee Programme (Flanders Traineeship Programme)
603.description: The Flanders Trainee Programme gives young people who hold a secondary or higher education diploma obtained in Flanders financial support for an internship with a multilateral organisation. The grant is made up of a one-off travel allowance and a monthly lump-sum amount for accommodation and living expenses, both set in advance; the monthly amount depends on the host city. Nationality and official place of residence are irrelevant, and the programme targets people interested in global challenges such as climate change, food security or human rights. The 2026 budget is exhausted; a budget is available again for 2027, with applications reopenable from January 2027.
603.deadline_display: No more grants for 2026: 'You can no longer apply for a grant for internships continuing into 2026. There is no more budget available for 2026. A budget will be available again in 2027. You can reapply for internships taking place in 2027 as from January 2027.' Within a funded budget year: 'You can submit your grant application up to six months in advance until one day before the start of your internship.'

603.region: Belgium (Government of Flanders). The internship itself is taken at the headquarters or a field office of a qualifying multilateral organisation within the jurisdiction of the Diplomatic Representations of Flanders. Published monthly grant amounts cover Antwerp, Brussels, Luxembourg, Geneva, London, Montreal, Nairobi, New York, Paris, Pretoria, Rome, Strasbourg, The Hague, Vienna, Warsaw, Washington D.C., Bonn, Madrid, Stockholm, Copenhagen, Maputo, Lilongwe and Midrand. Applicants may be of any nationality and resident anywhere, but must hold a Flemish secondary or higher education diploma.
603.duration: The grant covers an internship of at least two and up to six months. The internship can be extended to a total duration of six months, or nine months where the internship concerns a project funded by the Government of Flanders.
603.application_period: The 2026 budget is exhausted and applications for 2026 are closed. The 2027 budget reopens for applications in January 2027 for internships taking place in 2027, and new internship vacancies will be published on the programme's internships page from late 2026 onwards. Inside a funded budget year the published rule is that you may apply at any time of the year until one day before your internship starts, up to six months in advance, but a grant is only granted while budget remains.

603.selection_notes: No competitive jury or published ranking is described for this programme. The published route is a budget-limited reimbursement scheme: in principle you can apply at any time of the year, but you only get a grant if budget is still available, and if a budget is no longer available for the current year that is announced clearly on the programme website; an application submitted after the budget is gone is not processed and is not kept until a new budget is available. The average administrative turnaround time is three weeks. The grant is reduced by any remuneration or financial allowance you receive for the same internship from another Belgian or foreign government or from the multilateral organisation itself.

official_details.description: The Flanders Trainee Programme offers young global citizens financial support for an internship with a multilateral organisation. The grant consists of a one-off amount for travel expenses and a monthly amount for living expenses; both are lump sums, meaning they are set in advance. You must hold a secondary or higher education diploma obtained in Flanders, be under 35 when the internship starts, and secure the internship yourself with an organisation on the published qualifying list.
purpose: Give young people financial support for an internship with a multilateral organisation
Recruit socially engaged young people interested in global challenges such as climate change, food security or human rights
Give Flemish-trained young people international exposure and, through Flanders' diplomatic representatives abroad, involve them in Flemish foreign policy
Build a network between young Flemish graduates and multilateral organisations
degree_levels: Secondary education diploma or higher education diploma obtained in Flanders
study_type: Internship with a multilateral organisation
official_details.degree_award: Not a degree award. The programme funds an internship and confers no credit, degree or diploma.
official_details.duration: At least two and up to six months. Extensible to a total duration of six months, or nine months where the internship concerns a project funded by the Government of Flanders.
official_details.application_cycle: Budget-year based rather than a fixed annual call. The 2026 budget is exhausted; a budget is available again in 2027 and you can reapply for internships taking place in 2027 as from January 2027. Inside a funded year applications may be made at any time until one day before the internship starts, up to six months in advance.
official_details.deadline_central_display: No more grants for 2026 — 'You can no longer apply for a grant for internships continuing into 2026. There is no more budget available for 2026. A budget will be available again in 2027. You can reapply for internships taking place in 2027 as from January 2027.' Inside a funded year: submit up to six months in advance, until one day before the start of the internship.
official_details.deadline_institutional: None published. The host organisation does not set a deadline; the internship supervisor only has to complete and submit the attestation regarding the internship offer to stages.dkbuza@vlaanderen.be.
official_details.deadline_note: No absolute closing date is published for the 2027 round. The only published timing is that applications for 2027 internships reopen in January 2027, so deadline_date is left null and deadline_precision is set to month to reflect the month-level January 2027 opening. The standing in-year rule is that applications close one day before the internship start date.

It is a budget-limited reimbursement scheme: 'In principle, you can apply for a grant at any time of the year, but you can only get a grant if there is still budget available. If a budget is no longer available for the current year, it will be clearly announced on this website. If you submit an application when there is no more budget available, it will not be processed. 603.notes: The grant is explicitly not a salary but a lump-sum reimbursement of expenses actually borne, made up of a one-off travel allowance and an expense allowance for accommodation and living expenses. Coverage is partial: it does not pay tuition or course fees, there is no travel payment for an internship in Belgium, and the amounts are capped at a fixed 200 or 500 EUR travel payment plus a city-based monthly living amount. The internship can be extended to a total of six months, or nine months for internships linked to a project funded by the Government of Flanders. If you end the internship early you must inform the programme and may have to repay part of the grant, the amount being determined by the number of days you actually worked. There is no clinical or professional restriction published beyond the requirement that the host be a qualifying multilateral organisation.

605.title: ANU Vice-Chancellor's International Achievement Award
605.description: The ANU Vice-Chancellor's International Achievement Award is an Australian National University award whose stated objective is to attract a diverse range of academically capable overseas students to enrol in undergraduate and postgraduate coursework programs at ANU, funded by the University. ANU publishes the value as 20% off first-year tuition fees, with the tuition scholarship applied towards tuition at the start of each semester for the one year of the award. It is restricted to residents of China (including Taiwan, Hong Kong SAR and Macau SAR), Japan, Mongolia, the Republic of Korea and the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, and excludes the Doctor of Medicine and Surgery (MChD) and the Master of Digital Transformation and Entrepreneurship (MDTE). Recipients are responsible for the costs of books, study materials, accommodation and all other costs of study.

eligibility: You are an international student.
You are a new commencing student, or a continuing student who has received an offer of admission to a higher AQF level of studies.

You hold residential status in one of the following Countries or Regions: China (including Taiwan, Hong Kong SAR and Macau SAR), Japan, Mongolia, Republic of Korea, or The Democratic People's Republic of Korea.

You meet the minimum academic entry requirements: undergraduate applicants a Selection Rank of 85 (or equivalent as determined by the University) or above, or postgraduate applicants a minimum GPA of 5.5 (or equivalent).
You are not the recipient of an external sponsorship that covers all or part of your tuition fees at the University.

You acknowledge that the award can be offered only once at each level of study, except where you progress from an undergraduate degree (AQF Level 7) to a one-year Honours program (AQF Level 8), or accept a packaged offer such as a Graduate Certificate leading to a Master's degree.
Your program is an eligible program, excluding the Doctor of Medicine and Surgery (MChD) and the Master of Digital Transformation and Entrepreneurship (MDTE).
Study level: Undergraduate/Bachelor, Honours, Postgraduate/Masters and Graduate certificate. Selection basis: academic merit.

Do count on the automatic assessment happening at the time your admission application is assessed, so a strong academic record in the qualification used for admission is what matters.

606.degree: Doctoral, Postdoctoral, Research (faculty and Ph.D/PDF scholars)
606.description: The ICSSR provides financial assistance to Indian social science scholars who need to travel abroad for data collection or to consult archival material in connection with their research. It is aimed at scholars who proposed fieldwork abroad in their original approved ICSSR fellowship or project proposal and have made substantial progress, or at independent scholars for whom data collection abroad is academically justified and the research is at an advance stage. 607.title: Japan Africa Dream Scholarship (JADS) Program
607.description: The Japan Africa Dream Scholarship (JADS) is a capacity building programme of the African Development Bank and the Government of Japan that offers high-achieving African students a two-year scholarship to pursue post-graduate study at master's level in energy, agriculture, health, environmental sustainability and engineering. AfDB states it covers tuition for the 24-month study programme, a monthly living stipend, air travel between the scholar's home country and the host university at the start and end of the scholarship period, and health insurance usually obtained through the university, plus an additional six months for advance preparatory study or internships after graduation. It is not complete funding in AfDB's own terms: the Bank publishes an explicit exclusion list covering visa application costs, family members, extra-curricular courses, additional travel during the study programme, supplementary educational materials, field trips, workshops, seminars, internships and educational equipment such as computers. AfDB publishes no stipend figure and no central call date, so the amount and the closing date must both be confirmed with the chosen partner university and the JADS Secretariat.
607.deadline_display: The African Development Bank publishes no central JADS call opening or closing date, so there is no central deadline to quote. official_details.description: "The Japan Africa Dream Scholarship (JADS) is a capacity building program by the African Development Bank and the Government of Japan. The overarching goal of the African Development Bank and the Government of Japan is to enhance human resources capacity in Africa, in keeping with the Bank's High 5 strategic priorities, namely Feed Africa, Light up and power Africa, Industrialize Africa, Integrate Africa, and Improve the quality of life of the people of Africa. These priorities are also in line with key Japanese development assistance initiatives. The program offers high-achieving African students a two-year scholarship opportunity to pursue post-graduate studies at master's level in energy, agriculture, health, environmental sustainability, and engineering."

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are a citizen of an African Development Bank regional member country before anything else - this is the first gate.
Confirm you are 35 years old or younger and in good health on the date you apply.

Confirm you hold a bachelor's degree or equivalent in energy, agriculture, health, environmental sustainability, engineering or a related field, with the academic record and professional experience to match.

Confirm you have at least 1 year of paid employment in your home country or another African country, earned within the 3 years after your bachelor's degree, and start collecting proof of employment for every job in that period.
Shortlist an approved JADS partner university and the exact approved master's course, using the AfDB List of Universities page, before contacting anyone.
Contact the partner university using the contacts published on the AfDB List of Universities page and request its application forms, procedure and current dates.
Take the TOEFL iBT or TOEC English proficiency test and keep the result, because AfDB names it as a preparation step.
Write the research plan and proposal, and identify two professional referees in advance.
Do not apply to the African Development Bank directly and do not pay any application fee to the Bank - AfDB states no separate application to the Bank is necessary.
important_advice_for_students: Do not treat a university admission offer as a scholarship offer. AfDB states plainly: "Admission by the JADS partner university does not mean that you have been accepted for scholarship support; accordingly you should not take any action with respect to your current employment or otherwise, until you have been informed by the African Development Bank that you have been awarded the scholarship."
Do not apply directly to the African Development Bank. There is no Bank-side JADS form or portal, and the Bank warns this is the only route.

Do not wait for a single central deadline. AfDB publishes no central call date; the dates belong to the partner universities, and they differ widely between October and the following spring, so drive the schedule from the university you have chosen.
Do not carry undeclared outside funding. The programme supplements and never duplicates other support, and the stipend can be withdrawn wholly or partly if other funding is found during the award.

Do not budget on the assumption that everything is paid. Visa application costs, family travel and support, extra-curricular courses, additional travel, supplementary educational materials, field trips, workshops, seminars, internships and educational equipment such as computers are all excluded.
Do not plan on the 24 months being flexible. The scholarship covers the duration of the graduate programme or two years, whichever is less, so overrun beyond the approved course length is not funded.
Do not assume the stipend figure - AfDB publishes none, so get the current monthly amount in writing from the partner university or the JADS Secretariat before you commit.
Do not ignore the age limit of 35 or the one-year-paid-employment-in-the-past-three-years rule; both are stated as strictly adhered to, and criteria are fixed for the duration of an open call.
common_rejection_risks: Not a citizen of an African Development Bank regional member country.
Older than 35 at the point of application.
No bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in an approved field, or an academic record that does not meet the "excellent academic records" standard.
No 1 year of paid employment in the home country or another African country within the past 3 years after the bachelor's degree, or no proof of that employment supplied.
Already enrolled in another graduate degree programme.
Applying to the African Development Bank instead of, or as well as, the partner university - such an application is not considered.
Applying for a course that is not on the approved programme list for the chosen partner university.
Being an AfDB Group staff member, Executive Director, alternate, or a close relative by blood or adoption of such a person.
Not in good health, where health is assessed at selection.
Missing or uncertified copies of the most advanced university degree certificate.
Failing the English proficiency step (TOEFL iBT or TOEC).
Providing only one professional reference where two are required.

The scholarship "may only supplement, and does not duplicate, any other source of financial support/fellowship you might have"; finalists and awardees must inform the JADS Secretariat of other funding, and "The JADS stipend may be withdrawn completely or partially if during the scholarship period the program has evidence of additional sources of support." Deferral and renewal are not addressed on the AfDB pages. Scholars "are expected to return to their home countries and contribute to national and continental socio-economic development, using the newly acquired knowledge and skills." No clinical or field-of-practice restriction is published, but the approved master's courses are limited to energy, agriculture, health, environmental sustainability, engineering and related areas. 610.title: UNHCR Tertiary Refugee Scholarship Programme (DAFI) - Albert Einstein German Academic Refugee Initiative
610.country: Multi-country (host countries of asylum; country-of-asylum operations run their own calls)
610.description: DAFI is UNHCR's dedicated tertiary scholarship programme for refugees and returnees, founded in 1992 and funded principally by the Government of Germany. The published scholarship package covers a range of costs including tuition and study materials, food, transportation and accommodation, and depending on the needs and capacity of the individual country operation or programme partner may also cover academic preparatory, language and ICT courses as well as psychosocial support. It funds ISCED 6 bachelor's or equivalent programmes and ISCED 5 short-cycle tertiary and TVET programmes of two years or more, and it explicitly does not cover master's studies. Applications are made through the DAFI Programme Management Platform, which was live and accepting registrations and submissions on 2026-10-01.
610.deadline_display: No single global deadline is published. Deadlines are set per country operation and published on the UNHCR country help pages (published 2026/2027 examples: Rwanda 7 August 2026; Kyrgyzstan 21 August 2026; Slovakia 31 August 2026). Applicants must check their own country operation's call.
610.region: Multi-country (applicant countries: refugees and returnees under UNHCR mandate; country-of-asylum operations issue their own calls)
610.duration: Duration follows the degree programme enrolled in: ISCED 6 bachelor's or equivalent, or ISCED 5 short-cycle tertiary / TVET of two years or more
610.application_period: Country-specific. The 2026/2027 cycle ran on country-published windows in July-August 2026 (Rwanda 15 July-7 August 2026; Kyrgyzstan 7 July-21 August 2026; Slovakia 1 July-31 August 2026). New country calls for the next cycle are announced on the relevant UNHCR country help page and applications are submitted through the DAFI Programme Management Platform.

610.notes: The scholarship does not cover master's degree programmes (published: 'DAFI does NOT cover Masters studies.' / 'Please note that the scholarship does not cover master's degree programs.'). Awards are not deferrable, renewable or multi-year by default: funding follows admission to an ISCED 5 or ISCED 6 programme in the cycle applied for. No return-home obligation is published, and because studies take place in the country of asylum or home country no relocation is required. No clinical or field-of-study restriction is published beyond the general rule that the programme targets undergraduate and short-cycle tertiary/TVET study. The 2024 cycle was the first since 2020 with a decrease in the number of scholars supported, reflecting reduced global funding. As this is a multi-country programme with no published global deadline, the applicable deadline is the one published by the applicant's own UNHCR country operation; the published 2026/2027 country windows had all closed by 31 August 2026 at the time of verification, and the platform itself remained live and accepting registrations on 2026-10-01.

614.title: Programa RESTART — 4ª Edição (FCT research funding after parental leave)
614.description: RESTART is an FCT funding instrument that competitively finances individual R&D projects in all scientific domains for researchers who have recently taken a parental leave, including adoption leave. The award is a project grant of up to EUR 50,000 per project for a maximum of 18 months, drawn from a total budget allocation of EUR 1.6 million, and it is held by the beneficiary R&D unit rather than paid as a personal living stipend. Candidates must hold a doctorate, be an integrated doctoral member of an R&D unit or hold a contract with a State laboratory, and have taken a parental leave of at least 120 days (or at least 72 days in a shared leave, whether exclusive or shared) between 3 June 2025 and 1 October 2026 inclusive.

official_details.description: The Fundação para a Ciência e a Tecnologia (FCT), alongside its commitment to promoting the advancement of scientific and technological knowledge, aims to promote gender equality in R&D activities and careers, inseparable from equality of opportunity for the whole national scientific community. With this objective FCT launches the 4th edition of the RESTART programme. RESTART is intended to promote gender equality and opportunity through the competitive funding of individual R&D projects in all scientific domains, when carried out by researchers who have recently taken a parental leave, including for adoption. Aligned with public policies in this area, RESTART also covers, with specific eligibility conditions, cases of shared parental leaves. By empowering a competitive return to research activity in new circumstances, RESTART will support researchers in pursuing and developing an original and innovative research idea, with the possibility of associating other human and/or material resources, according to the funding made available and the planned execution time. This funding instrument is aligned with the concerns and recommendations of various international bodies, namely the Council of the European Union and the OECD.

616.title: Nanyang President's Graduate Scholarship (NPGS)
616.description: The Nanyang President's Graduate Scholarship is NTU President's premier PhD scholarship, tenable for up to 4 years for a full-time PhD at NTU with no bond attached. It pays the annual tuition fee plus a monthly stipend published by citizenship status - S$5,300 for Singapore Citizens, S$4,800 for Singapore Permanent Residents and S$4,300 for International Students - with CPF contributions on top for citizens, and with overseas conference, book, IT and thesis allowances. International students must perform teaching or laboratory supervision duties to satisfy the Graduate Assistantship Programme requirement. There is no separate scholarship application: candidates are considered through the normal NTU research degree application by indicating interest in the 'NTU Scholarship'.
616.deadline_display: The NPGS application window is open annually from October/November to December. The application period for Academic Year 2027-2028 will be announced in due course. The application period for National Institute of Education (NIE) will also be announced in due course. (NTU Research Programmes Admission Guide: for the August intake the application portal opens on 1 October and the last day for submission of the online application with supporting documents is 31 January, with school-specific deadlines of 15 November for ADM, SoH, SSS and WKWSCI, and 31 December for LKCMedicine and RSIS.)

The application period for National Institute of Education (NIE) will also be announced in due course." Also "This award also covers the annual tuition fee." No application date is publishe
616.duration: The award is tenable for one year in the first instance and is renewable subject to good progress. The maximum period of the Scholarship is 4 years for PhD candidates, as determined by school as well as availability of research funding in each case.
616.application_period: Annually from October/November to December for NPGS, with outcomes sent by email together with the offer of admissions. This sits inside NTU's research degree application periods: August (Semester 1) intake - portal opens 1 October, university last day 31 January; January (Semester 2) intake - portal opens 1 June, university last day 31 July.

The University of Cambridge states: 'If English is not your first language, you may need to show that you meet the English language requirement for your course', and 'For most courses, you don't need to provide your language test results until you're made an offer.' 617.selection_notes: Two-stage selection. Stage 1: academic departments at Cambridge nominate a small number of eligible applicants who meet all four criteria to a very high level; only departmentally nominated applicants are invited to interview. Stage 2: a 25-30 minute interview with one of four subject-based panels (Arts, Biological Sciences, Physical Sciences, Social Sciences) consisting of academics and practitioners, and possibly Gates Cambridge alumni and a Trust representative. The interview has four sections: welcome and introduction; Gates Cambridge (knowledge of the scheme, motivation, why you could be a Scholar, thoughts on the opportunities and responsibilities); academic and career plans; final thoughts and questions. Scholars are selected after interview. Gates Cambridge states it cannot provide feedback to unsuccessful applicants.
617.best_fit: Postgraduate applicants from outside the UK who are academically outstanding, can show a commitment to improving the lives of others and demonstrate leadership potential, and who want a health, medicine, public health or life-science related postgraduate degree at Cambridge.
617.notes: Not covered: bench fees and the costs of scientific equipment or similar academic resources - the Trust expects such core course costs to be covered by the Cambridge academic department. No funding is provided for a partner under the Dependent Children Allowance. The Trust does not fund other fieldwork costs; these should be funded by the University Composition Fee. Where a student has already gained a fee award from public authorities (such as UKRI) they should accept it, and the Trust will not pay their fee or may share their fee and maintenance costs. If the applicant is receiving a salary from an employer or has another substantial scholarship, the Trust reserves the right to reduce or not pay the standard maintenance allowance, and must be told ASAP of any other funding awarded towards the degree. Deferred entry and part-time study: a pilot continues to allow applications to fund a part-time doctoral degree; part-time degrees other than the PhD are not considered. University rules bar a second degree of the same type from Cambridge.

621.title: Rufford Small Grants Programme
621.description: The Rufford Small Grants Programme funds fieldwork costs for small-scale, pilot nature conservation projects run by early-career conservationists in developing and emerging economy countries. Funding is staged across four levels - 1st Rufford Small Grant up to GBP 7,000, 2nd Rufford Small Grant up to GBP 8,000, Booster Grant up to GBP 12,000 and Completion Grant up to GBP 18,000 - and the Foundation aims to provide between 50% and 100% of project costs, requiring evidence of co-funding where it is not the only funder. Only fieldwork costs are considered, and award holders must provide project updates and a final report that are posted on their Rufford webpage. There are no deadlines, so the programme was open on the verification date.
621.deadline_display: There are no deadlines - applications can be submitted at any time of year. 623.title: Ernst Mach Grant – worldwide
623.description: The Ernst Mach Grant – worldwide finances short research stays in Austria for young researchers from all disciplines and all countries except Austria. The published grant benefit is a supplementary monthly grant of EUR 1,300, together with assistance in arranging accommodation and health insurance, but scholarship holders pay the costs of accommodation and insurance themselves and must show own funds. Tuition fees at Austrian public universities and universities of applied sciences do not have to be paid by grant holders, and may be waived upon request to the rectorate, but this does not apply to private universities and private colleges. Holders from listed non-European developing countries also receive a travel costs subsidy of up to EUR 1,200 upon submission of original travel invoices.

623.selection_notes: The selection follows a multistage process: 1. Examination of the formal requirements; 2. Examination of the application's general plausibility; 3. Assessment and evaluation of the application by experts; 4. Final decision by the BMFWF. Incomplete applications and applications not complying with the application criteria will not be accepted for the further selection process. All formally valid applications are then evaluated by experts from the respective field and the selection committee awards the best applicants. The selection is competitive, i.e. there is no legal claim to a grant even if all application requirements are fulfilled; the number of grants awarded during one call depends on the quota and/or the available budget.

official_details.description: The Ernst Mach Grant programme is named after the Austrian physicist and philosopher Ernst Mach (1838-1916) and is financed by the Austrian Federal Ministry of Women, Science and Research (BMFWF). The Ernst Mach Grant – worldwide is a supplementary grant for young researchers from all countries except Austria who wish to pursue a research project in Austria for 1 to 9 months. The published grant benefit is a monthly grant rate of EUR 1,300 plus assistance in arranging accommodation and health insurance, with own funds required.

623.notes: Grant period is 1 to 9 months and must be consumed by the end of 2028. Extensions are not possible for this grant. The earliest possible start is September 2027 (the Austrian academic year 2027/28). Stay dates must consist of full months only, starting on the first of a month and ending on the last; short-term grants of 1 month should be consumed in February or September. Applicants must have interrupted any stay in Austria for at least six months before taking up the grant. Gainful employment is not allowed, with a marginal employment exemption of EUR 551.10 per month in 2026. A final report is obligatory at the end of the stay. The grant contract (Letter of Award and Letter of Acceptance) defines start and end date, grant amount, payment modalities, compulsory attendance at the guest institution, performance report and final report, data protection and repayment obligations. The grant cannot be used to enrol in a Master or PhD programme in Austria. Without written proof of accommodation in Austria, a residence permit is not granted. Applicants from non-EU/EEA countries planning a stay of more than 6 months whose accommodation costs exceed EUR 386.43/month may need to prove additional funds to the Austrian residence authority.
